These war illustrations were compiled and published in eleven volumes titled *Nisshin Sentou Gahou (A Pictorial Record of the Sino-Japanese War)*, documenting the war from its beginning to the signing of the peace treaty, including depictions of naval victories and the advance into Manchuria.

In 1893, Kubota was sent to the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago by *Kokumin Shimbun*, where his artwork was exhibited and earned him a First Class Medal. That same year, his paintings were also compiled into a multi-volume book titled *Kakuryū sekai hakurankai bijutsu hin gafu*.  In 1897, his artwork was presented as a gift to Queen Victoria on the occasion of her Diamond Jubilee.

Kubota Beisen was a prolific artist and writer, with a substantial body of published work.  He authored the book *The New theory of Aesthetics* in 1905, and *Beisen gadan* in 1901, alongside several other publications. His work is held in numerous library collections worldwide, with one English-language publication appearing in 84 libraries.

title: Salome Maswime
text:
Salome Maswime is a South African medical doctor specializing in obstetrics and gynaecology, currently serving as the Head of Global Surgery at the University of Cape Town. Her work centers on improving women’s health, advocating for equitable surgical and maternal care, and ensuring healthcare access for underserved communities. She frequently provides advice and consultation to organizations like the World Health Organization. 

Born in Limpopo, Maswime’s path to specializing in maternal health was profoundly influenced by a formative experience during her medical internship in Greytown, KwaZulu-Natal. Witnessing the preventable deaths of two mothers in a maternity ward motivated her to dedicate her career to addressing maternal mortality. She completed her medical degree at the University of KwaZulu-Natal in 2005. 

Following her internship, she spent ten years at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg and the Chris Hani Baragwanath Academic Hospital in Soweto. This period led her to pursue further education, culminating in a PhD funded by the Carnegie Corporation of New York and the South African Medical Research Council. Her doctoral research, completed at the University of the Witwatersrand, focused on reducing maternal morbidity related to hemorrhage following caesarean sections across hospitals in Gauteng.

Throughout her career, Maswime has held several key positions, including as a lecturer and Director of the Obstetrics and Gynaecology Clinical Research Division at the University of the Witwatersrand, and as an obstetrician at Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital. She focuses on high-risk pregnancies and researches maternal near-miss cases and mortality. Her work has highlighted an increase in maternal deaths stemming from bleeding during caesarean sections in South Africa and evaluated hospital preparedness for surgical complications. 

Maswime’s research also reveals the significant global burden of maternal mortality, noting that Africa accounts for approximately two-thirds of all maternal deaths worldwide, totaling around 200,000 deaths annually. She has published articles on this issue, including work concerning the increasing rate of caesarean sections in Africa. 

Recognized for her contributions, Maswime received the Trailblazer and Young Achiever Award in 2017, presented by Jacob Zuma, and was listed among the Mail & Guardian’s Top 200 South Africans the same year. In 2018, she founded the South African Clinician Scientists Society to support emerging specialists and researchers. She was also awarded a Discovery Foundation Harvard University Fellowship, worth R2.1 million, to research the causes of stillbirths in HIV-positive individuals. This fellowship led to her being one of only two representatives from her field at meetings with the World Health Organization and UNICEF, where she also explored the link between maternal and child mental health. She was appointed Professor of Global Surgery at the University of Cape Town in 2019 and named a Young Scientist by the World Economic Forum in 2020. She is a member of both the Academy of Science of South Africa, the South African Perioperative Research Group, and the International Network of Obstetric Survey Systems. She is a mother to two children, Taurai and Farai.

title: Flavio Méndez Santiago
text:
Flavio Méndez Santiago, also known as “El Amarillo,” is a prominent figure in Mexican drug trafficking, specifically identified as a leader within the Los Zetas criminal organization. His notoriety stems primarily from being designated as a significant drug trafficker by the United States government. 

On March 24, 2010, the U.S. Department of the Treasury took action against Méndez Santiago under the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act. This legislation, often referred to as the “Kingpin Act,” is a tool used by the U.S. government to combat international drug trafficking. The imposition of this act against Méndez Santiago, alongside fifty-three other individuals and ten separate entities internationally, signifies the U.S. government’s assessment of his substantial involvement in the illegal drug trade.

The consequences of being sanctioned under the Kingpin Act are significant. It effectively barred all United States citizens and businesses from engaging in any form of commercial or financial transactions with Méndez Santiago. Furthermore, the act resulted in the freezing of any assets he held within the jurisdiction of the United States. This financial restriction aimed to disrupt his operations and limit his ability to profit from his criminal activities. 

Approximately eleven months after the imposition of these sanctions, Méndez Santiago was apprehended by authorities. His arrest took place on January 18, 2011, in the municipality of Villa de Etla, located within the state of Oaxaca, Mexico. 

The article also places Méndez Santiago within a broader context of Mexican organized crime, noting his inclusion in a list identifying the 37 most-wanted drug lords operating within Mexico. This placement underscores the perceived level of threat and influence he held within the landscape of Mexican drug cartels. The information provided focuses narrowly on his designation by the U.S. government and his subsequent arrest, with no details given regarding the scope of his operations, specific drugs trafficked, or his role within the Los Zetas hierarchy beyond being identified as a “drug lord.”

title: Matt Hunter (singer)
text:
Matt Hunter, born Matthew Alexander Hunter Correa on February 20, 1998, is an American singer, songwriter, and voice actor with Colombian and Italian heritage. He was born in New York City and grew up in Paramus, New Jersey. Hunter began his career in entertainment at a young age, working as a voice actor from ages nine to twelve. During this time, he started a YouTube channel where he posted videos of himself singing covers and playing the guitar, sometimes performing in Spanish. These videos gained significant attention, leading to a growing fanbase throughout Latin America, built through grassroots efforts. He was even referred to as the “Latino Justin Bieber” and received praise from Marc Anthony, who predicted he would be “the future” of music.

His initial foray into music involved releasing singles. He debuted with “Mi Amor” at age thirteen, followed by “Right Here, Right Now” and “Mi Senorita” in 2012, and an EP titled *Right Here, Right Now* in the same year. In 2014, coinciding with the FIFA World Cup, Hunter collaborated with Pitbull to release “Minha Mina Ta Loca” and “Mi Chica Esta Loca,” in both Portuguese and Spanish. By 2016, he had accumulated a substantial social media following, with over 200,000 subscribers on YouTube and more than 500,000 followers on Twitter. He frequently travels between New York, Los Angeles, Miami, and various locations in Latin America.

Beyond singing, Hunter is recognized for his voice work as Diego Márquez in the final two seasons of the animated television series *Go, Diego, Go!* and in *Dora the Explorer*. He secured the role after an audition at age ten and continued voicing the character until he was twelve. He also created and released a weekly comedy webisode series called *Fuego Fridays*. 

Hunter has performed live concerts across numerous countries, including the United States, Puerto Rico, Mexico, Spain, Chile, Brazil, Dominican Republic, Colombia, Argentina, Costa Rica, and Ecuador. A significant achievement was headlining and selling out the 12,000-seat Movistar Arena in Chile in May 2013. He received a nomination for Favorite Pop Artist at the 2013 Premios Juventud awards, presented by Univision. He has released a number of singles since 2011, including collaborations with artists like Augusto Schuster, Isabela Moner, Tommy Boysen, Lenny Tavarez, GASHI, Big Soto, Carla Fernandes, Corina Smith and Lalo Ebratt. He’s also released covers of popular songs, such as John Legend’s “All of Me” and a Spanish rendition of Justin Timberlake’s “Not a Bad Thing”.

title: Tappaya Sit-Or
text:
Tappaya Sit Or, also known as Mit Klinmee, born February 1, 1976, is a retired Muay Thai fighter who achieved championship status at Rajadamnern and the World Muay Thai Council (WMC). He reached the number one ranking at Lumpini Stadium, though he didn’t secure the championship title there. Following his fighting career, he transitioned into coaching and currently owns and operates Sor Klinmee Gym in Pattaya, Thailand.

Tappaya comes from a large family, being the youngest of eleven children. He began training and fighting at a very young age, starting at six years old alongside his brother, Yokthai Sit-Or, and nephew, Rambaa Somdet. Their early training consisted of rigorous sessions before and after school, followed by regular fights in local bars for financial gain. By the age of twelve, Tappaya was already competing in Bangkok. The three fighters were foundational to the original Sit Or camp in Pattaya, moving there from Petrungruang gym; the camp later relocated to Bangkok and became known for producing notable fighters like Nong-O Sit-Or and Petchmankong Petfergus.

The peak of Tappaya’s career came in 1997. He won the 61.5 kg Rajadamnern belt by defeating Ankandet BaoBaoin, a fight televised nationally on Channel 5. He held this title for three consecutive years. In the same year, on August 10th, he secured the WMC belt at 61.5 kg with a victory over Panmongkon Carryboy. He gained significant exposure during this period, becoming a prominent fighter on Channel 7. Throughout his career, which concluded in 2001, Tappaya amassed an impressive record of 200 wins, 36 losses, and 5 draws. 

Beyond Thailand, Tappaya broadened his martial arts experience towards the end of his fighting career by traveling to China, Japan, and the United Kingdom to both teach and compete. While in Japan, he participated in both kickboxing and mixed martial arts, notably defeating Hayato in a kickboxing match while representing Crosspoint Gym. 

After retiring, Tappaya realized a long-held ambition and opened Sor Klinmee Gym in 2009, located on Neung Phap Wan road in Pattaya. He serves as the gym's owner and head trainer. Currently, he guides several fighters who are actively competing in the major stadiums of Bangkok, including Robert Sor Klinmee, a southpaw fighting at 46 kg in Rajadamnern Stadium, and Sangpet Sor Klinmee, an orthodox fighter competing at 45.5 kg in both Rajadamnern and Lumpini. Other notable trainees include Sinsamut Klinmee, his brother Sudsakorn Sor Klinmee, and the son of Yokthai, Thepprasit champion Fasai Sor Klinmee, alongside several younger, developing boxers.

title: Karni Liddell
text:
Karni Liddell, born on March 1st, 1979, in Rockhampton, Queensland, is an Australian Paralympic swimmer who also works as a radio presenter for 4BC. Her life has been significantly shaped by a long and difficult journey to receive an accurate medical diagnosis. Initially diagnosed with Spinal Muscular Atrophy as an infant, at twelve months old, she recently discovered in 2019, through whole genome sequencing conducted in Europe, that she actually has Congenital Titinopathy, another neuromuscular wasting disease. This followed a twelve-year search for a definitive explanation for her condition, a process described as lengthy, traumatic, and financially burdensome for her family. 

From a young age, medical professionals predicted a limited future for Liddell, informing her parents she would likely never walk and would not survive into adulthood. Despite these initial prognoses, she achieved remarkable success as an athlete. By the age of fourteen, she had already broken a world record in swimming, demonstrating significant athletic talent and resilience. 

Liddell represented Australia at the Paralympic Games on two occasions: in 1996 and again in 2000. She was successful at both Games, winning medals and establishing herself as a prominent figure in Paralympic sport. Her accomplishments culminated in being named Captain of the Australian Swimming Team for the 2000 Sydney Paralympic Games, a testament to her leadership and standing within the team.

Beyond her athletic achievements, Liddell has also engaged in public awareness campaigns and artistic projects. She was one of eighteen Australian Paralympians who participated in a nude calendar project photographed by Emma Hack, aimed at challenging perceptions of disability. Liddell’s contribution to the calendar involved body paint designed to resemble a polka-dotted bikini, and she wore sunglasses as part of the image. Furthermore, in 2008, she was featured in artwork by Ludmila Clark, with her image displayed at the Customs House in her hometown of Rockhampton, alongside other Queenslanders. This demonstrates her willingness to participate in projects that celebrate diversity and challenge conventional representations.

title: Lokesh Kanagaraj
text:
Lokesh Kanagaraj, born on March 14, 1986, is a prominent Indian film director, screenwriter, and producer working in the Tamil film industry. He began his filmmaking journey with short films, notably “Acham Thavir” in 2012, which garnered awards, and “Kalam” included in the 2016 anthology *Aviyal*. He transitioned to feature films with *Maanagaram* in 2017.

Kanagaraj is best known for creating the “Lokesh Cinematic Universe” (LCU) following the success of *Kaithi* (2019), an action thriller starring Karthi. He then directed *Master* (2021), a standalone film starring Vijay and Vijay Sethupathi, which became the highest-grossing Indian film of that year. *Vikram* (2022), featuring Kamal Haasan, Vijay Sethupathi, and Fahadh Faasil, further cemented his reputation and expanded the LCU. His most commercially successful film to date is *Leo* (2023), which earned over ₹600 crore (US$71 million) worldwide and serves as another installment within the LCU. He is currently working on *Coolie*, starring Rajinikanth, scheduled for release after announcing his intention to retire after directing ten films.

Prior to his film career, Kanagaraj studied Fashion Technology and later pursued an MBA. He worked as a bank employee before following his passion for filmmaking, inspired by encouragement from Karthik Subbaraj after a corporate short film competition. 

His filmmaking style is rooted in the neo-noir action genre, drawing influence from directors like John Woo, as well as 1980s and 90s action films, and filmmakers such as Martin Scorsese and Quentin Tarantino. He is known for incorporating retro songs, violence, and hyperlink narratives into his work, often aiming for a brutal and realistic aesthetic in his action sequences by avoiding the use of wires and special effects. While acknowledging criticism for potentially glorifying violence, he notes a need to moderate such elements for wider appeal. 

Beyond directing, Kanagaraj has expanded into producing through his company, G Squad, with his first production being *Fight Club*. He is also involved in expanding the LCU with projects like the short film *Chapter Zero*, a prequel to *Kaithi 2*, and the film *Benz*, for which he wrote the story. He frequently collaborates with a core group of crew and actors, including editor Philomin Raj, stunt choreographers Anbariv, composer Anirudh Ravichander, and actors Arjun Das, Arun Alexander and Dheena. 

Lokesh Kanagaraj is married to Aishwarya and they have two daughters.

title: Rana Sanaullah
text:
Rana Sanaullah Khan, born January 1, 1955, is a Pakistani politician currently serving as Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs, a position he assumed in April 2024. Prior to this, he served as the 39th Interior Minister of Pakistan during the first Shehbaz Sharif government and is considered the second most influential figure within that administration. He represented Faisalabad in the National Assembly from 2018 to 2023 and currently holds the position of president of the Pakistan Muslim League-N (PML-N) in Punjab, a role he’s held since May 2019. 

Sanaullah’s political career spans several decades, beginning with his election to the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab in 1990 as a candidate for the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP). He later switched allegiance to the PML-N, and was repeatedly re-elected to the Punjab Assembly in 1997, 2002, 2008, and 2013. During his time in the provincial assembly, he held several key ministerial positions including Law and Parliamentary Affairs, Local Governments and Community Development, Revenue, and Public Prosecution. He also served as Deputy Leader of the Opposition twice, from 1990-1993 and 2002-2007. 

His political journey hasn’t been without controversy. In 2003, he was reportedly abducted and tortured by the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) for publicly criticizing the military regime. He also faced accusations, leveled by the assassinated Punjab Governor Salman Taseer, of having links to militant organizations like Sipah-e-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP), and was criticized for meeting with SSP leader Maulana Ahmed Ludhianvi, justifying it as a pragmatic political move given the group's support base.

Sanaullah’s time as a minister has been marked by incidents that drew public scrutiny. In 2014, as Law Minister, he was heavily criticized for the police response during a clash with followers of Tahir-ul-Qadri in Lahore, known as the Model Town incident, which resulted in multiple deaths.  This led to his temporary removal as Law Minister, though he was later reinstated. 

In 2019, he was arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) and accused of drug trafficking, a case he maintained was politically motivated. After multiple hearings and denial of bail by a trial court, he was eventually acquitted by a special court in Lahore in December 2022, claiming the case was fabricated.  He contested the 2024 general election but was unsuccessful, losing the seat for NA-100 to an independent candidate.

Throughout his career, Rana Sanaullah has been a prominent and often controversial figure in Pakistani politics, demonstrating a long-standing commitment to the PML-N and holding significant positions within both provincial and national governments.

title: Chris Duffield
text:
Christopher Paul Duffield, born on May 20, 1952, is a former senior figure in London local government, best known for his role as the Town Clerk of London and Chief Executive of the Corporation of the City of London. He held this position until 2012, when John Barradell succeeded him. 

Duffield’s background includes a solid educational foundation, beginning with his schooling at St Albans School in Hertfordshire, an all-boys private institution at the time of his attendance. He then went on to earn a Bachelor of Arts degree with honors from Newcastle University in 1973. His career in local government spans almost three decades, encompassing various roles across different authorities before ascending to his prominent position within the City of London.

Prior to joining the City of London Corporation in September 2003, Duffield served as the Chief Executive of Bexley Council. His earlier career also included positions with the Greater London Council (GLC), Redbridge Council, and Essex County Council, demonstrating a broad range of experience within the sector. 

As Town Clerk and Chief Executive, Duffield oversaw a remarkably diverse portfolio of responsibilities. These included the efficient management and execution of all City functions, serving as a key advisor on policy and resource allocation. A significant part of his role involved the detailed servicing of meetings for both the Court of Common Council and the Court of Aldermen, along with their associated committees. He was also responsible for investigating any complaints made against the city and acted as the Electoral Registration Officer. 

Beyond the core administrative duties, Duffield’s remit extended to overseeing crucial areas such as public relations, economic development, and human resources. He also held the position of chief executive of the Police Authority, responsible for the management of its staff and working with the chairman to ensure effective policing within the City of London.

Duffield is professionally affiliated with the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy (CIPFA), indicating his expertise in public finance and accounting. 

On a personal level, Christopher Duffield is married and has three sons: Mark, Jack, and Joe. He is also a grandfather to four grandchildren – Amelia, Alex, Katie, and Stanley. He has a brother, Ian Duffield, who has two children of his own, Paul and Melanie.

title: Ted Mack (politician)
text:
Edward Carrington Mack, born in 1933 and passing away in 2018, was a unique figure in Australian politics, distinguished as the only person to be elected and re-elected as an independent across local, state, and federal levels of government. Often called the “father of the independents,” he deliberately limited his time in office to two terms at both the New South Wales state level and in federal parliament to avoid accumulating a parliamentary pension, demonstrating a principled stance against what he saw as excesses in public office.

Mack’s early life saw him educated at Sydney Boys High School and serving in the RAAF before training as an architect at the University of New South Wales, graduating in 1958. He worked as an architect for many years, specializing in hospitals and public housing, and even held positions overseeing hospital design and construction for the NSW Public Works Department and the NSW Housing Commission. He also served on a committee focused on Aboriginal housing in remote areas.

His political career began in 1974 with election to the North Sydney Municipal Council, where he rose to become mayor in 1980, a position he held until 1983, and again in 1987. As mayor, he implemented open government policies, opening council meetings and files to the public, and established numerous committees to encourage public participation in decision-making. He also focused on diversifying council funding sources, successfully reducing reliance on rates. 

In 1981, Mack unexpectedly won the state seat of North Shore, defeating the Liberal opposition leader Bruce McDonald. He continued this pattern of defying expectations in 1990, capturing the federal seat of North Sydney from the long-serving Liberal MP John Spender. As a federal member, he opposed policies like unilateral tariff removal and privatization, and notably voted against Australian involvement in the Gulf War, citing concerns about oil interests and the origins of the conflict. He also championed citizen-initiated referendums and served on the transport and communications committee. 

True to his principles, Mack retired from federal parliament in 1996 to avoid a pension, a move that influenced the subsequent preselection process for his seat. He remained engaged in public life, serving as a delegate to the Australian Constitutional Convention and actively opposing the proposed republican model. He was recognized as a “National Living Treasure” in 1997. 

Even in his later years, Mack continued to support independent candidates, notably assisting Stephen Ruff in the 2015 North Sydney by-election, criticizing the Liberal party’s preselection process. He was diagnosed with brain cancer in 2016 and succumbed to a stroke in November 2018, leaving behind a legacy of independent thought and commitment to public service. A park in North Sydney was renamed in his honour in 2019.

title: Giorgi Papunashvili
text:
Giorgi Papunashvili, known as Papu, is a Georgian professional footballer born on September 2, 1995, currently playing as a winger for Zira in the Azerbaijan Premier League, having signed a one-year contract with an option for another in August 2024. He has also represented the Georgian national team at both senior and youth levels.

Papunashvili began his club career at Dinamo Tbilisi, progressing through the reserve side before making his debut in the Erovnuli Liga in November 2013. He quickly became a key player for Dinamo, notably scoring 16 goals in all competitions during the 2014-15 season, including a hat-trick against Tskhinvali in October 2014. That season culminated in Dinamo winning the Georgian Cup, with Papunashvili contributing two goals in the final against Samtredia.  He was also part of the team that won the Umaglesi Liga and Georgian Super Cup in 2013-14, and the Georgian Cup again in 2014-15.

In the summer of 2015, he moved to Germany on a season-long loan to Werder Bremen, where he played for the reserve team in the 3. Liga. However, his time in Germany was hampered by injury, limiting him to 20 appearances and two goals. 

He then transferred to Spanish side Real Zaragoza in June 2017, signing a four-year deal and making his debut against Granada CF in August 2017.  After a period with Zaragoza, he joined Racing de Santander on loan in January 2020 for the remainder of the season. 

Following his loan spell, Papunashvili moved to Apollon Limassol FC in Cyprus in December 2020. He returned to Georgia in January 2022, joining Torpedo Kutaisi, but moved again six months later to Serbian club Radnički Niš. His time in Serbia was brief, as he signed with Samtredia in March 2023, followed by a move to Telavi four months later. After a single league appearance for Telavi, he joined Kapaz in Azerbaijan before ultimately signing with Zira.

Internationally, Papunashvili debuted for the Georgian national team in a friendly match against the United Arab Emirates in June 2014. He also represented the Georgia national under-17 team at the 2012 UEFA European Under-17 Championship, scoring a crucial late goal against England during the qualifying stage.

title: Cobhams Asuquo
text:
Cobhams Asuquo, born January 6, 1981, is a Nigerian musician, producer, and songwriter. Beginning his career after working at Questionmark Entertainment, he established his own recording facility and later co-managed CAMP (Cobhams Asuquo Music Productions) alongside Bez Idakula and Stan Iyke. He later founded Vintage Gray Media Ltd., which produced the music countdown show “The Top 12 Countdown with Cobhams Asuquo,” consisting of 74 episodes.

Initially trained as a lawyer, Asuquo gained prominence producing for other artists. He notably produced Asa’s debut album, co-writing hit singles like "Fire on the Mountain" and "Jailer." Throughout the early 2000s and continuing afterward, he produced numerous successful tracks for a wide array of Nigerian artists, including Maintain, Omawumi, Djinne, Banky W, and Tiwa Savage, among many others. 

Beyond studio production, Asuquo has performed internationally with bands at events like the Harare International Festival of Arts and concerts in France, South Africa, and Nigeria. He has also contributed to film and television, composing and arranging scores for projects such as “A Voice for Ella” and “Bayelsan Sillhouttes.”

Asuquo’s involvement extends to global advocacy. He performed at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, and participated in events with Bono’s ONE Campaign, raising awareness for agriculture in Nigeria and contributing to the US-Africa summit. He produced the anthem "Strong Girl" for the ‘Poverty is Sexist’ campaign, later remixing it with Bono, and co-produced "Tell Everyone" for the UN Global Goals campaign, featuring artists from across Africa. He performed at the Global Citizen Festival in New York City to further promote the UN Global Goals. He has also held production roles with Coke Studio Africa and events like Rhythm Unplugged and Hennessy Artistry.

As a recording artist in his own right, Asuquo released his debut single “Ordinary People” in 2014, followed by several others including “Do the Right Thing” featuring Bez, “Star of Wonder,” “Boosit” featuring Falz, “The Other Room,” “Adore,” and most recently, “We Plenti” featuring Simi in 2019. Despite being visually impaired, Asuquo has built a highly successful career. He married Ojuolape Veronica Olukanni in 2010, and they have two sons together.

title: Nancy Onyango
text:
Nancy Onyango is a Kenyan accountant, businesswoman, and corporate executive currently serving as the Director of the Office of Internal Audit and Inspection at the International Monetary Fund, a position she assumed on February 1, 2018, following her appointment in December 2017. Her professional background includes extensive experience in risk management, governance, and financial consulting, primarily within prominent firms in both Africa and the United Kingdom. 

Onyango received her higher education at the University of Nairobi, beginning her studies in 1984. She earned a Bachelor of Commerce degree in Accounting and Finance in 1987 and followed that with a Master of Business Administration degree in 1989, also from the University of Nairobi. Later in her career, she pursued doctoral studies, completing a Doctor of Business Administration degree from the United States International University Africa in 2016. Her doctoral work included coursework at Columbia Business School in New York City.

Her career began with nearly four years at PricewaterhouseCoopers, starting in July 1995, working as a manager in Uxbridge, London. She was subsequently promoted to senior manager at the same firm, a role she held for another three and a half years until August 2002. Returning to Kenya, she joined PwC East Africa in July 2005 as a Partner, leading the consulting unit with a focus on technology, governance risk, and compliance. She held this position until June 2012. She then became the head of the newly formed Risk Assurance Services Unit at PwC East Africa, serving in that capacity until October 2014. 

Prior to her appointment at the IMF, Onyango spent twenty months as a partner at Ernst & Young, beginning in January 2015, where she led governance, risk, and compliance initiatives for the entire African continent until August 2016. Before taking on her role at the IMF, she founded and served as CEO of Reliance Risk Advisory Solutions, a Nairobi-based consultancy firm.

Beyond her executive roles, Onyango actively participates in board positions. She is a non-executive director of the Kenya Commercial Bank Group and Cytonn Investments. She also serves on the board of Fairtrade Africa, where she chairs the audit and finance committee. 

Nancy Onyango is married and a mother of three sons.

title: Alexander Vovin
text:
Alexander Vovin was a Soviet-born, Russian-American linguist specializing in East Asian languages who passed away in April 2022 at the age of 61 from cancer. He was known for his extensive research on Japanese historical linguistics, particularly its etymology, morphology, and phonology, as well as Japanese philology of the Nara and Heian periods. He served as Director of Studies at the Centre de recherches linguistiques sur l'Asie orientale (CRLAO) at the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales (EHESS) in Paris, France, from 2014 until his death.

Vovin’s academic journey began with a Master's degree in structural and applied linguistics from Saint Petersburg State University in 1983, followed by a Ph.D. in historical Japanese linguistics and premodern Japanese literature from the same institution in 1987. His doctoral dissertation focused on the *Hamamatsu Chūnagon Monogatari*.  He initially worked as a Junior Researcher at the St. Petersburg Institute of Oriental Studies before moving to the United States in 1990. Over the next fourteen years, he held assistant and associate professorships at the University of Michigan, Miami University, and the University of Hawaiʻi, achieving full professorship at the latter in 2003. He also had several visiting professorships at institutions in Kyoto, Bochum, Germany, and Tokyo, Japan.

His research interests were broad, encompassing not only Japanese but also the moribund Ainu language, as well as Inner Asian languages and Kra–Dai languages, often analyzing them through Chinese transcriptions. He also studied Old and Middle Korean texts.  A significant, unfinished project at the time of his death was a complete academic translation, with critical edition and commentary, of the *Man'yōshū*, the oldest and largest premodern Japanese poetic anthology.  He also recently completed work on the *Bussokuseki no Uta* of Yakushi-ji temple in Nara, published in 2021. 

Vovin was deeply involved in the large-scale project of creating an Etymological Dictionary of the Japonic Languages, coordinating the effort from 2019 until his death, supported by a €2,470,200 grant from the European Union. Unfortunately, this project was discontinued following his passing.  He authored numerous publications throughout his career, including *A Reconstruction of Proto-Ainu* (1993) and *Korea-Japonica: A Re-evaluation of a Common Genetic Origin* (2008), and a multi-volume translation of the *Man'yoshu* spanning from 2009 to 2018. 

He was married twice, first to Varvara G. Lebedeva-Vovina, with whom he had a son, and later to fellow researcher Sambi Ishisaki, with whom he had two more children. A festschrift was published in 2021 in his honor, marking his 60th birthday, reflecting the esteem he held within the academic community.

title: David Bogue
text:
David Bogue was a Scottish religious leader born on February 18, 1750, at Hallydown Farm in Berwickshire, Scotland. He was the son of farmer John Bogue and Margaret Swanston, and initially received his education in Eyemouth. Following his studies in Divinity at Edinburgh University, he was authorized to preach by the Church of Scotland. However, unable to secure a position within Scotland, he moved to London in 1771. There he worked as a teacher in schools located in Edmonton, Hampstead, and Camberwell.

In 1777, Bogue became the minister of an independent Congregational church in Gosport, Hampshire, succeeding James Watson and Thomas Williams in that role. He is particularly remembered for establishing an institution in 1771 dedicated to training men for the ministry. This academy played a crucial role in the formation of the London Missionary Society, effectively serving as its initial foundation. By 1800, the London Missionary Society was formally sending prospective missionaries to Bogue for preparation. 

Bogue’s influence extended to the training of some of the earliest Protestant missionaries to China, notably Robert Morrison and William Milne, whom he instructed in 1804-1805 and 1809-1812 respectively. He himself had intended to travel to India as a missionary in 1796, but was prevented from doing so due to opposition from the East India Company. Later in his life, in 1824, he prepared Samuel Dyer for missionary work before Dyer departed for Penang. 

Beyond his work in education and the ministry, Bogue was actively involved in the founding of both the British and Foreign Bible Society and the Religious Tract Society. He collaborated with James Bennett, the minister of Romsey, to produce a notable three-volume *History of Dissenters*, published in 1809. He also authored *An Essay on the Divine Authority of the New Testament*. In 1815, Yale University recognized his contributions by awarding him a Doctor of Divinity degree. David Bogue died on October 25, 1825, in Brighton while accompanying the London Missionary Society on their annual tour. He left behind a legacy as a pivotal figure in the development of missionary work and nonconformist religious thought.

title: Daniil Medvedev
text:
Daniil Sergeyevich Medvedev, born in Moscow in 1996, is a Russian professional tennis player who has reached the world No. 1 ranking. He currently holds 20 ATP Tour-level singles titles, most notably the 2021 US Open and the 2020 ATP Finals. He began his professional career with a debut in the 2015 Kremlin Cup and first competed in a Grand Slam tournament at Wimbledon in 2017. His breakthrough year was 2019, marked by reaching the top 10 and a string of six consecutive tournament finals, including a run to the US Open final. 

Medvedev’s most significant achievement to date was winning the 2021 US Open, defeating Novak Djokovic and preventing him from completing a calendar-year Grand Slam. He followed this with a period of fluctuating form, briefly dropping out of the top 10 before returning to the top 5 in early 2023, reaching two further major finals. In 2022, he became the first player since Andy Murray, outside of the “Big Three” (Federer, Nadal, Djokovic), to achieve the world No. 1 ranking, joining fellow Russians Yevgeny Kafelnikov and Marat Safin in this accomplishment. 

Growing up in Moscow, Medvedev's father, a computer engineer, ran a building materials business. He has two older sisters. His introduction to tennis came at age six, prompted by an advertisement and encouraged by his father. His first coach was Ekaterina Kryuchkova, who had previously worked with Vera Zvonareva. He pursued both musical interests, studying the harpsichord and guitar, alongside his athletic training. He initially studied physics and math, then economics at Moscow State Institute of International Relations, but later switched to physical education to focus on tennis, eventually training at an academy in Antibes, France, where his parents now reside as retirees.

Medvedev is fluent in Russian, French, and English, having spent much of his career living and training abroad. He married Daria Chernyshkova in 2018, and they have two daughters, Alisa born in 2022 and Vika born in 2025. He credits his marriage with improving his tennis results, noting a significant ranking increase after proposing. He is also a supporter of FC Bayern Munich. 

As a junior player, Medvedev achieved a career-high ranking of No. 13 and reached the third round of the Junior Australian Open and US Open in 2013 and 2014 respectively. His professional career began with doubles play at the 2015 Kremlin Cup, followed by his first ATP singles main draw appearance in 2016. He faced controversy early in his career, being disqualified from a Challenger event for comments perceived as racially insensitive. He steadily climbed the rankings, achieving his first ATP title in Sydney in 2018 and subsequently winning titles in Winston-Salem and Tokyo that same year. He continued his success in 2019 with Masters 1000 titles in Cincinnati and Shanghai, and a runner-up finish at the US Open. He capped off 2020 by winning the ATP Finals, defeating the top three ranked players en route to the championship. He began 2021 strongly, winning the ATP Cup and reaching the Australian Open final before securing his first Grand Slam title at the US Open.

title: Minako Honda
text:
Minako Honda, born Minako Kudo on July 31, 1967, was a Japanese idol and singer who achieved fame in the 1980s and continued a diverse career in music and theatre until her death in 2005. She initially gained attention as a young singer influenced by her mother’s aspirations, competing in the televised “Star Tanjō!” show at age 14, although she was ultimately unsuccessful in winning. While at school in 1983, she became involved with Bondo Kikaku, a record label, but felt their direction was not for her and resolved to pursue a solo career.

Her breakthrough came in 1984 when she won the Grand Prix at the Nagasaki Kayo Festival, a televised competition for new idols. This led to her debut in 1985 as Minako Honda with the single "Satsui no Vacance," for which she received a Japan Record Award for best new artist. Early in her career, she briefly sparked controversy with a performance of “1986 nen no Marilyn”, considered provocative for the time due to her suggestive dancing and attire. 

In 1988, Honda attempted to revitalize her career by forming the all-girl rock group “Minako with Wild Cats”, but the group disbanded after a year without achieving success. A significant turning point arrived in 1990 when she successfully auditioned for the role of Kim in the Tokyo production of *Miss Saigon*, beating out over 15,000 other candidates. While performing in *Miss Saigon*, an incident occurred during a visit to Vietnam where she was photographed in the Củ Chi tunnels draped in a Vietnamese flag, resulting in a fine and expulsion from the country.

Honda continued to excel on stage, taking on leading roles in productions of *Fiddler on the Roof*, *The King and I*, and *Les Misérables*.  Throughout her career, she branched out musically, exploring classical genres and releasing albums featuring soprano vocals and religious pieces. She also contributed theme songs to anime series, including "Kaze no Uta" for *Hunter x Hunter*.  In her later years, she became known for her improved vocal ability, particularly for her sustained 30-second note in the song “Tsubasa”. 

In late 2004, she added a period to her name, believing it addressed perceived judgment about her surname.  She was diagnosed with acute myelogenous leukemia on January 5, 2005, after initially experiencing cold-like symptoms. Despite brief periods of recovery following treatment, the leukemia relapsed and she developed lung complications. Minako Honda died on November 6, 2005, at Juntendo University Hospital in Tokyo, at the age of 38. Throughout her career, she released a substantial body of work, including 14 original albums, 25 singles, and several home-video releases.

title: Ronaldinho
text:
Ronaldo de Assis Moreira, known globally as Ronaldinho Gaúcho or simply Ronaldinho, was a Brazilian professional footballer considered one of the greatest players of all time. Born in Porto Alegre, Brazil in 1980, he excelled as an attacking midfielder or left winger, earning accolades including two FIFA World Player of the Year awards and a Ballon d'Or. Uniquely, he achieved the distinction of winning a World Cup, Copa América, Confederations Cup, Champions League, Copa Libertadores, and Ballon d’Or – a feat unmatched by any other player. Renowned for his exceptional dribbling, accurate free kicks, skillful use of tricks and feints, and creative passing, he was nicknamed “O Bruxo” ('The Wizard').

Ronaldinho began his career with Grêmio in 1998, then moved to Paris Saint-Germain in 2001, winning the UEFA Intertoto Cup before joining Barcelona in 2003. It was at Barcelona where he truly flourished. His second season saw him win his first FIFA World Player of the Year award as Barcelona secured the 2004–05 La Liga title. The following season was arguably his peak, playing a vital role in Barcelona winning the 2005–06 UEFA Champions League – their first in fourteen years – and another La Liga title, completing a league and Champions League double. This success led to him receiving the 2005 Ballon d'Or and a second FIFA World Player of the Year award. His performance in the El Clásico against Real Madrid in 2005 was particularly memorable, earning him a standing ovation from the opposing fans at the Santiago Bernabéu, a rare honor previously only given to Diego Maradona. He is credited with significantly changing Barcelona’s fortunes during his time there.

After a period of decline marked by injury and a perceived lack of dedication, Ronaldinho left Barcelona for AC Milan in 2008, where he won the 2010–11 Serie A. He then returned to Brazil to play for Flamengo in 2011 and Atlético Mineiro in 2012, winning the 2013 Copa Libertadores with the latter. Subsequent moves took him to Mexico with Querétaro and back to Brazil with Fluminense in 2015. Throughout his career, he was repeatedly recognized with individual awards, including three inclusions in the UEFA Team of the Year and the FIFA World XI. He also earned the UEFA Club Footballer of the Year award in 2006 and the South American Footballer of the Year in 2013, and was named in Pelé’s FIFA 100 list in 2004. In 2009, he was voted World Player of the Decade 2000s, surpassing Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Internationally, Ronaldinho earned 97 caps for Brazil, scoring 33 goals and participating in two FIFA World Cups. He was a key member of the 2002 FIFA World Cup winning team, playing alongside Ronaldo and Rivaldo, and was included in the tournament’s All-Star Team. He also captained Brazil to victory in the 2005 FIFA Confederations Cup, earning man of the match in the final, and led the Olympic team to a bronze medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics. His early life was marked by tragedy when his father died in a swimming pool accident when he was eight, but his brother Roberto became his manager and his sister Deisi acted as his press coordinator. He developed his signature skills through futsal and beach football, and was identified as a rising star at the 1997 U-17 World Championship.

title: PewDiePie
text:
Felix Kjellberg, known online as PewDiePie, is a Swedish YouTuber celebrated and scrutinized for his influence on internet culture. Born in Gothenburg in 1989, he began his YouTube channel in 2010, initially focusing on “Let’s Play” videos of horror and action games. His channel rapidly gained popularity, becoming one of the fastest-growing in 2012 and 2013 and ultimately surpassing all others in subscriber count by August 2013. For a period between 2014 and 2017, PewDiePie also held the title of YouTube’s most-viewed channel.

As his audience grew, Kjellberg broadened his content beyond gaming, incorporating vlogs, comedy sketches, formatted shows, and music videos. YouTube itself enlisted him to star in a reality web series as part of its subscription service relaunch. However, his content increasingly attracted controversy, culminating in a 2017 *Wall Street Journal* article alleging antisemitic content and imagery. While Kjellberg acknowledged some content was inappropriate, he defended it as misinterpreted humor and criticized the reporting. This led to companies severing business ties with him.

A notable period followed involving a public competition with Indian record label T-Series for the most subscribers, ultimately resulting in T-Series overtaking his channel in early 2019. Kjellberg responded by refocusing on gaming, particularly *Minecraft*, which generated record viewership. In the 2020s, he adopted a more reserved online presence, reducing upload frequency and taking breaks from the internet. He moved to Japan with his wife, Italian internet personality Marzia, and has since semi-retired from YouTube, prioritizing personal enjoyment over career demands. Despite this shift, his channel remains one of the most subscribed and viewed on the platform, boasting over 110 million subscribers and 29.4 billion views.

Throughout his career, Kjellberg has been recognized as a pioneer of YouTube and a key figure in gaming and internet culture. His popularity has boosted game sales and facilitated charity fundraising. While much debate surrounds his legacy, he's been lauded as influential, yet also criticized for potentially promoting harmful ideologies. He himself has admitted to underestimating his impact as a content creator. He was named one of Time magazine’s 100 most influential people in 2016.

Kjellberg’s early life saw an interest in art, drawing video game characters and playing games like *Star Fox* and *Donkey Kong Country*. In high school, he prioritized gaming and internet cafes over classes, funding a computer purchase by selling artwork. He briefly attended Chalmers University of Technology to study industrial engineering and management but left in 2011, stating a lack of interest in the subject rather than a deliberate pursuit of YouTube stardom. He initially funded his early videos through various jobs, including working as a harbor captain and at a hot dog stand.

His initial YouTube success came from gaming commentaries, specifically Let’s Plays of horror games like *Amnesia: The Dark Descent*. He launched a weekly vlog series, “Fridays with PewDiePie,” diversifying his content early on. He initially signed with Machinima but moved to Maker Studios after feeling neglected, eventually launching the Revelmode sub-network with other YouTubers. Over time, his content evolved, becoming more experimental and incorporating viral challenges and meme reviews, a shift he attributed to boredom and platform incentives. He faced criticism for jokes about sensitive topics, and controversies surrounding his content have shaped his public image.

title: Jeremy Northam
text:
Jeremy Northam is an English actor born on December 1, 1961, in Cambridge, Cambridgeshire. His father, John Northam, was a professor of literature and theatre. He received his education at Bedford College, London, earning a B.A. in English in 1984, and furthered his training at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School and is also an alumnus of Royal Holloway, University of London.

Northam began his screen career with a television appearance in “American Playhouse” in 1987, followed by roles in “Wish Me Luck” and “Piece of Cake.” He quickly gained recognition on stage, notably stepping into the role of Hamlet at the Royal National Theatre in 1989, filling in for both Ian Charleson and Daniel Day-Lewis. This performance earned him the 1990 Laurence Olivier Award for Best Newcomer in a Play for his work in *The Voysey Inheritance*.

Throughout his career, Northam has consistently appeared in both British and American films. Some of his notable film credits include *The Net* (1995), *Emma* (1996), *Amistad* (1997), *An Ideal Husband* (1999), *The Winslow Boy* (1999), *Gosford Park* (2001), and *Enigma* (2001). He portrayed Welsh actor and singer Ivor Novello in *Gosford Park* and also showcased his singing ability on the film’s soundtrack, performing several of Novello's songs with his brother Christopher accompanying him on piano. Later film roles included portraying singer Dean Martin in the CBS film *Martin and Lewis* (2002), golfer Walter Hagen in *Bobby Jones: Stroke of Genius* (2004), John Brodie Innes in *Creation* (2009), and philosopher Bertrand Russell in *The Man Who Knew Infinity* (2015). 

He has also worked extensively in television, most recently playing British Prime Minister Anthony Eden in the Netflix series *The Crown* (2016–2017) and earlier as Thomas More in the Showtime series *The Tudors* (2007–2008).

Beyond acting, Northam has a strong presence in audiobook narration, having recorded works by authors such as C.S. Lewis, Henry James, Gerard Manley Hopkins, Graham Greene, Michelle Paver, and George Orwell. 

He was married to Canadian make-up artist Liz Moro in April 2005, but they later divorced. He has a substantial stage career as well, with performances in productions of *The Three Sisters*, *Love’s Labour’s Lost*, and *Hay Fever* amongst others.

title: Isla Fisher
text:
Isla Lang Fisher, born in Oman in 1976 to Scottish parents, is an Australian actress who began her career in commercials before gaining recognition for her role as Shannon Reed on the Australian soap opera *Home and Away* from 1994 to 1997. During her time on the show, she received two Logie Award nominations. She transitioned to Hollywood in 2002 with a part in *Scooby-Doo*, and has since appeared in numerous films including *Wedding Crashers* (2005), *Confessions of a Shopaholic* (2009), *The Great Gatsby* (2013) and *Now You See Me* (2013). She has also lent her voice to animated features like *Horton Hears a Who!* (2008) and *Rango* (2011). 

Fisher’s early life was spent moving from Oman to Scotland and then to Perth, Australia, when she was six. She describes herself as feeling very Australian and having a laid-back attitude to life. She attended Swanbourne Primary School and Methodist Ladies’ College and actively participated in school theatre productions.  At 21, she pursued further training at L'École Internationale de Théâtre Jacques Lecoq in Paris, studying clowning, mime, and musical theatre. Prior to her success as an actress, she even published two young adult novels.

After leaving *Home and Away*, Fisher continued to hone her skills with theatre work in the UK and a role in a German slasher film before finding success in Hollywood. *Wedding Crashers* proved to be a breakthrough role, earning her a Best Breakthrough Performance Award at the MTV Movie Awards. She continued to take on diverse roles, including parts in the thriller *The Lookout* and the comedy *Hot Rod*.  She also voiced characters in animated films, winning an Alliance of Women Film Journalists Award for her work in *Rango*. 

Fisher starred in *The Great Gatsby* and *Now You See Me* in 2013, cementing her mainstream recognition. She also took on a recurring role in the Netflix revival of *Arrested Development* and has starred in the comedy-drama series *Wolf Like Me* since 2022. Beyond acting, she has continued to write, authoring both young adult novels and the *Marge in Charge* book series. 

From 2010 until 2025, Fisher was married to English comedian Sacha Baron Cohen, and they have three children together. Throughout her career, she has described herself as fortunate, acknowledging the sometimes unpredictable nature of the industry, and expressed gratitude for the opportunities she’s been given.

title: Don Beard
text:
Donald Derek Beard, born in 1920 and passing away in 1982, was a New Zealand cricketer who also enjoyed a career in education and excelled in several other sports. He represented New Zealand in four Test matches between 1952 and 1956. Before his cricketing career gained prominence, Beard demonstrated dedication to his studies, commuting 15 miles daily by bicycle to attend Palmerston North Boys’ High School. He then trained as a teacher in Auckland and later earned a Diploma in Education and a Master of Arts degree from Victoria University in Wellington, completing his Master’s thesis on the history of physical education in New Zealand primary schools.

Beard began his first-class cricket journey with Wellington in 1945, though initial appearances were hampered by recovery from burns sustained while fighting a fire. He later became a key figure for Central Districts, debuting for them in their inaugural Plunket Shield match in 1950-51. His performances in the 1951-52 Plunket Shield season, where he claimed 16 wickets, earned him selection for the Test series against the West Indies, where he took four wickets.

He was a consistent performer for Central Districts, notably contributing to their first Plunket Shield victory in the 1953-54 season with both bat and ball, scoring 255 runs and taking 15 wickets. During this season, he achieved his highest first-class score of 81 not out. Known for his sweep shot, some believed he could have scored more runs had he focused less on bowling. His bowling prowess peaked in the 1955-56 season, topping the Plunket Shield bowling averages with 28 wickets at a remarkable average of 10.64, including a significant number of maiden overs. 

A strong performance against the West Indies in a non-Test match at Wanganui, where he excelled with both bat and ball, led to his recall to the Test team. He played a vital role in New Zealand’s historic first Test victory, contributing with both batting and bowling. This proved to be his final appearance in Test cricket. He continued playing first-class cricket, delivering his best innings and match figures in 1956-57 against Otago.

After retiring from playing regularly, Beard became principal of Te Aroha College in Waikato in 1961, and continued to play a few games for Northern Districts. He maintained his form, taking multiple five-wicket hauls in consecutive matches. He played his last game in 1964-65, shortly after his 45th birthday, and also participated in Hawke Cup cricket for several teams over a lengthy period. Beyond cricket, Beard was a tall, multi-talented sportsman, representing New Zealand in basketball, being a skilled amateur golfer, and playing rugby union for various teams, even captaining Wanganui and the North Island. He died during a holiday in England in 1982, leaving behind a legacy that included his son, Derek, who also played first-class cricket.

title: Harry Cave
text:
Henry Butler “Harry” Cave was a New Zealand cricketer born in 1922, who represented his country in 19 Test matches, nine of which he captained. He came from a farming and cricket family in the Wanganui region, with an uncle who served as a Test umpire. After schooling, he continued farming, a profession that often impacted his cricket commitments, though he was supported by his brother Tom. 

Cave was an all-rounder, standing six feet two inches tall, known for initially bowling accurate medium-pace before adapting to seamers, cutters, and in-swingers after a 1947 elbow injury. He began playing for Wanganui in his teens and excelled in the Hawke Cup, later debuting for Wellington in 1945. He first toured with New Zealand to England in 1949, playing in all four Tests, but struggled to take wickets on the favorable batting surfaces.

The 1950s brought significant success. He was instrumental in Central Districts’ promising start in the Plunket Shield, and in 1952-53, he set a New Zealand record for the ninth wicket partnership, adding 239 runs with Ian Leggat against Otago. He also achieved an impressive feat of taking 13 wickets in a single day against Auckland, with figures of 7 for 31 and 6 for 33. He captained Central Districts to their first Plunket Shield title in 1953-54, also leading the bowling averages for the competition.

Cave regained his Test place in 1954 and was appointed captain for a demanding tour of Pakistan and India in 1955-56. The tour was fraught with challenges – harsh conditions, poor facilities, illness, and contentious umpiring – but Cave maintained a diplomatic approach, bowling the most overs of any player. The strain took a toll, causing him significant weight loss and a lengthy recovery period. He captained New Zealand in the first Test against the West Indies following the tour, and later contributed to New Zealand's first Test victory against the same opponents in 1956, achieving his best Test bowling figures of eight wickets for 43 runs.

While he wasn't a consistent success on subsequent tours, including a less fruitful trip to England in 1958 as vice-captain, he demonstrated his skill in unofficial matches against Australia in 1956-57, taking 17 wickets while his teammates collectively took the same number. 

Outside of cricket, Cave married Vonnie Anderson in 1951 and they had two sons. He was a keen camellia grower, developing a variety named after himself. He passed away in Wanganui in 1989, and his wife continued to contribute to the community through photography and horticulture, being recognized with a New Zealand Order of Merit in 2009 before her death in 2021.

title: Thierry Henry
text:
Thierry Henry, born in 1977, is a French football icon considered one of the greatest players of all time, and particularly celebrated as the best in Premier League history. Renowned for his finishing, dribbling, speed, and ability to create chances, he twice came close to winning the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year awards in 2003 and 2004. He achieved numerous individual accolades, including a record three FWA Footballer of the Year awards and being named to the PFA Team of the Year six consecutive times. He was also recognized by Pelé in the FIFA 100 list of the world’s greatest living players in 2004.

Henry began his professional career with Monaco in 1994 before a relatively short and unfulfilling stint with Juventus, where limited playing time and disagreements with management prompted a move to Arsenal in 1999. Under the guidance of Arsène Wenger, he flourished, becoming Arsenal’s all-time leading scorer with 228 goals. He led the team to three FA Cups and two Premier League titles, famously being a key member of the ‘Invincibles’ team that went undefeated throughout the 2003-04 Premier League season. He served as club captain in his final two seasons, reaching the 2006 Champions League final before transferring to Barcelona in 2007. At Barcelona, he was instrumental in a historic treble win in the 2008-09 season, securing La Liga, Copa del Rey, and Champions League titles. He later played for the New York Red Bulls in Major League Soccer, with a loan spell back at Arsenal in 2012 before retiring in 2014.

Henry also enjoyed significant success with the French national team, winning the 1998 FIFA World Cup, UEFA Euro 2000, and the 2003 FIFA Confederations Cup. He was a five-time French Player of the Year and held the record for most international goals for France from 2007 until 2022. He retired from international football after the 2010 FIFA World Cup, having made 123 appearances and scored 51 goals.

Following his retirement as a player, Henry transitioned into coaching. He began by coaching Arsenal’s youth teams while also working as a pundit. He then served as an assistant coach for Belgium before taking on the head coach role at Monaco in 2018, followed by a managerial position at Montréal Impact. He subsequently returned to Belgium as an assistant coach and, more recently, managed the France national under-21 and Olympic teams, leading them to a silver medal at the 2024 Summer Games.

Born and raised in Les Ulis, a suburb of Paris, Henry’s talent was evident early on, initially encouraged by his father despite his initial lack of enthusiasm for the sport. He progressed through youth academies, eventually joining Monaco after impressing a scout with a six-goal performance in a single match. While at Monaco, he was initially deployed as a winger before being developed into a prolific striker, a position where he would ultimately achieve global recognition. His early career was marked by a desire to prove himself and reach the highest levels of the game.

title: Rory Burns
text:
Rory Burns, born in 1990 in Epsom, Surrey, is an English cricketer who currently captains Surrey in first-class and List A cricket, while also having represented England in Test matches. A left-handed opening batsman, he began his domestic career with Surrey, making his first-class debut in 2011 after playing Second XI cricket for both Surrey and Hampshire. He initially filled various roles, including wicket-keeping, before establishing himself as a consistent opening batsman, reaching 1000 runs in a season for the first time in 2014. 

A significant incident in his domestic career occurred in 2015 during a T20 Blast game where he collided with teammate Moisés Henriques, both sustaining injuries that led to the match being abandoned. Burns’s leadership qualities were recognized when he was appointed Surrey captain in 2018, leading the team to County Championship titles in 2018, 2022, 2023 and 2024. He consistently performed well with the bat, scoring over 1000 runs in five consecutive seasons up to 2018, and being the leading run-scorer in Division One that year with 1359 runs. His availability for Surrey was sometimes limited due to his international commitments.

Burns earned his England Test debut in 2018, stepping in to replace Alastair Cook for the tour of Sri Lanka. He continued to feature in the Test side, touring the West Indies and eventually securing his place as an opener. A breakthrough moment came during the 2019 Ashes series, where he scored his maiden Test century at Edgbaston, contributing significantly to England’s campaign and becoming the third-highest run scorer in the series. 

His form continued into the 2019-20 winter with a second Test century against New Zealand, but an ankle injury sustained while playing football ruled him out of the remainder of the South Africa series. He returned for series against the West Indies and Pakistan in 2020, with mixed results, and was later dropped after a disappointing showing in India in 2021. However, he regained his place and was named England’s player of the series against New Zealand in 2021, showcasing strong form. The following series against India proved less successful, and he endured a particularly difficult start to the 2021-22 Ashes, becoming the first batsman since 1936 to be dismissed with the first ball of an Ashes series. He was subsequently dropped from the Test team after the series.

Outside of cricket, Burns is close friends with fellow cricketer Jason Roy, with whom he attended school and who served as his best man at his wedding, and vice versa. He missed the 2021 tour of Sri Lanka due to the birth of his daughter.

title: James Theodore Bent
text:
James Theodore Bent, born in 1852 in Liverpool, was a British explorer, archaeologist, and author who dedicated much of his life to investigating ancient civilizations and documenting his findings. He came from a wealthy background; his grandfather founded Bent’s Breweries, a successful business that provided the family fortune. He was educated at Malvern Wells, Repton School, and Wadham College, Oxford, graduating from the latter in 1875. 

Bent’s travels and research began after marrying Mabel Hall-Dare in 1877, who became a crucial partner in his work, acting as his photographer and keeping a detailed diary of their expeditions. They frequently travelled abroad, initially exploring Italy and Greece, and Bent published several books early in his career, including works on San Marino, Genoa, and Giuseppe Garibaldi.  He focused increasingly on archaeological and ethnographic research, publishing “The Cyclades” based on extensive research in the Aegean islands.

Much of Bent’s work centered on the Eastern Mediterranean and Anatolia between 1883 and 1888, with findings shared through publications in journals like the *Journal of Hellenic Studies*. He undertook significant excavations in the Bahrein Islands in 1889, seeking evidence of Phoenician origins, and travelled through Persia, meeting Shah Naser al-Din Shah Qajar. In 1890, he moved on to South Africa, specifically Mashonaland, where he conducted the first detailed examination of the Great Zimbabwe ruins, believing them to be built by ancestors of the Shona people – a view contested at the time but now largely accepted by modern archaeologists.

Bent continued his explorations in Ethiopia in 1893, documenting the ruins of Axum in his book “The Sacred City of the Ethiopians.” He then ventured into the remote Hadramut region of Southern Arabia, undertaking risky journeys between 1893 and 1894 to study the region’s ancient history and physical features. Further explorations along the Dhofar coast in 1894-1895 led him to identify ruins he believed to be related to the frankincense trade. 

Tragically, Bent contracted malarial fever during a journey to South Arabia and Socotra in 1896-1897 and died in London in May 1897, shortly after his return. His wife, Mabel, continued their work by publishing “Southern Arabia, Soudan and Sakotra” in 1900, detailing their final expedition. 

Bent’s extensive collections of artefacts, numbering in the hundreds, are largely held in the British Museum, with smaller collections distributed amongst various museums in the UK, Greece, Turkey, South Africa, and Zimbabwe. His legacy extends beyond his written works and collections; several species of shells, plants, and a lizard have been named in his honour. Digitized versions of his original notebooks are now accessible through the Hellenic Society’s archive.

title: Kajal Aggarwal
text:
Kajal Aggarwal, born on June 19, 1985, is a prominent Indian actress working primarily in Telugu, Tamil, and Hindi films. She is recognized as one of the highest-paid actresses in South Indian cinema and has received three SIIMA Awards, alongside four Filmfare Awards South nominations. Aggarwal began her acting career with a small role in the 2004 Hindi film *Kyun! Ho Gaya Na…* and debuted in Telugu cinema with *Lakshmi Kalyanam* in 2007. However, it was *Chandamama* later that same year that brought her wider recognition.

A significant turning point in her career came with the 2009 film *Magadheera*, a massive commercial success that earned her critical acclaim. This propelled her to stardom, leading to a string of notable Telugu films including *Darling*, *Brindavanam*, *Mr. Perfect*, *Businessman*, *Naayak*, *Baadshah*, *Govindudu Andarivadele*, *Temper*, *Khaidi No. 150*, *Nene Raju Nene Mantri*, *Awe*, and *Bhagavanth Kesari*.  She also achieved success in Tamil films like *Naan Mahaan Alla*, *Maattrraan*, *Thuppakki*, *Jilla*, *Vivegam*, *Mersal*, and *Comali*.  Her Hindi film credits include *Singham* and *Special 26*. 

Aggarwal’s rise to fame was not immediate; she faced initial struggles gaining recognition after her debut. She comes from a Punjabi family settled in Mumbai; her father is a textile entrepreneur and her mother is a confectioner who also manages her career. She has a younger sister, Nisha Aggarwal, who is also an actress. Kajal pursued a degree in mass media with a specialization in marketing and advertising, having once aspired to an MBA.

In 2020, she achieved another milestone with the unveiling of her wax figure at Madame Tussauds Singapore, the first for an actress from South Indian cinema.  Throughout her career, she’s been praised for her performances, notably in *Magadheera*, where she played dual roles, and more recently in *Nene Raju Nene Mantri*. While some roles have been more challenging, and some films haven't performed as well, she has consistently remained a prominent figure in the industry.

Her personal life took a new turn when she married Gautam Kitchlu in a private ceremony in Mumbai on October 30, 2020, after announcing their engagement earlier that month.  The couple welcomed their son, Neil, in April 2022.  Aggarwal continues to work, with upcoming projects including *Sikandar*, *Kannappa*, *Indian 3*, *The India Story*, and a role as Mandodari in *Ramayana: Part 1*.

title: Gary Woodland
text:
Gary Woodland is an American professional golfer who achieved his greatest success by winning the U.S. Open in 2019, his first major championship. Born in Topeka, Kansas in 1984, he initially pursued basketball on a scholarship at Washburn University before switching to golf at the University of Kansas, where he studied sociology and won four collegiate tournaments. He turned professional in 2007 after a successful amateur career, spending time on the Nationwide Tour before earning his PGA Tour card through qualifying school in 2008.

His early PGA Tour career was marked by inconsistency and a shoulder injury in 2009. He spent time alternating between the PGA and Nationwide Tours in 2010, again relying on qualifying school to regain his full PGA Tour status. His breakthrough came in 2011 with a victory at the Transitions Championship, securing his first PGA Tour title and a place in the Masters Tournament. He also won the Omega Mission Hills World Cup that year alongside Matt Kuchar. 

Throughout his career, Woodland has accumulated four PGA Tour victories, including the Waste Management Phoenix Open in 2018 after a five-year drought. He demonstrated strong performance at the PGA Championship, reaching the final of the WGC-Cadillac Match Play in 2015 and leading after 36 holes in 2018, ultimately finishing sixth. He also came close at the 2019 Sentry Tournament of Champions, losing to Xander Schauffele after leading the final round.

His 2019 U.S. Open win at Pebble Beach was particularly notable. He held the 54-hole lead and finished with a score of 271, three strokes ahead of the defending champion, Brooks Koepka. This victory was especially meaningful as he shared it with Amy Bockerstette, a collegiate golfer with Down syndrome, whom he invited to play a hole at a practice round and later FaceTimed after his win. Woodland was also part of the winning U.S. team at the 2019 Presidents Cup.

More recently, in August 2023, Woodland publicly revealed his diagnosis of a brain lesion and underwent surgery in September of the same year. In recognition of his courage, he was awarded the PGA Tour Courage Award in February 2025. Throughout his career, he’s been recognized for his consistency, achieving six consecutive cuts made twice and a two-tournament streak of top-10 finishes in 2019.

title: Andriy Yarmolenko
text:
Andriy Yarmolenko, born in Leningrad in 1989 to Ukrainian parents, is a professional footballer who currently plays as a winger or forward for Dynamo Kyiv and captains the Ukraine national team. His family relocated to Chernihiv, Ukraine, when he was young, and he began playing football at the age of four or five, initially with a self-made ball due to financial constraints. He was first formally coached by Mykola Lypoviy at the Yunist Chernihiv football school.

Yarmolenko's club career began with various Ukrainian clubs including Yunist Chernihiv and Desna Chernihiv before he joined Dynamo Kyiv in 2007. He initially played for Dynamo’s reserve team before debuting for the first team in 2008, scoring the winning goal against Vorskla Poltava. Quickly recognized for his speed and physique, he was dubbed the "new Andriy Shevchenko" by the media. He enjoyed significant success with Dynamo Kyiv, winning the Ukrainian Premier League multiple times (2008-09, 2014-15, 2015-16, 2024-25), the Ukrainian Cup (2013-14, 2014-15), and the Ukrainian Super Cup (2009, 2011, 2016). 

In 2017, Yarmolenko moved to Borussia Dortmund, making his debut as a substitute and later scoring in a Champions League match against Tottenham Hotspur. He then joined West Ham United in 2018, where he experienced both success and injury setbacks. He achieved a memorable brace against Everton, contributing to West Ham’s first Premier League win of the 2018-19 season, but suffered a severe Achilles tendon tear that sidelined him for a significant period. He continued to make contributions upon his return, scoring key goals against Norwich City and Manchester United, and notably scoring the winning goal against Chelsea in 2020. After a period with Al-Ain in the United Arab Emirates, he returned to Dynamo Kyiv in 2023, signing a two-year contract.

Yarmolenko has been a key figure for the Ukraine national team since 2009, earning over 125 caps and scoring 46 goals. He has represented Ukraine in four UEFA European Championships (2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024) and played a vital role in their qualification for Euro 2016. He holds the record for the fastest goal scored by a Ukrainian international player. He recently assisted in Wales qualifying for the 2022 World Cup, though the goal was initially credited to Yarmolenko before being attributed to Gareth Bale.

Beyond football, Yarmolenko is a respected figure in his hometown of Chernihiv, where he was made an honorary citizen in 2021. He has demonstrated considerable philanthropy, donating a substantial sum to the Armed Forces of Ukraine following the Russian invasion in 2022 and actively assisting in the evacuation of his wife’s family. He also presented an ambulance to Chernihiv. In September 2024, he achieved his UEFA "A" coaching license. He has received numerous individual accolades, including being named Ukrainian Footballer of the Year on multiple occasions and winning the Ukrainian Premier League’s Player of the Year award.

title: Nelson Mandela
text:
Nelson Mandela was born Rolihlahla Mandela in 1918 in the village of Mvezo, South Africa, into the Thembu royal family. His father was a local chief and councillor, and Mandela received the English name “Nelson” from his teacher at a Methodist school. After his father’s death, he was placed under the guardianship of Chief Jongintaba Dalindyebo, receiving a Western-style education at Clarkebury and Healdtown, before attending the University of Fort Hare. He began studying law at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, where he encountered racial discrimination but also formed friendships with people of various ethnicities and political persuasions.

In Johannesburg, Mandela became involved in anti-colonial politics, joining the African National Congress (ANC) in 1943 and co-founding its Youth League in 1944. Fueled by a desire for Black self-determination, the Youth League advocated for more assertive action against racial segregation. He married Evelyn Mase in 1944 and began working as an articled clerk at a law firm, continuing his legal studies. With the 1948 election bringing the National Party to power and instituting the system of apartheid, Mandela and the ANC committed to dismantling racial segregation. 

Initially committed to non-violent protest, Mandela became influenced by Marxist ideas and, in 1961, co-founded the militant uMkhonto we Sizwe, which launched a sabotage campaign against the apartheid government. He was arrested in 1962 and, after the Rivonia Trial, sentenced to life imprisonment in 1964 for conspiring to overthrow the state. He spent the next 27 years in prison, serving time on Robben Island, Pollsmoor Prison, and Victor Verster Prison.

Amidst growing pressure both within South Africa and internationally, President F.W. de Klerk released Mandela in 1990. Mandela and de Klerk then collaborated to negotiate the end of apartheid, culminating in the first multiracial general election in 1994. Mandela led the ANC to victory and became South Africa's first Black head of state. As president, he focused on racial reconciliation, creating the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to address past human rights abuses. While his administration retained a liberal economic framework, he also introduced measures to address land reform, poverty, and healthcare. 

After serving one term, Mandela stepped down in 1999, dedicating himself to combating poverty and HIV/AIDS through the Nelson Mandela Foundation. Throughout his life, he was a controversial figure, facing criticism from both the right and the left, but he ultimately gained international acclaim for his activism and commitment to social justice. He received numerous honors, including the Nobel Peace Prize, and is widely revered in South Africa as “Madiba” and the “Father of the Nation”. He died in 2013, leaving behind a legacy as a global icon of democracy and equality.

title: Vicente Guerrero
text:
Vicente Ramón Guerrero Saldaña was a key figure in the Mexican War of Independence and served as the nation’s second president in 1829. Born in Tixtla in 1782, he came from a family with diverse occupations including landowners, traders, and members of the Spanish militia. His upbringing involved working in his father’s mule-driven freight business, exposing him to growing discontent with Spanish rule. While his exact ethnic background is debated, he was known for his ability to speak both Spanish and indigenous languages, particularly Nahuatl, which aided his interactions with native populations throughout the revolution.
