Guerrero joined the insurgent army led by José María Morelos in 1810, quickly demonstrating military aptitude. He played a vital role in battles like Zitltala and Tixtla, where his knowledge of the local terrain and ability to communicate with indigenous people proved invaluable. After Morelos’s death in 1815, Guerrero continued the fight, employing guerrilla tactics and becoming a symbol of resistance, remaining the last major rebel leader at large. He secured victories in various regions of southern Mexico, including Ajuchitán and Santa Fe. 

A turning point came in 1820 when Agustín de Iturbide, initially sent to suppress Guerrero’s forces, ultimately allied with him. This alliance, formalized under the Plan de Iguala, proclaimed Mexico’s independence, established a constitutional monarchy, and maintained the Catholic Church's position. Crucially, Guerrero insisted on including a clause guaranteeing equal rights to all inhabitants regardless of race, dismantling the existing casta system. The Army of the Three Guarantees marched into Mexico City in 1821, marking the end of the war.

Following a period of political turmoil and Iturbide’s brief reign as emperor, Guerrero became president in 1829 amidst contested circumstances. His election was secured through a rebellion led by Santa Anna and the resignation of the elected president, Gómez Pedraza. As a liberal, Guerrero championed reforms, most notably the abolition of slavery throughout Mexico in September 1829, though he later exempted Texas due to pressure from American settlers. He also advocated for public education, land reform, and economic development. 

However, Guerrero’s presidency was short-lived. He was overthrown in a rebellion led by his own vice president, Anastasio Bustamante, bringing an end to his time in office and ultimately leading to his death in 1831. Despite the brevity of his term, Guerrero’s legacy remains significant as a champion of independence, equality, and a popular hero representing the hopes of a truly inclusive Mexico.

title: Danny Faure
text:
Danny Faure, born on May 8, 1962, is a Seychellois politician who served as the fourth President of Seychelles from October 16, 2016, to October 26, 2020. Prior to his presidency, he held the position of Vice-President of Seychelles from 2010 to 2016, and is a member of the United Seychelles Party, formerly known as the People’s Party. 

Faure was born in Kilembe, Uganda, to Seychellois parents, and received his primary and secondary education in the Seychelles itself. He then pursued higher education at the University of Havana in Cuba, where he earned a degree in political science.

His career in public service began in 1985, at the age of 23, when he joined the Seychelles education ministry as an assistant curriculum officer. He also shared his knowledge as a lecturer at both the National Youth Service and the Seychelles Polytechnic. Following the return of multiparty democracy to the Seychelles in 1993, Faure became the leader of government business in the National Assembly, a role he fulfilled until 1998. He subsequently entered the cabinet as Minister of Education. 

Over the years, Faure held a diverse portfolio of ministerial positions, including those relating to youth, finance, trade and industries, public administration, and information and communication technology. A significant period was spent as Minister of Finance, beginning in 2006, where he oversaw economic reforms recommended by the International Monetary Fund from 2008 to 2013. He also served as designated minister from 2004 to 2010, concurrently holding the finance portfolio when he became Vice-President in July 2010.

Faure ascended to the presidency following the unexpected resignation of President James Michel on September 27, 2016, officially taking office on October 16th. This transition occurred alongside an election resulting in an opposition majority in the National Assembly. As Michel’s term had four years remaining, this period counted towards a full presidential term for Faure. During his presidency, he notably drew attention to environmental concerns, delivering a speech from underwater while visiting a British research submersible in April 2019, advocating for stronger ocean protections. This commitment was further recognized in June 2019 when he received the National Geographic Society’s ‘Planetary and Leadership Award’ in Washington D.C.

In the 2020 presidential election, Faure was defeated by Wavel Ramkalawan, marking the end of his time as President of Seychelles. He is a father to five children: four daughters and one son. He married Shermin Rudie Bastienne on April 4, 2021.

title: Ayman al-Zawahiri
text:
Ayman al-Zawahiri, born in Giza, Egypt in 1951 and dying in 2022, was a physician and pan-Islamist militant who became the second emir of al-Qaeda following the death of Osama bin Laden in 2011. He was a key figure in orchestrating the September 11th attacks and was wanted by both the United States and the United Nations for his involvement in numerous terrorist acts, including the 1998 US embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania, and the 2002 Bali bombings. He was killed in a CIA drone strike in Afghanistan in July 2022.

Al-Zawahiri came from a highly educated and politically active family. His father was a surgeon and professor of pharmacy, and his mother was the daughter of a prominent scholar and diplomat who served as the first rector of King Saud University. His family had ties to both religious and political institutions, and even a connection to the Saudi royal family. He excelled in his studies, earning degrees in medicine and surgery from Cairo University. 

He became involved in Islamist activism during his youth, influenced by figures like Sayyid Qutb, and formed an underground cell dedicated to overthrowing the Egyptian government. This led to his involvement with the Egyptian Islamic Jihad, where he rose to the position of emir and was imprisoned from 1981 to 1984 for his role in the assassination of President Anwar Sadat. Even after his release, he continued planning attacks against the Egyptian government, including the 1995 embassy bombing in Pakistan, resulting in a death sentence *in absentia*.

Al-Zawahiri’s path intertwined with Osama bin Laden's in the late 1980s, and their relationship became central to the growth of al-Qaeda. He initially disapproved of some of bin Laden’s operations, such as the 1995 Pakistani embassy attack.  He eventually merged the Egyptian Islamic Jihad with al-Qaeda in 2001 and formally became bin Laden’s deputy in 2004.  He traveled extensively, working as a surgeon in Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, while simultaneously developing and supporting militant networks. 

Throughout the years, his involvement in terrorist activities expanded, extending to attacks in the United States and Pakistan. He was implicated in the USS Cole bombing and the assassination of former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto. A $25 million bounty was offered for information leading to his capture. He was married multiple times and had several children, some of whom were killed alongside his first wife in a US airstrike in 2001.  Despite years of pursuit, he remained a central figure in al-Qaeda until his death.

title: Ilhan Omar
text:
Ilhan Abdullahi Omar, born in Mogadishu, Somalia in 1982, is currently serving as the U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 5th congressional district since 2019. A member of the Democratic Party, she previously served in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2017 to 2019. She is a prominent figure, being the first Somali American, and the first woman of color to represent Minnesota in Congress, as well as one of the first two Muslim women to serve in the U.S. Congress.

Omar’s early life was marked by the Somali Civil War, leading her family to spend four years in a Kenyan refugee camp before arriving in the U.S. in 1995. The family eventually settled in Minneapolis, where her father worked as a taxi driver and later for the post office. She became a U.S. citizen in 2000.  Her upbringing emphasized the importance of democracy, and she recalls experiencing bullying in school due to her appearance and religious attire. She earned a bachelor's degree in political science and international studies from North Dakota State University in 2011.

Before entering politics, Omar worked as a community nutrition educator and held positions managing campaigns and serving as a policy aide for Minneapolis city council members. In 2016, she was elected to the Minnesota House of Representatives, becoming the first Somali-American legislator in the United States. She then successfully ran for the U.S. House of Representatives in 2018, winning with a significant margin and being sworn in on a copy of the Quran. She has since been re-elected in 2020, 2022, and 2024.

In Congress, Omar is the deputy chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and advocates for policies such as a $15 minimum wage, universal healthcare, student loan debt forgiveness, and the protection of DACA recipients. She also supports abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). She is a vocal critic of Israel, supporting the BDS movement and opposing Israeli settlement policies.  Her views on Israel have attracted controversy and accusations of antisemitism, culminating in a vote by the Republican-controlled House in 2023 to remove her from the Foreign Affairs Committee. 

Omar is a member of "The Squad," a group of progressive female members of Congress advocating for policies like the Green New Deal and Medicare for All. She introduced a resolution supporting the right to boycott as a form of political expression and has introduced articles of impeachment against former President Trump. One of her sponsored bills, designating a Minneapolis post office, became law in 2022.  She has faced scrutiny regarding campaign finance practices, resulting in a requirement to reimburse funds spent on out-of-state travel and a fine, as well as questions regarding joint tax filings.

title: Joey Jordison
text:
Nathan Jonas “Joey” Jordison, born April 26, 1975, and passing away July 26, 2021, was an American musician best known as the original drummer for the heavy metal band Slipknot, identified by the number #1. He was also the guitarist for the horror punk supergroup Murderdolls and involved in numerous other musical projects throughout his career. Jordison grew up in Des Moines, Iowa, beginning to play drums at the age of eight, encouraged by his parents’ preference for radio over television. His parents divorced when he was young, and he took on responsibility within the family, working at his mother’s funeral parlor and playing in bands like Modifidious during his youth.

Before finding fame with Slipknot, Jordison played in a series of bands including The Rejects and Anal Blast, often with future Slipknot members. He joined Paul Gray’s project, the Pale Ones, in 1995, which would evolve into Slipknot. Of the band’s eventual nine-member lineup, Jordison was the third to join. He participated in Slipknot’s first five studio albums and produced their 2005 live album, *9.0: Live*. Alongside Slipknot, Jordison contributed to acts like Rob Zombie, Metallica, Korn, Ministry, and Satyricon, and frequently performed session work for various artists.

In 2002, Jordison revived The Rejects, rebranding them as the Murderdolls, where he played guitar and co-wrote material. The Murderdolls released two studio albums, *Beyond the Valley of the Murderdolls* in 2002 and *Women & Children Last* in 2010, and toured extensively, though their final tour was marred by Jordison’s tinnitus and other issues.  He also founded Scar the Martyr in 2013, which disbanded in 2016, and later formed Vimic and Sinsaenum, the latter being a blackened death metal supergroup he was actively involved with at the time of his death.

Jordison’s departure from Slipknot in December 2013 was initially attributed to personal reasons, but he later revealed he had been fired. He subsequently disclosed a diagnosis of transverse myelitis, a neurological disease that affected his ability to play towards the end of his time with Slipknot. He underwent rehabilitation to regain his physical abilities. 

Throughout his career, Jordison cited influential drummers like Neil Peart, Keith Moon, and John Bonham as inspirations. He utilized various drum brands including Pearl, ddrum, Paiste cymbals, and Promark drumsticks.  Jordison received numerous accolades, including being voted the best drummer of the past 25 years by *Rhythm* magazine in 2010 and being honored with The Golden God Award at the Metal Hammer Golden Gods Awards in 2016. Following his death, numerous musicians paid tribute to his talent and influence. Slipknot dedicated their 2022 album *The End, So Far* to his memory.

title: Diego Suarez (garden designer)
text:
Diego Suarez was born in Bogotá, Colombia in 1888 and died in New York City in 1974. He was a garden designer most recognized for his work on the gardens of James Deering’s Villa Vizcaya in Miami, Florida. His background was steeped in diplomacy and art; his father, Roberto Suarez, was a Colombian diplomat and historian, and his mother, Maria Costa, was Italian. After his father’s death, Suarez and his siblings were raised in Italy. 

He received training in architectural design at the Accademia delle Belle Arti in Florence, where he came under the influence of Arthur Acton. Acton, while restoring the gardens of his Villa La Pietra, imparted Renaissance garden ideals to Suarez, reviving styles favored by designers like Achille Duchêne. Through Acton’s connections, Suarez began designing gardens for wealthy Anglo-Americans in Florence, including projects at Villa Schifanoia for Lewis Einstein and for Charles Loeser, an early collector of Cézanne’s work.

Suarez’s most significant commission came about through a chance encounter. While visiting La Pietra with James Deering and Paul Chalfin, Acton arranged for Suarez to show them various villas. Later, stranded in New York due to the outbreak of war, Suarez reconnected with Deering and Chalfin and was subsequently commissioned to design the gardens at Villa Vizcaya.

The gardens at Vizcaya are designed around the villa’s boat basin, featuring a boat-shaped island, and a south-facing expanse leading to a casino. A key element was a fountain purchased by Deering and Chalfin, which Suarez deliberately placed off the main axis to create a sense of discovery. His design incorporated French baroque-style parterres, contrasts of light and shadow, and subtle changes in elevation to add interest to the flat landscape.

Later in his career, in 1952, Suarez collaborated with architect Frederic Rhinelander King to build a neoclassical house with gardens in Brookville, New York. In 1937, he married Evelyn Marshall Field, the daughter of Charles Henry Marshall and former wife of Marshall Field III, becoming stepfather to Barbara, Bettine, and Marshall Field IV. Diego Suarez is buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in The Bronx, New York City.

title: Ivan Perišić
text:
Ivan Perišić, born in 1989, is a Croatian professional footballer currently playing as a winger for PSV, though he’s versatile enough to play multiple positions including wing-back and attacking midfielder. He is widely considered one of the greatest Croatian players ever. His youth career was spent with Hajduk Split and Sochaux, ultimately signing with Sochaux in 2006 after interest from several other clubs. Though he impressed in the youth ranks, winning the Coupe Gambardella in 2007, he didn't make a first-team appearance for Sochaux, spending time with the B team and a loan spell at Roeselare.

He truly began to make a name for himself at Club Brugge, joining them in 2009. He quickly became a key player, scoring 9 goals in his first season and then topping the Belgian Pro League scoring charts with 22 goals in the 2010–11 season, earning him the Belgian Footballer of the Year award. This success led to a transfer to Borussia Dortmund in 2011, where he won the Bundesliga title. However, his time there was somewhat disrupted by a perceived lack of support from manager Jürgen Klopp, leading to a transfer to VfL Wolfsburg in 2013 for €8 million.

At Wolfsburg, Perišić continued to excel, winning the DFB-Pokal in 2015 and consistently contributing goals. In 2015, he moved to Inter Milan for €16 million, becoming a consistent performer for the club. A loan spell at Bayern Munich in 2019 proved highly successful, as he won the treble – the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and Champions League. Returning to Inter, he added to his trophy cabinet with a Serie A title in 2020–21, the Supercoppa Italiana, and the Coppa Italia in 2021–22.

Perišić has also been a crucial member of the Croatia national team since his debut in 2011, participating in four European Championships (2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024) and three FIFA World Cups (2014, 2018, and 2022). He famously scored an equalizer in the 2018 World Cup final and earned a bronze medal at the 2022 tournament. He is Croatia’s all-time leading goal contributor in major tournaments, with a total of 18 goal involvements, and is seen as a key figure in the nation’s “golden generation.” Throughout his career he has been recognized for his ambidexterity and adaptability, allowing him to thrive in various roles on the field.

title: Jeremy Corbyn
text:
Jeremy Corbyn, born in 1949, is a British politician who served as the Member of Parliament for Islington North from 1983 until his expulsion from the Labour Party in 2024, and now sits as an independent MP. He led the Labour Party as Leader of the Opposition from 2015 to 2020, identifying politically as a socialist. 

Corbyn’s early life was steeped in left-wing activism through his parents, who were involved in supporting the Spanish Republic during the Spanish Civil War. He joined the Labour Party at 16 and became a trade union representative, later being elected to Haringey Council in 1974. Throughout his early career, he was actively involved in various campaigns including Anti-Fascist Action, the Anti-Apartheid Movement, and the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, and consistently advocated for a united Ireland and Palestinian statehood.

As a backbencher MP, Corbyn frequently voted against the Labour whip, demonstrating his independence from party leadership, including challenging New Labour governments. He was a prominent opponent of the Iraq War, chairing the Stop the War Coalition from 2011 to 2015, for which he received peace awards. Following Ed Miliband’s resignation after the 2015 general election, Corbyn unexpectedly won the Labour leadership election, leading to a surge in party membership.

His leadership saw a shift to the left, advocating for policies such as renationalizing public utilities and railways, reducing military intervention, and reversing austerity measures. While historically critical of the European Union, he supported the Remain campaign in the 2016 referendum. He faced a leadership challenge in 2016, which he successfully defended against Owen Smith. The 2017 general election under Corbyn’s leadership saw Labour gain a significant 10 percentage point increase in vote share, its largest gain since 1945. However, his tenure was also marked by criticism regarding antisemitism within the Labour Party, despite his condemnations and efforts to strengthen disciplinary procedures.

After parliamentary deadlock over Brexit in 2019, Corbyn supported a referendum on the withdrawal agreement, remaining personally neutral on the issue. The 2019 general election resulted in a significant loss for Labour, falling to their lowest seat count since 1935. Corbyn resigned as leader in 2020, with Keir Starmer succeeding him and later leading the party to victory in the 2024 election.

Controversially, Corbyn was suspended from the Labour Party in 2020 after stating the extent of antisemitism had been exaggerated. Subsequently, he was barred from standing as a Labour candidate in the 2024 general election, leading him to run as an independent in Islington North, where he was re-elected. He and fellow independent MP Zarah Sultana announced the formation of a new political party in 2025. Throughout his career, Corbyn’s political activities have been consistently rooted in his socialist beliefs and dedication to social justice issues, though often marked by controversy and internal party conflict.

title: Muhammad Qutb
text:
Muhammad Qutb was born in 1919, the younger brother of the prominent Egyptian revolutionary Sayyid Qutb. He pursued studies in English Literature at Cairo University, adding diplomas in psychology and education to his credentials. Following his brother’s execution by the Egyptian government in 1966, Muhammad moved to Saudi Arabia and dedicated himself to promoting and preserving Sayyid’s ideas.

In Egypt, Muhammad Qutb was arrested alongside his brother in 1965, accused of plotting against the government and prominent figures. While Sayyid was executed, Muhammad found refuge in Saudi Arabia, where he became a significant figure in Islamic scholarship. He spent years editing and publishing his brother’s works, ensuring their continued circulation. He also taught Islamic Studies at universities in Mecca and Jeddah, with figures like Osama bin Laden and Ayman al-Zawahiri reportedly among his students. Bin Laden specifically recommended one of Qutb’s books in a 2004 video.

Within the Saudi context, Muhammad Qutb worked to bridge ideological gaps between more radical followers of his brother and the more conservative Muslim community, particularly those within the Muslim Brotherhood. He offered a less stringent interpretation of Sayyid Qutb’s assertion that the modern Muslim world had reverted to a state of *jahiliyya* (pre-Islamic ignorance), specifically denying that Saudi Arabia itself fell into this category. He also publicly opposed *takfir*, the practice of declaring Muslims as non-believers, and sought to reconcile the Brotherhood’s doctrines with prevailing Salafism. He supervised several dissertations, including one by Safar Al-Hawali, whose work contributed to the “sahwa” – an Islamist awakening blending radical Wahhabism and Sayyid Qutb’s ideas.

Qutb’s writings often criticized the state of the Muslim world, attributing its weakness to the failings of Muslims themselves and to external enemies, specifically Christians and Jews. He employed terms like “Crusaders” and “Zionists” to invoke historical conflicts, and believed Jews exerted significant control over Western society and actively sought to undermine Islam through cultural imperialism, perceiving this as a more insidious threat than military invasion. He expressed concern over the influence of Western education and the changing role of women, seeing both as corrupting influences on Islamic values. His arguments frequently drew on anti-Semitic conspiracy theories, including references to *The Protocols of the Elders of Zion*. Interestingly, he also defended traditional Islamic slavery, arguing it was preferable to Western forms of exploitation.

Muhammad Qutb was a prolific author, publishing 36 books on varying subjects, including religion, psychology, and literary criticism. His work, notably *Jahiliyya of the Twentieth Century* and *Islam: The Misunderstood Religion*, had a wide reach within the Arab world and played a significant role in shaping 20th-century Muslim thought. He died in Mecca in 2014 at the age of 94, leaving behind a legacy of scholarship and influence within Islamist circles. He also held editorial control over his brother’s publications, allowing him to shape their dissemination.

title: Daniel Alexander Cameron
text:
Daniel Alexander Cameron was a Canadian politician from Nova Scotia, notable for being among the first legislators from the province to pass away while still in office in the 20th century. Born on December 10, 1870, in Sydney River, Nova Scotia, he was the son of John and Isabella (Macdonald) Cameron. His early education took place at Sydney Academy, and he later pursued legal studies at Dalhousie University, ultimately earning a Bachelor of Laws degree. 

Cameron was officially admitted to the Nova Scotia bar in October 1893, following which he established a law practice in Sydney, beginning in 1894. Beyond his legal career, he was actively involved in local government. He served as a member of the County Council for a considerable period, from 1900 to 1911. During this time, he also held the position of stipendiary magistrate for Sydney from 1905 to 1911, demonstrating a commitment to local judicial administration. In 1911, his responsibilities expanded as he was appointed treasurer and solicitor for the Municipality of Cape Breton.

Cameron’s provincial political career began in 1916 when he successfully ran for a seat in the Nova Scotia House of Assembly, representing the electoral district of Cape Breton. As a member of the Nova Scotia Liberal party, he served one term before being defeated in the 1920 election. However, his political involvement didn’t end there. From 1921 to 1923, he transitioned to the Legislative Council of Nova Scotia and was appointed as a Minister Without Portfolio in the cabinet led by George Henry Murray. He voluntarily resigned from the Legislative Council in 1923, choosing instead to contest and win a seat in the House of Assembly, this time for the electoral district of Victoria County. 

This return to the House of Assembly led to another cabinet position, serving as Provincial Secretary in the government of Ernest Howard Armstrong from 1923 to 1925. Following a period out of office, he resigned a position in 1930 and attempted a transition to federal politics, running as the Liberal candidate for the electoral district of Cape Breton South in the 1930 federal election, but was unsuccessful. He re-entered provincial politics in 1935, winning a seat in the House of Assembly for the combined district of Cape Breton North and Victoria. Unfortunately, his time in office was cut short, as he died while still serving as a Member of the Legislative Assembly in 1937, having served for just under two years of that term.

title: Shin Jea-hwan
text:
Shin Jea-hwan, a South Korean artistic gymnast, was born on March 3, 1998, in Seoul. He completed his education at the Korea National Sport University, graduating in 2020, and later moved to Jecheon in 2021. He considers his teammate, Yang Hak-seon, to be a significant influence.

Shin began his senior international career in 2019, competing at the Zhaoqing World Cup where he earned a silver medal on the vault and placed fourth in the floor exercise. He continued to compete on both vault and floor throughout the 2020 World Cup circuit, achieving gold medals on vault in both Melbourne and Baku. Following the 2019 World Championships, a reallocation of points placed him in a leading position to qualify for the 2020 Summer Olympics; however, the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the remainder of the 2020 series.

To secure his Olympic qualification, Shin participated in the 2021 Doha World Cup, organized as a final qualification event by the International Gymnastics Federation. Although he finished fifth in Doha, behind Japan’s Hidenobu Yonekura, Shin ultimately won the overall World Cup series on a tiebreaker, earning him a place to compete individually at the Olympic Games in Tokyo.

At the 2020 Summer Olympics in Tokyo, Shin successfully qualified for the vault final, achieving a tie with Armenia’s Artur Davtyan with a score of 14.866. He progressed to the final based on a tiebreak, having a higher individual vault score of 15.100 compared to Davtyan’s 15.000. In the vault final itself, Shin once again faced a tie, this time with Denis Ablyazin of the ROC, both gymnasts receiving a score of 14.783. Shin won the gold medal due to his superior individual vault score of 14.833, exceeding Ablyazin’s 14.800. This victory marked South Korea’s second Olympic gold medal in the vault event, following Yang Hak-seon’s win at the 2012 London Olympics.

title: Nuh Omar
text:
Nuh Omar, born June 5, 1988, is a Pakistani-born director and screenwriter with a diverse career spanning film, television, and advertising. He comes from a notable family; his grandfather was entrepreneur Safdar Kureishi, and he is related to Hanif and Maki Kureishi. He spent his early years in Karachi, Pakistan, attending Karachi Grammar School alongside Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, and has both an older sister and a younger brother. His mother was a pioneering sports photojournalist in Pakistan.

Omar’s formal education began with the New York Film Academy’s 2nd Year Film Program in 2006, followed by a Bachelor’s degree in The Science of Film from Full Sail University. Post-graduation, he gained experience through an internship at The Institute and freelance assistant directing work on various short films. He also demonstrated early talent with his short film “We're Americans, Eh?”, which won awards at the 24 Hour Film Festival in 2011.

Returning to Pakistan in 2012, Omar directed short films for Engro Corporation Excellence Awards, including “Mojiza-e-Fun (The Miracle of Art),” which became the last documented project featuring sculptor Shahid Sajjad before his death. He then worked in internet-based projects, ghostwriting commercials, and as a director for the entertainment channel DeVida Lifestyle. A period with the advertising agency IAL Saatchi & Saatchi followed, where he contributed to campaigns for major brands like Head & Shoulders and Pampers. He left this role in 2014 to refocus on filmmaking.

Omar has found success with his long-running YouTube series, “The Fortress of Dorkness,” which he both wrote and directed, producing over 100 episodes with collaborator Christian Villarreal between 2015 and 2019. He is currently developing several new projects, including the historical drama “The Alexandrian” with Mark Davis, and the screenplay “The Porter & The Stone,” a modern adaptation of Oscar Wilde’s “The Happy Prince,” which has garnered multiple awards and high rankings on the Coverfly platform. 

He is also working on TV pilot “A Matter of Time,” co-written with Villarreal, which won Filmmatic’s TV Pilot Awards, and the series “I’m Here”, first conceived as a student project in 2007. Current collaborations with Rustic Lightbulb and producer Severn Lang include the short film “The Universe at Midnight” and the feature “Tijuana Bible.” He is also writing two feature films, “The Imaginary Friend Society” and “Ophelia.” 

Currently based between Karachi and Los Angeles, Omar is a vocal advocate for mental health awareness, openly discussing his own experiences with depression.

title: Jackie Shroff
text:
Jackie Shroff, born Jaikishan Kakubhai Shroff on February 1, 1957, in Mumbai, is a prolific Indian actor who has worked in over 250 films across 13 languages during a career spanning four decades. He is known for his work primarily in Hindi cinema and has received four Filmfare Awards throughout his career. 

Shroff’s beginnings in film were humble, with an uncredited role in *Swami Dada* (1982). He gained instant stardom with Subhash Ghai’s *Hero* (1983), which launched his career. The 1980s and 90s saw him consistently starring in commercially successful films, including *Teri Meherbaniyan*, *Karma*, *Ram Lakhan*, *Tridev*, *Baap Numbri Beta Dus Numbri*, *Khalnayak*, *Rangeela*, and *Border*. He won a Filmfare Award for Best Actor for his performance in *Parinda* (1989) and earned Filmfare Awards for Best Supporting Actor for *1942: A Love Story* and *Rangeela*.

As the 2000s progressed, Shroff transitioned into more supporting and sometimes villainous roles in films like *Refugee*, *Mission Kashmir*, *Devdas*, *Dhoom 3*, and *Sooryavanshi*. He has also expanded his filmography to include work in Punjabi (*Sardar Saab*), Konkani (*Soul Curry*), Tamil (*Bigil*, *Jailer*), and Telugu (*Saaho*) cinema.

Prior to acting, Shroff’s early life involved various attempts at employment, including unsuccessful applications to Taj Hotels and Air India. He worked as a travel agent before being discovered as a model at a bus stop. He attended an acting school run by Aasha K Chandra, where he was introduced to Dev Anand, who offered him his first film role.

Shroff’s family history is marked by financial hardship and migration. His father, a Gujarati merchant, lost the family fortune in the stock market. His mother was a Turkmen who fled Kazakhstan with her family, eventually settling in Mumbai. Shroff himself dropped out of junior college after the 11th standard due to financial constraints.

Beyond acting, Shroff is an environmentalist and owns an organic farm. He is married to Ayesha Dutt, a former model and producer, and they have two children – actor Tiger Shroff and entrepreneur Krishna Shroff. He has also been involved in social activism, supporting causes such as thalassemia awareness, HIV/AIDS awareness, and the prevention of female foeticide, and has funded education and treatment for underprivileged children.

Throughout his career, Shroff has been recognized with numerous awards including multiple Filmfare nominations and wins, as well as accolades for his work in regional cinema such as the Goa State Award for Best Actor for *Soul Curry*. He continues to work in the film industry, with recent and upcoming projects including *Housefull 5*.

title: Jeff Long (athletic director)
text:
Jeff Long, born September 21, 1959, is an American athletic director whose career has spanned multiple universities, most recently at the University of Kansas. He began his administrative career with positions at Eastern Kentucky University, Virginia Tech, the University of Michigan, and the University of Oklahoma before becoming an athletic director at the University of Pittsburgh. He then moved to the University of Arkansas in 2008, succeeding Frank Broyles.

Long earned a bachelor’s degree in economics from Ohio Wesleyan University in 1982, followed by a master’s degree in education from Miami University in 1983. His tenure at Arkansas was marked by both success and controversy, most notably surrounding the hiring and subsequent firing of football coach Bobby Petrino. Long hired Petrino in 2008, but terminated his employment in April 2012 after discovering Petrino had engaged in an extramarital affair with a former volleyball player, Jessica Dorrell. The situation escalated when it was revealed Petrino had attempted to cover up the affair following a motorcycle accident involving Dorrell, and had secretly provided her with a significant financial gift. Long stated Petrino’s deception regarding the accident and the relationship were the primary reasons for his dismissal, alongside concerns about potential legal repercussions. This led to the temporary appointment of John L. Smith and then the hiring of Bret Bielema.

Beyond Arkansas, Long served as the inaugural chairman of the College Football Playoff selection committee in 2013. His time at Arkansas ended in November 2017 when the university leadership determined he had “lost the support” of fans, alumni, and key stakeholders. 

In 2018, Long accepted the position of athletic director at the University of Kansas, aiming to revitalize the football program which hadn’t experienced a winning season since 2008. He initially hired Les Miles, a former coach he knew from their time together at Michigan, to lead the team. However, Miles was later forced to resign following allegations of sexual harassment from his time at LSU. Long publicly stated Miles had assured him there were no issues from his past that could damage the university’s reputation, but later admitted he learned of the allegations through media reports. 

Following Miles’ departure, Long himself left his position at Kansas the very next day. The university stated the decision was mutually agreed upon, but Long revealed he was effectively fired, though allowed to announce his departure as a resignation. He is married to Fanny Gellrich, and they have two daughters.

title: Sandra Pisani
text:
Sandra Pisani, born in Adelaide, South Australia on January 23, 1959, was a highly accomplished Australian field hockey player and contributor to the sport who sadly passed away on April 19, 2022, after a battle with cancer. She represented Australia in 85 international matches, serving as captain of the national team from 1985 to 1987. Her playing career culminated in a gold medal at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, a historic achievement as it marked Australia’s first Olympic gold in women’s field hockey. She had previously competed at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, where the team finished fourth.

Pisani’s involvement with hockey began at the club level with Burnside Hockey Club in 1976, where she was part of eight premiership-winning teams over fifteen years. She was recognised as their Best and Fairest player in 1985 and 1987 and later awarded Life Membership in 2002. She also achieved individual accolades, winning the Association Medal as South Australia’s Best and Fairest Player in both 1985 and 1992. She later played and coached at Port Adelaide for six years, leading them to a premiership in 1993 and earning Hockey SA’s Coach of the Year award. She also coached Woodville Hockey Club’s Premier League team for two years and was jointly named Hockey SA Coach of the Year again in 2012.

Beyond club hockey, Pisani dedicated significant time to state level hockey, serving as a State Selector, State Coach and State Team Manager for South Australia. She represented South Australia’s Southern Suns for twelve years, captaining the team for five of those. Internationally, she debuted for Australia at the 1981 World Cup and participated in numerous tournaments, including the 1983 World Cup where Australia won bronze and the 1987 Champions Trophy where they took silver. 

Following her playing career, Pisani transitioned into a highly successful role as a selector and manager. She was a National Women’s Senior Selector for the Hockeyroos from 1993 to 2000, serving as Head Selector during a period of unprecedented national success. Under her leadership, and with coach Ric Charlesworth, the Hockeyroos secured gold medals at both the 1996 and 2000 Summer Olympics. She continued to contribute to the sport as a National Youth Selector from 2012, and as Team Manager for a development tour in 2014.

Pisani received numerous accolades for her contributions to hockey. She was awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) in 1989, inducted into the South Australian Sport Hall of Fame in 2015, and recognised on the South Australian Sports Institute Hockey Honour Roll. She also received the Australian Sports Medal in 2000 and a Team Sport Australia Award in 2003, acknowledging the significance of the 1988 Olympic gold medal. She was twice a finalist for the Caltex SA Sports Star of the Year Award.

title: Gemma Arterton
text:
Gemma Arterton, born on February 2, 1986, is a British actress who began her career on stage and quickly transitioned to film and television. She first gained recognition with a role in the 2007 comedy *St Trinian's*, following a stage debut in Shakespeare’s *Love's Labour's Lost* at the Globe Theatre. A breakthrough came in 2008 when she was cast as Bond Girl Strawberry Fields in *Quantum of Solace*, a role for which she won an Empire Award for Best Newcomer. 

Throughout her career, Arterton has appeared in a diverse range of films. These include *The Disappearance of Alice Creed* (2009), a controversial role involving graphic scenes which she approached with intense method acting, *Tamara Drewe* (2010), *Clash of the Titans* (2010), *Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time* (2010), and later, *Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters* (2013), *Their Finest* (2016), and *The King’s Man* (2021) where she plays the character of Polly Wilkins. She has also taken on leading roles in films such as *Gemma Bovery* (2015), learning French for the part, and *Summerland* (2020).

Arterton’s theatrical work is also significant. She’s starred in productions of *The Duchess of Malfi* (2014), *Made in Dagenham* (2014), for which she received an Olivier Award nomination and won an Evening Standard Theatre Award, *Nell Gwynn* (2016), earning another Olivier nomination, and *Saint Joan* (2017). She has consistently been praised for her stage presence and skill.

Beyond acting, Arterton founded her own production company, Rebel Park Productions, in 2016. This venture focuses on creating content that features strong female leads both on and off screen, and she has produced several projects, including *The Escape* (2018), for which she received a Harper’s Bazaar Woman of the Year Award, and *Hayley Alien* (2019) with her sister. She has also been a vocal advocate for movements like Time's Up and ERA 50:50, actively campaigning for equality in the film industry.

Born at North Kent Hospital in Gravesend, Arterton experienced a childhood marked by her parent’s divorce and a working-class upbringing. She attended Gravesend Grammar School for Girls before studying Performing Arts at North Kent College and later graduating from the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in 2008. She has spoken openly about her early life and the influence of her family, including her actress sister Hannah Arterton.

Arterton’s personal life has included a marriage to Stefano Catelli, which ended in divorce in 2015, and a subsequent marriage to actor Rory Keenan in 2019. They have a son, born in December 2022. Throughout her career, she has been committed to challenging roles and using her platform to advocate for important social issues.

title: Antonio Leviste
text:
Jose Antonio “Tony” Leviste, born January 16, 1940, is a Filipino politician and businessman with a long and varied career. He comes from a prominent family in Batangas known for their involvement in both business and politics. He served as the Governor of Batangas for eight years, from 1972 to 1980, and during that time held several influential positions within regional and national organizations. These included membership in the Batasang Bayan, chairmanship of the Regional Development Council, Vice President of the League of Governors and City Mayors, and chairmanship of the Program for Forest Ecosystem Management.

Leviste’s governorship was marked by a focus on environmental concerns, specifically a forest ecosystem management program that became a model for reforestation efforts and earned him the “Ten Outstanding Young Men of the Philippines” award for Public Administration. Beyond his role as governor, he held directorships in numerous government agencies, including the People's Homesite and Housing Corporation, the Philippine Ports Authority, the Philippine Aerospace Development Corporation, Semirara Mining Corporation, and the Philippine Tourism Authority. He was a key figure in the real estate sector too, co-founding both the Pasay Board of Realtors and the Philippine Association of Real Estate Boards, and later serving as Chairman of the Philippine Leisure and Retirement Authority. He also maintains a rank of Lt. Commander in the Philippine Navy Reserve Force and currently functions as the Honorary Consul General of the State of Palestine. 

Currently, Leviste is actively involved in tourism, serving as charter president of the Resort Association of the Philippines and co-founder of the Tourism Council of the Philippines. He is also the chief executive officer of the Leviste Group of Companies, a real estate firm specializing in various development projects including housing, subdivisions, condominiums, and resorts.

However, Leviste’s career was significantly impacted by a legal case. In 2009, he was convicted of homicide for the death of his long-time aide, Rafael de las Alas. Leviste admitted responsibility for the shooting, claiming it was an act of self-defense. The Makati Regional Trial Court sentenced him to a prison term of six to twelve years. He served his sentence at the National Bilibid Prison in Muntinlupa and was granted parole after six years, leading to his release on December 6, 2013. 

Prior to his legal troubles, Leviste was married to Senator Loren Legarda, though they were separated before the 2004 election campaign. He also has a daughter, Toni Leviste, who is a decorated equestrian athlete having won medals in the Asian Games.

title: Sami Shalom Chetrit
text:
Sami Shalom Chetrit, born in Morocco in 1960, is a poet, scholar, teacher, and activist currently residing in New York City. He immigrated to Israel with his family at the age of three, growing up in Ashdod. He pursued higher education at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, earning degrees in Literature, Political Science, and a PhD in the latter field. He also holds an MA in International Affairs from Columbia University. He now teaches Hebrew language, literature, and Middle Eastern studies at Queens College in Flushing, New York.

Chetrit is a prominent figure in Mizrahi activism, having co-founded Kedma, an alternative school system focused on equal opportunities and a multicultural curriculum. He was also instrumental in establishing HaKeshet HaDemokratit HaMizrakhit (Mizrahi Democratic Rainbow Coalition), advocating for social justice and cultural freedom. He identifies as an Arab Jew. 

He is a prolific writer, having published numerous articles and books on Israeli society, culture, and politics, alongside a novel, four poetry books, and edited anthologies. His published works include *Intra-Jewish Conflict in Israel: White Jews, Black Jews*, and *Hamaávak HaMizrahi Be’Yisrael* (The Mizrahi Struggle in Israel), which has also been published in Arabic. He has also contributed to various academic journals and literary publications, including *Comparative Literature* and *Journal of Palestine Studies*. 

Beyond writing, Chetrit has produced two documentary films: *The Black Panthers (in Israel) Speak*, focusing on the Israeli protest movement of the 1970s, and *Az’i Ayima (come mother)*, which explores the experiences of first-generation Moroccan women in Israel. Both films have been screened at numerous international film festivals. He also founded a democratic Mizrahi blog dedicated to social justice and peace in Israel-Palestine and has had his poetry translated and published internationally.

title: José Hernández Delgadillo
text:
José Hernández Delgadillo was a Mexican painter and muralist born in 1927 in Tepeapulco, Hidalgo, and died in 2000. He is recognized for continuing the traditions of the Mexican muralism movement into the latter half of the 20th century, creating over 160 murals in both Mexico and the United States. A significant portion of his work, particularly after 1970, contained strong political messages, often making him a controversial figure and contributing to a degree of obscurity despite his artistic merit.

Hernández Delgadillo came from humble beginnings, working various manual labor jobs during his youth. He began his artistic training in Mexico City in 1945, studying painting and architectural drawing, and supporting himself by making portraits. He later attended the Escuela Nacional de Pintura, Escultura y Grabado "La Esmeralda" from 1955-1960, where he was inspired by Pablo O’Higgins to continue the ideals of Mexican muralism. 

Beyond his art, Hernández Delgadillo was deeply involved in politics, believing in grassroots organization to influence the government. He wrote a weekly column for the newspaper *Excélsior* from 1980 to 1983, and ran as a candidate for the Partido Mexicano de Trabajadores in 1985. He was also considered as a presidential candidate for the PRD in 1987, ultimately supporting Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas and creating murals for his campaign.

His artistic career began with an exhibition in 1954 and gained international recognition with awards at biennials in Mexico and Paris in 1961, leading to a French government grant that allowed him to exhibit throughout France and Spain. While he achieved success with easel paintings, he became most known for his mural work, beginning with the Escuela Primaria Belisario Dominguez in 1959. He served as director of arte for the Centro Residencial Morelos housing project in 1969, creating a large-scale mural complex there.  He often collaborated with students on these murals, utilizing simple colors and incorporating them as educational and political events. He began creating explicitly political murals in 1973, and later expanded his work to the United States in 1981, with commissions in California.

Despite his prolific output, many of Hernández Delgadillo’s murals have fallen into disrepair or been deliberately destroyed due to their political content. Efforts to restore his work began in 2013 in Pachuca, Hidalgo, his home state, which has increasingly focused on recognizing and preserving his legacy.  He also pursued sculpture and illustrated medical texts. 

Hernández Delgadillo’s artistry aligned with the second state of Mexican muralism, inspired by artists like Diego Rivera, José Clemente Orozco, and David Alfaro Siqueiros. His work, often expressionistic, frequently denounced violence and championed social justice.  He was a member of the Salón de la Plástica Mexicana, and after his death, the SPM established a prize in his name and held a retrospective of his work in 2009. While his work was often overlooked by the mainstream art world due to its challenging political themes, a biography of his life and work was published in 2008, signaling a growing effort to recognize his contributions to Mexican art.

title: Chi Pu
text:
Nguyễn Thùy Chi, better known as Chi Pu, was born in Hanoi, Vietnam on June 14, 1993. Her father is a member of the Vietnamese military and her mother is an English teacher; she also has an older sister working in banking. Chi Pu first gained recognition as a teen idol after placing in the Top 20 of Miss Teen Vietnam 2009. By November 2016, she had the most followers on Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube of any Vietnamese actress, according to Socialbaker.

Her acting career began in 2013 with leading roles in the television dramas *Waterdrop* and *Happy Dream*, both broadcast nationally. She also joined the cast of the popular series *5S Online* that same year.  Chi Pu expanded into filmmaking, producing and starring in the short film *Under One Sky*, which won a Golden Kite Award. She continued her film work with *Thần tượng (The Talent)*, which also garnered six Golden Kite Awards, and appeared in the horror films *Chung cư ma (Hush)* and *Hương Ga (Rise)*, the latter winning Best Vietnamese Film at the San Francisco International New Concept Film Festival in 2016. She starred in further television dramas including *Vẫn có em bên đời (You’re Always by my Side)*, for which she won an HTV Award, *Yêu (Love)*, which grossed over half a million USD in its first three days, and hosted shows like *Dancing with the Stars Kids Vietnam* and *The Voice Kids Vietnam*.

Beyond acting and hosting, Chi Pu also ventured into music, officially launching her singing career in 2017. She has released numerous singles, including “Fighting Fighting,” “Stay with me,” and “Ngày bồng bềnh,” and extended plays. In 2023, she competed on the Chinese reality show *Sisters Who Make Waves*, achieving the sixth-highest score in the final episode and winning both the "Fan Favorite" and "Overcoming Challenges" awards. This success led to her inclusion in the 11-member girl group formed after the show.

Chi Pu’s accomplishments have been recognized through various awards, including being named Upcoming Female Actress at the ELLE Style Awards in 2015 and inclusion in Forbes Asia Pacific’s list of 100 most influential digital stars in 2020. She’s a brand ambassador for several companies, including Yamaha Janus and Dove Vietnam, and was the first Vietnamese artist to collaborate with Google on an advertising campaign.  

She actively participates in philanthropic work, advocating for causes such as flood relief, funding heart surgeries for children, and animal welfare, and encouraging the end of rhino horn consumption. She also has launched fashion collections in collaboration with TheBlueTshirt and PUSW.

title: Neil Sinclair
text:
Neil Sinclair, born February 23, 1974, was a professional boxer from Northern Ireland who competed between 1995 and 2010. His career encompassed both significant amateur achievements and a decade and a half in the professional ranks, culminating in a challenge for a world title. 

Sinclair began his boxing journey as an amateur, representing Ireland with success. In 1992, he earned a bronze medal at the Junior World Championships held in Montreal. He continued to demonstrate his talent, notably winning a gold medal representing Northern Ireland at the 1994 Commonwealth Games in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. These early accomplishments laid the foundation for his professional career.

Sinclair transitioned to professional boxing in April 1995, making his debut at the Ulster Hall in Belfast. He secured a knockout victory over Marty Duke in his first fight, appearing on a card that also featured Darren Corbett and marked the final professional bout for Damien Denny. He continued to build his professional record over the following years. 

A period of relative inactivity saw Sinclair announce his retirement in June 2007. However, his passion for the sport led to a swift return to the ring within a couple of months. He continued to fight, and in May 2009, achieved a victory on home soil at the Odyssey Arena in Belfast, winning the Irish light-middleweight title with a stoppage against Henry Coyle.

Throughout his professional career, Sinclair also held the British welterweight title from 2001 to 2003, establishing himself as a prominent fighter at the national level. He also challenged for the EBU European Union title once in 2008. The peak of his professional career came in 2010 when he received the opportunity to compete for the WBO welterweight title, though the article does not specify the outcome of this fight. 

Details of his complete professional boxing record can be found on BoxRec, although registration is required to access it. Further information regarding his participation in the Commonwealth Games is archived on the Commonwealth Games Federation website.

title: Paul Anka
text:
Paul Anka, born in Ottawa, Ontario in 1941, is a Canadian and American singer, songwriter, and actor with a career spanning decades. He achieved early fame with the 1957 hit “Diana,” which topped charts in both Canada and the United States and remains one of the best-selling singles by a Canadian artist. He followed this success with a string of Top 20 hits in 1958, including “It’s Time to Cry” and “(All of a Sudden) My Heart Sings”, quickly becoming a teen idol. He also wrote “It Doesn’t Matter Anymore”, which Buddy Holly recorded shortly before his death, with Anka dedicating royalties from the song to Holly’s family.

Beyond performing, Anka demonstrated songwriting talent, composing the theme for *The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson* and the English lyrics to “My Way,” originally a French song that became a signature piece for Frank Sinatra and has been covered extensively by artists like Elvis Presley. He also penned “She’s a Lady” for Tom Jones and contributed to the soundtrack of *The Longest Day*, even appearing in a cameo role in the film.

While enjoying continued success, Anka experienced a chart comeback in the 1970s with the 1974 hit "(You're) Having My Baby," a duet with Odia Coates that broadened his appeal. This led to further collaborations with Coates, producing three more Top 20 duets. He also recorded the popular jingle for Kodak, “Times of Your Life,” which was later released as a full song and reached the Top 10. 

Anka’s career saw further peaks in the 1990s with the album *A Body of Work*, featuring collaborations with artists such as Celine Dion and Kenny G. In 2005, his album *Rock Swings*, featuring big-band arrangements of contemporary rock songs, earned him renewed recognition, including a star on Canada’s Walk of Fame. He also became involved in later collaborations with Michael Jackson, receiving co-writing credit and royalties for songs like "This Is It," "Love Never Felt So Good," and "Don't Matter to Me," released posthumously.

Anka’s international appeal is notable, particularly in Italy where “Ogni giorno” reached number one in 1962, and in Finland, where he has performed multiple times. He also attempted to gain traction in France and Japan, with some success. He has also performed in Israel and refused to participate in boycott attempts against the country.

Alongside his musical career, Anka has acted in numerous films and television shows, including *The Longest Day*, *Girls Town*, and guest appearances on *That '70s Show* and *Gilmore Girls*. He was also the subject of a National Film Board of Canada documentary, *Lonely Boy*. He even appeared as himself on *The Simpsons* and *American Idol*, and competed on *The Masked Singer* as “Broccoli”. 

Throughout his life, Anka has been recognized for his contributions, including being named an Officer of the Order of Canada. He has also explored business ventures, co-founding the holographic tech startup ARHT Media. He has been married four times and has children, including a daughter who is married to actor Jason Bateman.

title: Joseph Kony
text:
Joseph Kony was born in Uganda in 1961 and rose to infamy as the founder and leader of the Lord’s Resistance Army (LRA), a group designated as terrorist by multiple international bodies. Initially an altar boy, Kony became involved in rebellion following the Ugandan Civil War, eventually forming the LRA in 1987 with the aim of establishing a Christian theocratic state based on dominion theology. His rise to prominence followed the overthrow of Acholi President Tito Okello by Yoweri Museveni, and the subsequent violence inflicted by Museveni’s forces.

Kony’s LRA became notorious for its brutal tactics, most prominently the mass abduction of children. An estimated 66,000 children were forcibly recruited as soldiers and sex slaves, and two million people were displaced between 1986 and 2009 due to LRA activities. The group operated for years within Uganda before being driven out and relocating to South Sudan, and later spreading its operations into the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Central African Republic, and Sudan. 

In 2005, the International Criminal Court (ICC) indicted Kony on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity. Despite an Interpol Red Notice issued in 2006, he has remained at large. Attempts at peace talks in 2006, known as the Juba peace talks, failed to secure his surrender. By 2013, reports indicated Kony was in poor health, and there were even claims of negotiations for his surrender through the President of the Central African Republic. 

Over time, the LRA’s strength diminished, falling from an estimated 3,000 fighters to around 100 by 2017. This decline led both the United States and Uganda to end their active pursuit of Kony, believing the LRA no longer posed a significant threat. Kony's ideology is a complex mix of Acholi nationalism, Christian fundamentalism, and mysticism; he claims to be a spirit medium guided by multiple spirits. He advocates for strict adherence to the Ten Commandments, justifying his actions as divinely ordained.

A key figure within the LRA, Dominic Ongwen, surrendered in 2015, a significant blow to the organization. Ongwen was later convicted by the ICC of crimes against humanity and war crimes in 2021. Despite ongoing efforts, Kony remained elusive. As of 2022, reports place him hiding in the Darfur region of Sudan, allegedly continuing to issue orders to remaining fighters. More recently, in April 2024, reports indicated he fled a camp in the Central African Republic after an attack by the Wagner Group, seeking refuge in Sudan. While once a major regional threat, Kony’s influence has significantly waned, though he remains a fugitive from international justice.

title: Dascha Polanco
text:
Dascha Polanco, born on December 3, 1982, is a Dominican actress best known for her work in television and film. She was born in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, and immigrated to the United States as a child, growing up in both Sunset Park, Brooklyn, and Miami. She is the eldest of three children, with a brother and a sister. Her father worked as a mechanic and her mother as a cosmetologist.

Despite harboring a lifelong ambition to become an actress, Polanco initially pursued higher education, earning a bachelor’s degree in psychology from Hunter College. She was the first in her family to attend college. Following her degree, she began a career in healthcare, intending to become a nurse, and was employed in hospital administration at Montefiore Medical Center in the Bronx while also continuing her nursing studies. It was during this time that she decided to revisit her dream of acting, enrolling at BIH Studios in New York.

Her early acting work included small roles in the television series *Unforgettable* and *NYC 22*. A significant turning point came in 2012 when she was cast as Dayanara "Daya" Diaz in the Netflix series *Orange Is the New Black*. Initially a recurring role, she was promoted to series regular beginning with the show’s third season in 2015. 

Beyond *Orange Is the New Black*, Polanco has appeared in a variety of projects. She had roles in the independent film *Gimme Shelter* and the comedy films *The Cobbler* and *Joy*, as well as *The Perfect Match*. In 2018, she took on recurring roles in *The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story* and, in 2019, in the Netflix series *Russian Doll* and *When They See Us*. 

More recently, Polanco portrayed Cuca, a lead character in the 2021 film *In the Heights*. She also lent her voice to the animated series *Karma's World* from 2021 to 2022, voicing the character of Ms. Camilla Torres. Her upcoming work includes a starring role as Michelle Borgas in the 2025 Lifetime film *Terror Comes Knocking: The Marcela Borgas Story*.

Polanco is a mother to two children, a daughter and a son. Notably, her daughter appeared as a younger version of her character, Daya, in the fifth season of *Orange Is the New Black*.

title: Alfred Hitchcock
text:
Alfred Hitchcock was a highly influential English film director, born in 1899 and passing away in 1980, who directed over 50 feature films across six decades. He became widely known as the "Master of Suspense," achieving celebrity status through his films, frequent cameo appearances within them, interviews, and his work hosting and producing the television series *Alfred Hitchcock Presents*. Despite receiving 46 Academy Award nominations and winning six, he was never awarded Best Director, though he was nominated five times.

Hitchcock began his film career in 1919 as a title card designer after working as a technical clerk and copywriter. His directorial debut came with the 1925 British-German silent film *The Pleasure Garden*. He gained significant recognition with *The Lodger: A Story of the London Fog* (1927), a film that helped define the thriller genre, and *Blackmail* (1929), which was Britain’s first “talkie.” His films *The 39 Steps* (1935) and *The Lady Vanishes* (1938) are considered among the best British films of the 20th century. In 1939, producer David O. Selznick brought him to Hollywood, where he directed a series of successful films including *Rebecca* (1940), which won the Academy Award for Best Picture, *Foreign Correspondent* (1940), *Suspicion* (1941), *Shadow of a Doubt* (1943), *Notorious* (1946), *Lifeboat* (1944), *Spellbound* (1945), *Rear Window* (1954), and *Psycho* (1960), the latter earning him another Oscar nomination. 

Throughout his career, Hitchcock frequently collaborated with prominent actors, directing Cary Grant in four films, James Stewart in four, Ingrid Bergman in three, and a consecutive run of three with Grace Kelly. He became an American citizen in 1955. His filmography includes other notable works such as *Rope* (1948), *Strangers on a Train* (1951), *Dial M for Murder* (1954), *To Catch a Thief* (1955), *The Birds* (1963), *Marnie* (1964) and *Frenzy* (1972). In 2012, his film *Vertigo* was named the greatest film ever made by the British Film Institute, displacing *Citizen Kane*. As of 2021, nine of his films are preserved in the United States National Film Registry, including his personal favorite, *Shadow of a Doubt*.

Hitchcock’s early life was marked by a disciplined upbringing, the son of a greengrocer. He attended a series of schools, including Jesuit colleges where he developed a sense of fear and was often punished with a “ferula”. He initially studied engineering, but after his father’s death he took a job at the Henley Telegraph and Cable Company, where he began to explore his interest in art and advertising. He entered the film industry through Famous Players–Lasky, beginning as a title card designer and quickly taking on various roles including art direction and scriptwriting. He worked with Gainsborough Pictures and spent time filming in Germany, learning from filmmakers like F. W. Murnau.  He actively promoted himself as a director, believing the director’s name should be synonymous with quality, and gained recognition with early successes like *The Ring* before establishing himself as a master of suspense with *The Lodger*.

title: Peter Gallagher
text:
Peter Gallagher is an American actor born in New York City on August 19, 1955. He comes from an Irish Catholic background and was raised in Armonk, New York, as the youngest of three children. His mother was a bacteriologist, and his father worked in advertising. He attended Tufts University, where he participated in theater productions like Stephen Sondheim’s *Company* and sang with the a cappella group the Beelzebubs, and later studied acting at the William Esper Studio and with Mira Rostova.

Gallagher began his acting career on Broadway, appearing alongside Glenn Close in *The Real Thing*, and made his film debut in *The Idolmaker*. He first gained recognition for his role in Steven Soderbergh’s *sex, lies, and videotape* in 1989. He has since appeared in a wide range of films including *Bob Roberts*, *The Player*, *Short Cuts*, *While You Were Sleeping*, *American Beauty*, *Mr. Deeds*, and *Palm Springs*. 

He is perhaps most widely known for his portrayal of Sandy Cohen, a public defender and corporate lawyer, in the television series *The O.C.*, which aired from 2003 to 2007.  Inspired by this role, he established "The Sandy Cohen Awards," an annual scholarship for students at UC Berkeley pursuing public defender careers. Gallagher has also had recurring roles in several other television shows, including *Law & Order: Special Victims Unit*, *Californication*, *Grace & Frankie*, and *Covert Affairs*.  More recently, he appeared in *Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist* and *Grey's Anatomy*.

Beyond acting, Gallagher also has musical interests. He released an album, *7 Days in Memphis*, in 2005, which included a recording of “Don't Give Up On Me” that was featured on *The O.C.* He also created a music video with his *O.C.* co-star Kelly Rowan for his single “Still I Long For Your Kiss.” 

Gallagher has been recognized for his contributions to the entertainment industry with awards from Tufts University, including the P.T. Barnum Award in 2005 and the "Light on the Hill" award in 2007. He has returned to Broadway several times, most recently starring in *On the Twentieth Century* in 2015, and is scheduled to appear in a new play, *Left on Tenth*, in 2024. He is married to Paula Harwood and has two children, James and Kathryn, with Kathryn also pursuing a career as an actress and singer.

title: Amelia Earhart
text:
Amelia Mary Earhart, born in Atchison, Kansas in 1897, was a pioneering American aviator who captivated the world with her ambition and ultimately, her mysterious disappearance. She rose to prominence in the late 1920s and 1930s, not only as a record-breaking pilot but also as a symbol of women’s rights and a celebrity who embraced the burgeoning culture of fame. Earhart’s life was marked by a spirit of adventure, beginning in childhood with explorations and a fascination with unconventional pursuits. 

Her initial foray into aviation came as a passenger in 1920, sparking an immediate passion for flying. She diligently pursued lessons, working various jobs to fund her training with Neta Snook, and eventually purchased her own aircraft, a Kinner Airster she affectionately called “The Canary.”  Earhart quickly established herself as a skilled pilot, setting a world record for female pilots in 1922 by reaching an altitude of 14,000 feet. She received her pilot’s license in 1923, becoming the 16th woman in the United States to do so. 

A pivotal moment came in 1928 when she became the first female passenger to cross the Atlantic by airplane, catapulting her to international fame. This was followed by the groundbreaking achievement in 1932 of becoming the first woman to fly solo non-stop across the Atlantic Ocean, earning her the Distinguished Flying Cross. Beyond her flying accomplishments, Earhart was a prolific writer, publishing best-selling books detailing her experiences, and actively promoted commercial air travel.  She also co-founded the Ninety-Nines, an international organization dedicated to the advancement of female pilots. 

Earhart’s commitment extended beyond aviation; she was a member of the National Woman’s Party and a vocal supporter of the Equal Rights Amendment. Her influence was often compared to that of Charles Lindbergh and First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt, both admired figures who championed progress and inspired others. In 1935, she accepted a position at Purdue University, serving as a faculty member and career counselor for female students in aeronautical engineering.

In 1937, Earhart embarked on her most ambitious endeavor: a circumnavigational flight around the world in a Lockheed Model 10-E Electra.  She and her navigator, Fred Noonan, disappeared over the Pacific Ocean near Howland Island, their last confirmed sighting being in Lae, New Guinea. It is widely believed they ran out of fuel and crashed into the ocean. Despite extensive searches, the aircraft was never found, fueling countless theories and speculation about their fate.  Earhart was officially declared dead in 1939, at the age of 41. 

Her legacy endures through numerous memorials – including a US airmail stamp, airports, museums, and even a minor planet named in her honor – and through the continued fascination with her life and disappearance. She was posthumously inducted into both the National Aviation Hall of Fame and the National Women's Hall of Fame, solidifying her place as an iconic figure in aviation history and a lasting inspiration for generations.

title: Blair Tugman

title: Tom Coburn
text:
Thomas Allen Coburn, born in 1948 and passing away in 2020, was a physician and politician who served as a United States Senator for Oklahoma from 2005 to 2015, and previously as a U.S. Representative from 1995 to 2001. He initially practiced as an obstetrician in Muskogee, Oklahoma, delivering over 4,000 babies and treating more than 15,000 patients. Elected to the House of Representatives during the 1994 Republican Revolution, he kept a promise to serve no more than three terms, stepping down in 2001. He returned to politics in 2004 with a successful Senate run, again adhering to a self-imposed two-term limit and announcing his resignation in 2014 due to a recurrence of prostate cancer, effective at the end of his term.

Coburn was a staunch fiscal and social conservative, known for his opposition to government spending, particularly what he considered wasteful “pork barrel” projects, and was a strong opponent of abortion. He championed term limits, gun rights, and the death penalty, while opposing same-sex marriage and embryonic stem cell research. His frequent use of procedural tactics to block legislation led Democrats to nickname him “Dr. No.” After leaving Congress, he continued his policy work as a senior fellow at the Manhattan Institute, focusing on FDA reform, and as a senior advisor advocating for a constitutional convention with Citizens for Self-Governance.

Born in Wyoming, Coburn graduated from Oklahoma State University with a degree in accounting and worked in management at his family’s optical business, significantly expanding its operations. Following a battle with melanoma, he pursued a medical degree, graduating from the University of Oklahoma Medical School. He was active in his church, serving as a deacon. A controversial event during his medical career involved a sterilization procedure performed on a 20-year-old patient during an emergency surgery; a lawsuit alleging lack of consent was dismissed without finding fault, and a claim of Medicaid fraud was also dropped.

In the House, representing a historically Democratic district, Coburn distinguished himself as a conservative voice, often clashing with Speaker Newt Gingrich over what he perceived as a move toward the political center. He authored legislation expanding healthcare options for seniors, protecting rural healthcare access, and allowing access to cheaper medications. He also played a role in welfare reform and served as co-chair of the Presidential Advisory Council on HIV/AIDS. A notable incident involved criticism for his comments regarding the television broadcast of *Schindler's List*, for which he later apologized. 

As a Senator, Coburn continued his conservative stance, frequently employing the Senate hold to delay votes on legislation he opposed. This included bills relating to veterans’ benefits, aid to Uganda, honoring Rachel Carson, and land management issues. He was also connected to a scandal involving Senator John Ensign and a religious organization called "The Family," where he attempted to mediate the situation prior to the public revelation of an extramarital affair.

title: Chris John (boxer)
text:
Yohannes Christian “Chris” John, born in Banjarnegara, Indonesia in 1979, was a professional boxer who enjoyed a remarkably long and successful career from 1998 to 2013. He became the fourth Indonesian boxer to win a world title, and held the World Boxing Association (WBA) featherweight title from 2004 until his retirement, initially the standard version and then the “Super” version from 2009. His nearly decade-long reign is the second-longest in the division’s history, surpassed only by Johnny Kilbane. Throughout his championship run, John successfully defended his title a total of 16 times, second only to Eusebio Pedroza in featherweight history.

Boxing was ingrained in John’s life from a young age, as his father, Johan Tjahjadi (originally Tjia Foek Sem), was a former amateur boxer of Chinese descent. He began training his sons, Chris and Adrian, at the age of five, sharing stories of his own boxing experiences. Chris excelled, becoming an amateur champion in Banjarnegara before turning professional in 1997, initially fighting under the nickname “Thin Man” before adopting “The Dragon.”

Early in his professional career, John gained recognition after knocking out national featherweight champion Muhammad Afaridzi in a 12-round bout, despite being knocked down twice in the first round. He continued to rise through the ranks, eventually capturing the PABA Featherweight title and earning a shot at the WBA featherweight title against Oscar León in 2003. He won the title by split decision, becoming a world champion. 

John’s reign saw notable victories against fighters like Derrick Gainer, whom he defeated by unanimous decision after a first-round knockdown, and Juan Manuel Márquez, also by unanimous decision, a result Márquez disputed. He also had a technical draw against Jose Rojas due to an accidental head clash. He fought Hiroyuki Enoki, winning by unanimous decision in a sold-out arena in Tokyo, and faced Rocky Juarez twice, with the first fight ending in a controversial draw and the rematch resulting in a unanimous decision win for John. He also secured victories over Daud Yordan, Shoji Kimura, and Chonlatarn Piriyapinyo, defending his title multiple times across Indonesia, Japan, and Singapore. 

John's career ended with a controversial technical draw against Satoshi Hosono, where a headbutt caused severe bleeding, and ultimately a loss to Simpiwe Vetyeka in 2013, marking his first professional defeat. He retired on his stool after six rounds, relinquishing his WBA Super World featherweight title. Following his retirement, John transitioned to business and motivational speaking, also appearing in television commercials.

Throughout his boxing journey, John was trained by his father until 1997, then by Sutan Rambing until 2004, and finally by Craig Christian from 2005 until his retirement. His accomplishments were recognized with the WBA’s Fighter of the Decade award for the 2000s. Before focusing solely on boxing, John was also a successful wushu athlete, earning medals at the Southeast Asian Games and Indonesian national championships.

title: Felipe (footballer, born 1977)
text:
Felipe Jorge Loureiro, known simply as Felipe, is a Brazilian football personality currently serving as the technical director of Vasco da Gama, having previously had a lengthy career as a player and is now transitioning into coaching. Born in Rio de Janeiro on September 2nd, 1977, he was a left-footed midfielder and left-back renowned for his playmaking abilities, earning him the nickname “Maestro.” He was known for his excellent ball control, dribbling, and vision in orchestrating attacks and delivering precise passes.

Felipe’s football journey began with Vasco da Gama, joining their futsal team at age six and transitioning to field football in 1990. He made his senior debut for Vasco in 1996 and quickly became a key player, contributing to a successful period for the club. In 1999, he was sold to Roma for US$20 million, though the manager declined to use him, eventually leading to a compensation payment of US$2 million to Vasco in 2002. 

His career saw spells with several clubs including Palmeiras, Atlético Mineiro, Galatasaray, Flamengo, and Fluminense. While at Flamengo in 2004, he won the Campeonato Carioca but the club narrowly avoided relegation. His time at Fluminense was hampered by injuries and a suspension for assaulting an opponent, leading to the rescission of his contract. He then spent five seasons with Al Sadd in Qatar, achieving multiple team and individual accolades. He returned to Vasco da Gama in 2010 for a second spell, but left in 2012 after disagreements with the director, before further returns to Fluminense and then announcing his retirement in 2014 at the age of 36.

Internationally, Felipe represented Brazil, earning his first cap in 1998. He participated in the 2004 Copa América, winning the competition with the national team. 

Since retiring, Felipe has moved into coaching. He began as head coach of Tigres do Brasil in 2016, followed by roles as a football coordinator at Ponte Preta and then as head coach of Bangu and Confiança. He’s also had multiple spells at Bangu, and a short stint at Volta Redonda, before returning to Vasco da Gama in 2024 as technical director, and twice acting as interim head coach. 

Throughout his career, Felipe accumulated a significant number of honors.
