With Vasco da Gama, he won the Campeonato Brasileiro Série A, Copa do Brasil, Copa Libertadores, Campeonato Carioca, Torneio Rio – São Paulo and Copa Mercosur. He also won the Campeonato Carioca with Flamengo and Fluminense, and a wealth of titles with Al Sadd in Qatar including the Qatar Stars League and various cup competitions. He was individually recognized with awards such as Copa do Brasil Player of the Year and Campeonato Carioca Player of the Year in 2004.

title: Mamunul Islam
text:
Mamunul Islam, born December 12, 1988, is a Bangladeshi footballer who primarily plays as a midfielder. He had a lengthy career with both club and national team, representing Bangladesh from 2009 to 2020, and serving as captain of the national team from 2013 until his international retirement in 2020. Throughout his career, he has secured five league titles playing for multiple clubs.

Mamunul began his professional journey with Brothers Union in 2005, winning both the Dhaka Premier Division League and the Federation Cup that year. He then moved to Abahani Limited Dhaka in the 2008-09 season, promptly winning the Bangladesh Premier League. A subsequent transfer took him to Mohammedan SC, where he achieved success by winning the Federation Cup and Super Cup. 

He then joined Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club in 2010-11, adding another league title to his collection. After a season with Muktijoddha Sangsad KC, he moved to Sheikh Russel KC in 2012-13, where he won the league, the Federation Cup and the Independence Cup. A return to Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club in 2013-14 yielded two more league titles, with Mamunul captaining the team to victory in the 2013-14 season. 

In a notable period, he was loaned to Indian Super League side Atlético de Kolkata for the inaugural season, becoming the only South Asian player outside of India to participate. He also impressed in the IFA Shield with Sheikh Jamal Dhanmondi Club, leading them to the final.  He later joined Chittagong Abahani Limited for a record transfer fee of 65 lakh taka, captaining the team in his first season before returning to Abahani Limited Dhaka in 2018, contributing his experience to the team. He rejoined Mohammedan SC in 2021 and later played for Rahmatganj MFS in 2022.

Beyond club success, Mamunul also achieved international recognition, winning a gold medal with the Bangladesh U-23 team at the 2010 South Asian Games. His career has been marked by consistent performance and leadership, making him a prominent figure in Bangladeshi football.

title: Grayston Burgess
text:
Grayston Burgess, born in Cheriton, Kent on April 7, 1932, and passing away on March 6, 2019, was a noted English countertenor and conductor. His musical journey began early in life as a chorister at Canterbury Cathedral during the Second World War. He continued his musical education at Cheltenham College, ultimately earning a choral scholarship to King’s College, Cambridge, where he sang under the direction of Boris Ord. 

Burgess’s professional career encompassed both performance and ensemble leadership. He was a member of the Purcell Singers and notably founded the Purcell Consort of Voices in 1963, a group with which he would later record. He also collaborated with international ensembles, performing with the Studio der frühen Musik and the Musica Reservata Ensemble, led by Michael Morrow and John Beckett. As a countertenor soloist, he was involved in premiering new works, including Michael Tippett’s “Songs for Ariel”. His work as a performer is documented in recordings such as a Dowland LP featuring him as a soloist. 

Later in life, Burgess relocated to rural Herefordshire in the 1980s and transitioned towards teaching. He initially taught singing at Ellerslie School in Malvern, and after its closure, continued his teaching at Malvern College. Among his students was Wendy Nieper, a former member of the Swingle Singers.

Even after a long and distinguished career, Burgess remained actively involved in music. In 2000, he accepted an invitation to establish and direct a community choir to commemorate the new millennium. This initial project evolved into Choir 2000, becoming a lasting musical presence in the area and a source of both inspiration and fulfillment for Burgess himself. 

In 2017, the Daily Telegraph recognized him as a ‘veteran conductor and choir director’ in an article concerning women's roles in British cathedral choirs, published on International Women's Day. Interestingly, the article did not acknowledge his connection, if any, to the Campaign for the Traditional Cathedral Choir, a group known for its opposition to the inclusion of women and girls in cathedral and church choirs. Burgess’s conducting work is represented in recordings such as "Music of Albert: Prince of Saxe, Coburg und Gotha" with the Purcell Consort of Voices.

title: Umika Kawashima
text:
Umika Kawashima, born on March 3, 1994, is a Japanese performer active as an actress, voice actress, and singer. She is perhaps best known as a former member of the girl group 9nine, with whom she spent nine and a half years before graduating in 2016 to concentrate on her acting work. Her musical efforts include the single “Maji de Koi Suru 5 Byō Mae/Ichigo Iro no Kimochi”, featured on the soundtrack for *Watashi no Yasashikunai Senpai*, which achieved a ranking of #46 on the Oricon chart.

Kawashima’s career began in 2006, with appearances in a variety of Japanese television dramas and films. She was initially scouted by Lespros Entertainment while in the 6th grade, after being discovered in Shibuya. She has expressed admiration for actresses Aoi Miyazaki, Yui Aragaki, and Kou Shibasaki, and has voiced a desire to collaborate with singer Masaharu Fukuyama. 

In 2016, Kawashima completed her education, graduating from Meiji University’s Faculty of Arts and Letters with a degree in psychology. Shortly before her graduation, she was announced as a regular cast member on the television program *ZIP!*, alongside Masu Taichi, expressing her intention to contribute to an exciting and smooth-running show. She took on her first leading role as a voice actress in 2017 with the anime series *Nana Maru San Batsu*. 

Beyond live-action and anime roles, Kawashima has also worked in dubbing, providing the Japanese voice for Mavis Dracula in all four *Hotel Transylvania* films: *Hotel Transylvania*, *Hotel Transylvania 2*, *Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation*, and *Hotel Transylvania: Transformania*. 

Throughout her career, Kawashima has received several awards recognizing her talent. She won the Best Newcomer Award at the 2nd Tokyo Drama Awards in 2009. In 2010, she was honored with a Special Prize at the 23rd Japan Best Dressed Eyes Awards. She also received recognition in 2013, winning in the teens section of the 24th Best Jewery Dresser in Japan awards.

On December 23, 2024, Kawashima announced her marriage to Olympic swimmer Katsumi Nakamura. Information about her can be found on her official blog, her agency’s profile, Anime News Network’s encyclopedia, and IMDb.

title: David Oyite-Ojok
text:
David Oyite Ojok was a Ugandan military officer born in Lira District in 1940, who played a pivotal role in Ugandan history, particularly during and after the regime of Idi Amin. He joined the Uganda Army in 1963, progressing through the ranks and becoming a key figure within the military during Milton Obote’s first presidency. He was considered a trusted advisor to Obote, serving as Assistant Military Secretary and undergoing training in Great Britain.

When Idi Amin seized power in 1971, Oyite Ojok was forced into exile in Tanzania, where he joined Obote’s guerrilla forces. He gained a reputation for daring raids into Uganda, even becoming the subject of a bounty placed on his head by Amin. He commanded Obote’s naval forces on Lake Victoria, supporting the rebel effort through smuggling operations. During the Uganda–Tanzania War, beginning in 1978, Oyite Ojok emerged as a crucial leader in the coalition that overthrew Amin, initially commanding Obote’s private army, Kikosi Maalum, and later becoming head of a battalion within the Uganda National Liberation Army (UNLA). His tactical abilities were widely recognized, with some crediting him with key victories like those at Lukaya and the fall of Kampala.

Following Amin’s removal, Oyite Ojok became a member of the powerful Military Commission that governed Uganda. He amassed considerable wealth, particularly through coffee exports, and remained a staunch supporter of Obote’s return to power. He actively worked to consolidate power for Obote and the Uganda Peoples Congress, ensuring the UNLA was dominated by Northerners, particularly from his own Lango ethnic group. This created tensions with Southern groups, especially the Buganda, who opposed Obote’s return. He was instrumental in the removal of President Yusuf Lule and, later, Godfrey Binaisa, consolidating the Military Commission's control. 

Oyite Ojok’s influence peaked in 1980 when he helped pave the way for Obote’s second presidency through a contested election. As Army Chief of Staff, he led the brutal suppression of guerrilla movements led by Yoweri Museveni and Andrew Kayiira, employing harsh tactics that resulted in significant civilian casualties, particularly in the Luwero Triangle, and widespread fear in Kampala through practices like “Panda Gari”. 

Despite initial successes against the guerrillas, tensions arose within the army, particularly between the Lango and Acholi ethnic groups, and between Oyite Ojok and Obote himself over corruption.  Oyite Ojok died in a helicopter crash in December 1983. While the NRA claimed responsibility, the government attributed the crash to technical failure, sparking conspiracy theories about Obote’s involvement. His death and the subsequent appointment of a Lango officer over a more senior Acholi officer contributed to the conditions that led to Obote's overthrow in 1985. Despite his controversial role, Oyite Ojok has since been recognized as a national hero by the government of Yoweri Museveni.

title: Richard Kuklinski
text:
Richard Kuklinski, nicknamed “the Iceman,” was a New Jersey criminal who engaged in burglary and at least five confirmed murders for financial gain between 1980 and 1984. He lived a double life, maintaining a seemingly normal family life in Dumont, New Jersey, while secretly committing violent crimes. His family claimed to be unaware of his activities. Kuklinski typically lured victims with promises of profitable business deals, then murdered them and stole their money, and also killed associates who posed a threat of informing on him. 

Born in Jersey City in 1935 to Polish and Irish-American parents, Kuklinski experienced a violent and unstable childhood. His father was a physically abusive alcoholic, and his early life was marked by beatings and trauma, including the accidental death of his older brother, Florian, due to his father’s violence. His mother was also abusive, employing harsh physical discipline. This difficult upbringing shaped his personality and contributed to a volatile temper. He married twice, first to Linda, with whom he had two sons, and later to Barbara, with whom he had three children. 

While outwardly appearing to be a successful businessman – described by his wife as a “wholesale distributor” – Kuklinski funded his family through illegal activities. He started by distributing pirated pornography and eventually became involved with members of the Gambino crime family through this trade. He was arrested once for a bad check, but the charges were dropped. 

Law enforcement began to focus on Kuklinski after an investigation into his burglary ring connected him to several missing men he was the last known person to see alive. An 18-month undercover operation culminated in his arrest in December 1986. He was convicted of four murders in 1988 and sentenced to life imprisonment, and later received an additional 30-year sentence in 2003 for the murder of an NYPD detective.

After his conviction, Kuklinski gained notoriety through interviews and media attention. He boasted of killing between 100 and 200 people, detailing gruesome methods, but these claims remain largely unverified. Law enforcement experts believe the actual number of murders he committed is significantly lower, estimating around 15. He also claimed connections to the Mafia, including involvement in the disappearance of Jimmy Hoffa, but these assertions were met with skepticism. Kuklinski’s story was dramatized in documentaries and a feature film, solidifying his place in true crime lore.

Several of his confirmed victims included George Malliband, killed in 1980 and frozen to obscure the time of death, earning him his nickname; Paul Hoffman, murdered in 1982; Gary Smith, killed in 1982 after being poisoned and strangled; Daniel Deppner, murdered in 1983; and Louis Masgay, whose body was discovered frozen in 1983. Kuklinski’s wife, Barbara, described his personality as shifting between a loving family man and a violently abusive individual, who was prone to unpredictable rages.  He filed for bankruptcy in 1984, listing significant debts despite his criminal enterprises.

title: Thomas Piketty
text:
Thomas Piketty is a French economist, born in 1971, currently working as a professor at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences, and holding positions at the Paris School of Economics and the London School of Economics. His work is largely focused on income and wealth inequality, a topic he’s explored extensively through both research and several influential books.

Piketty’s upbringing was shaped by parents involved in the political movements of the 1960s, though they had moved away from active political engagement by the time he was born. A formative experience – a visit to the Soviet Union – solidified his belief in capitalism and the market economy. He excelled academically, earning a mathematics and economics degree from the École Normale Supérieure and completing a PhD on wealth redistribution at the London School of Economics and EHESS, for which he received an award.

His career began with teaching positions at MIT before returning to France to work with the CNRS and later becoming a professor at EHESS. He briefly led the Paris School of Economics and served as an advisor to the Socialist Party candidate Ségolène Royal during the 2007 French presidential election. He regularly contributes op-eds to French newspapers like *Libération* and *Le Monde*. While initially supporting François Hollande’s presidential bid, he later expressed disappointment with his policies. He briefly served on the Labour Party’s Economic Advisory Committee in the UK, offering advice on tax policy, but resigned due to concerns about the party’s EU referendum campaign.

Piketty’s research utilizes historical data and statistical analysis to examine long-term trends in wealth and income distribution. He gained international recognition with his 2013 book, *Capital in the Twenty-First Century*, which argues that the rate of return on capital consistently exceeds economic growth, leading to increasing wealth concentration. He proposes measures like progressive global wealth taxation to address this. He followed this with *Capital and Ideology* (2019), which explores the ideological justifications for inequality throughout history and proposes solutions for wealth redistribution. His most recent book, *A Brief History of Equality* (2022), aims to make his research accessible to a broader audience. 

His work challenges conventional economic theories, including the Kuznets curve, and suggests that inequality is not a natural outcome of economic development but a product of political and social choices. He highlights the importance of estate taxation in reducing inequality during the 20th century and warns of a return to “patrimonial capitalism” where wealth is concentrated in the hands of a few families.  He also suggests that both left and right-wing political parties have become disconnected from the concerns of working-class voters, dominated instead by elites. 

Piketty has received numerous accolades for his work, including the Yrjö Jahnsson Award and the British Academy Medal, but notably rejected France's Legion of Honour, believing the government shouldn’t determine who is worthy of such recognition. He continues to teach and conduct research, focusing on wealth inequalities and contributing to ongoing debates about economic policy. He was previously in a relationship with politician Aurélie Filippetti, and she filed a domestic violence complaint against him in 2009.

title: Chris Cuomo
text:
Christopher Charles Cuomo, born in 1970, is an American television journalist currently working at NewsNation in New York City. His career began with appearances on CNBC, MSNBC, and CNN, and included a period as a correspondent for Fox News, where he covered controversial social issues. He later joined ABC News, becoming the chief law and justice correspondent and co-anchor of *20/20*, and also served as a news anchor for *Good Morning America* from 2006 to 2009. He is known for in-depth reporting, including coverage of the Haiti earthquake, heroin addiction, and various breaking news events, often reporting from the field in conflict zones like Iraq, Afghanistan and Pakistan.

Cuomo comes from a prominent political family; he is the younger brother of former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo and the son of former New York Governor Mario Cuomo. Both his parents were of Italian descent, with family roots in Southern Italy and Sicily. He received a law degree from Fordham University after studying at Yale and is a licensed attorney. 

He moved to CNN in 2013, initially co-hosting the morning show before transitioning to host *Cuomo Prime Time* in 2018. While at CNN, he also hosted a documentary series, *Inside with Chris Cuomo*, and a radio show, “Let’s Get After It” on SiriusXM. 

Cuomo’s tenure at CNN ended in December 2021 after an investigation revealed he had assisted his brother in responding to allegations of sexual harassment. The network determined his involvement was inappropriate and terminated his contract. This followed a period of suspension after documents emerged showing he used his media connections to gather information about his brother’s accusers and helped craft responses to the allegations. Prior to this, he faced criticism for interviewing his brother during the early stages of the scandal and for attempting to maintain objectivity while navigating a clear conflict of interest.

Before his dismissal, Cuomo was involved in a public incident where he confronted a heckler who called him “Fredo,” a derogatory term from *The Godfather*, stating the name was offensive to Italian-Americans. He later expressed regret for his reaction.

Following his departure from CNN, Cuomo launched *The Chris Cuomo Project*, a podcast, and ultimately joined NewsNation, debuting his show *Cuomo* in October 2022. He has stated his intention for the new program to be less partisan and more focused on neutral reporting. He also faced allegations of sexual misconduct from a former colleague, which contributed to his termination from CNN. He has denied the allegations. 

Throughout his career, Cuomo has received numerous awards, including Emmy, Polk, and Peabody Awards, for his reporting on a range of subjects. He is married with three children and resides in Manhattan, having recovered from a bout with COVID-19 in 2020, which he has said led to lasting long COVID symptoms.

title: Krystyna Szczepańska
text:
Krystyna Szczepańska, born on August 18, 1950, is a Polish designer working in stage and costume design. She was born in Kraków to parents with significant backgrounds: her father, Piotr Szczepański, was a lawyer and a graduate of Jan Kazimierz University, while her mother, Stanisława Żółtańska, was a teacher of the Russian language. Both parents originated from Berezhany and were involved in the Home Army during wartime. Szczepańska has a sister, Alicja, who followed in their father’s footsteps and became a lawyer.

A significant part of Szczepańska’s career involved a close professional relationship with director Andrzej Maj, whom she married. She frequently designed both the sets and costumes for his productions. This collaboration extended to various theatrical productions and television films. Their daughter, Magdalena, also pursued a career in design, specializing in costumes and sets, primarily within the advertising industry. Szczepańska also has another daughter, Elizabeth.

Szczepańska’s work appears extensively in Polish television productions from the early 1980s through the late 1980s. As a set designer, her credits include television plays such as *My wciąż spieszący*, *Kocham cię za to, że cię kochać muszę*, *Znana nasza*, *Milczeć pogodnie*, *Droga do Czarnolasu*, *Wiersze i krajobrazy*, *Piękność z Amherst*, *Obszar swobody*, *Nad wodą wielką i czystą*, *Twarze Witkacego czyli regulamin firmy portretowej*, *Dwie wigilie*, and *Trąd w pałacu sprawiedliwości*. She also contributed to the TV film *Harnasie* and the educational film *Dzieje kultury polskiej*, and the TV play *Koty? Koty!*. 

Beyond set design, Szczepańska also worked as a costume designer, notably for *Nad wodą wielką i czystą* and *Harnasie*. She also worked on interior decoration for the film *Kornblumenblau* in 1988.

Her theatrical work includes stage design for Andrzej Maj’s productions of *Niebezpieczne związki* at the Ludwik Solski Theatre in Tarnów in 1979, and *Jednorożec z gwiazd* and *Historia, czyli tu wcale nie chodzi o Mozarta* at the Stefan Jaracz Theatre in Łódź in 1982. She also worked on the decoration for *Ozimina* at the Stefan Jaracz Theatre in 1983, and designed costumes for *Pornografia*, also directed by Maj at the same theatre in 1985. Later in her life, Szczepańska emigrated to Vancouver.

title: Rangi Te Kanawa
text:
Rangituatahi Te Kanawa, also known as Warnes after marriage, is a New Zealand textile conservator and weaver dedicated to the preservation of Māori textiles. Her career began with a scholarship from the Department of Internal Affairs, driven by a desire within the Aotearoa Moananui a Kiwa Weavers for Māori involvement in conserving Māori artefacts held in institutions. Her initial training took place in Canberra, followed by a year at the National Museum of New Zealand’s conservation unit in Wellington. To qualify for a three-year degree in Conservation in Cultural Materials at Canberra University, she successfully completed sixth-form chemistry studies through a Wellington secondary school.

Further practical experience was gained through a six-month internship at the Textile Conservation Centre at Hampton Court Palace and time spent at the British Museum. Currently, Te Kanawa works at Te Papa Tongarewa, the Museum of New Zealand, where she specializes in the conservation of Māori textiles and conducts related research. A significant project she’s involved in is ‘Whakapapa of Paru’, a collaboration with a forensic scientist from GNS, focused on determining the origins of cloaks within Te Papa’s collection. 

Te Kanawa’s own weaving practice is also recognized, with examples of her work being collected by Te Papa itself. She is an active member of the New Zealand conservators of cultural materials association. In 2023, her contributions to Māori art and heritage preservation were formally acknowledged with her appointment as a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit in the King's Birthday and Coronation Honours.

Te Kanawa comes from a strong lineage of artistic and cultural practitioners. She is the daughter of Diggeress Te Kanawa and the granddaughter of the renowned Dame Rangimarie Hetet. She is affiliated with the Ngāti Maniapoto iwi, highlighting her deep connection to Māori heritage.

Beyond her practical work, Te Kanawa is also a published researcher. She co-authored an article titled “The Conservation of Māori Textiles in Aotearoa New Zealand” in the *Surface Design Journal* in 2020. She was also involved in a scientific study published in *Molecular Biology and Evolution* in 2011, which used ancient DNA to trace the origins of Māori feather cloaks. In 2021, she completed a PhD thesis entitled *Mana Taonga Kākahu: Exploring Approaches to Reconnecting Taonga Kākahu to Tangatawhenua* at Victoria University of Wellington, which is accessible through their Open Access Repository. Additional resources detailing her work, including a film about conserving cloaks and an interview discussing the challenges of Māori textile preservation, are publicly available.

title: Ki Fitzgerald
text:
Ki Fitzgerald, born Kiley McPhail, is a British DJ, musician, songwriter, and record producer who also performs as Azteck. He is the son of singer Scott Fitzgerald, known for the hit song “If I Had Words” and his participation in the 1988 Eurovision Song Contest. Fitzgerald began his musical journey early, becoming an original member of the pop punk band Busted in 2000, though his time with the group was brief, lasting until 2001. He later made an unsuccessful attempt to reclaim copyright ownership of some of Busted’s songs – “Year 3000”, “What I Go to School For”, and “Sleeping with the Light On” – despite having previously signed away his rights in 2003.

In 2007, Fitzgerald formed the band Eyes Wide Open, which toured the UK following a debut performance at the GWR Fiesta before an audience of 40,000. The band, also featuring members Tom Warner, TK, Pat Garvery, and Will Farquarson (later of Bastille), disbanded during the recording of their debut album with producers Steve Lironi and Simon Gogerly. 

Fitzgerald’s career shifted towards songwriting and production in 2011 when he signed with Global Talent Publishing. He quickly established himself as a successful writer and producer, working with a diverse range of artists including Galantis, Lawson, The Wanted, Jonas Brothers, B.o.B, Alex Hepburn, and Pitbull. He contributed to four top 10 singles by Lawson, namely “When She Was Mine”, “Standing in the Dark”, “Broken Hearted”, and “Roads”, as well as multiple tracks on their album *Chapman Square*. He also co-wrote songs for The Wanted’s album *Word of Mouth* and the debut single “Lipstick” by Sophia Del Carmen featuring Pitbull. 

In 2015, he signed an artist deal with RedOne’s 2101/Capital Records, leading to the release of “Come Follow” with Dutch DJ duo Sunnery James & Ryan Marciano. Fitzgerald has since been a featured vocalist on numerous EDM tracks, including collaborations with Hardwell, Wildstylez, DubVision, Firebeatz, Headhunterz (whose single “Into the Sunset” appeared on *Ellen DeGeneres* and *Dancing with the Stars*), and upcoming projects with Armin van Buuren and Dash Berlin. Beyond these vocal features, he has continued to write and co-produce songs for artists like Galantis, Madcon, and Saara Aalto, contributing to Aalto's song "Monsters” for the 2018 Eurovision Song Contest. He also co-wrote and provided vocals for Armin van Buuren’s single “Turn It Up” in 2019.

title: Griselda Blanco
text:
Griselda Blanco Restrepo, born in Cartagena, Colombia in 1943, rose to become a significant figure in the cocaine trade between Colombia and the United States during the 1970s through the early 2000s. She was killed in Medellín in 2012 at the age of 69. Her early life was marked by hardship; she moved to Medellín with her mother, becoming involved in petty crime like pickpocketing as a young teenager, and later fleeing an abusive home at 19, surviving through theft and potentially prostitution. 

Blanco initially engaged in marijuana dealing with her first husband, Carlos Trujillo, before shifting her focus to cocaine. After entering the US illegally in 1964, she and her second husband, Alberto Bravo, established a drug operation in New York City, linked to the Medellín Cartel. Facing federal drug conspiracy charges in 1975, the family fled back to Colombia. She later re-established a drug operation in Miami, a period coinciding with a surge in violence known as the “Miami drug war,” with hundreds of homicides annually. This led to the creation of CENTAC 26, a joint law enforcement task force to combat the cocaine influx.

In 1985, Blanco was arrested by DEA agents and convicted on charges of conspiring to manufacture, import, and distribute cocaine, receiving a 15-year sentence. While incarcerated, she faced multiple first-degree murder charges. A case built on the testimony of a hitman, Jorge Ayala, ultimately collapsed due to a scandal involving Ayala and state attorney’s office staff. She eventually pleaded guilty to three counts of second-degree murder in 1998, receiving a concurrent 20-year sentence. Due to declining health, she was granted compassionate release in 2004 and deported back to Colombia.

Blanco’s personal life was characterized by violence and turbulent relationships. She had three husbands and four children. She had her first husband, Carlos Trujillo, executed after a business dispute, and murdered her second husband, Alberto Bravo, after accusing him of theft. Her third husband, Darío Sepúlveda, kidnapped their son Michael after a disagreement, prompting Blanco to order his assassination and reclaim their child. Michael Blanco himself later faced drug trafficking charges and gained public attention through documentaries and a reality television series.  According to her son, Blanco found religion later in life. 

Blanco was assassinated in Medellín in 2012, shot twice in the head in a manner reminiscent of the killings she orchestrated during the height of the Miami drug war. Her life story has been the subject of numerous documentaries, television series, songs, and books, solidifying her notoriety and cementing her place in popular culture as the “Cocaine Godmother.”

title: Jimmy Weldon
text:
Jimmy Weldon, born Ivy Laverne Shinn on September 23, 1923, in Dale, Texas, was a multifaceted entertainer who worked as an actor, ventriloquist, and television host throughout a long career, passing away on July 6, 2023, at the age of 99. He is most widely recognized for voicing the Hanna-Barbera cartoon character Yakky Doodle.

Weldon’s career began in 1946 at KWCO in Texas, where he was the first announcer hired after the station’s launch following his service in World War II. It was at this radio station that he developed the character of Webster Webfoot, a duck who initially appeared as part of his disc jockey segments. Listeners enjoyed interacting with Webster, often believing him to be a separate individual, leading to the character’s growing popularity. 

He and Webster continued their work at KRHD in Duncan, Oklahoma for two years, before being recruited by WFAA in Dallas, Texas. This led to *The Webster Webfoot Show* premiering on WFAA-TV on April 4, 1950. In 1952, Weldon and Webster moved to California and joined KCOP-TV in Hollywood, continuing their television show. They garnered attention from established stars like Jeff Chandler and Randolph Scott, who playfully acknowledged Webster’s greater appeal to their own children. This notoriety led to an opportunity to co-host *Funny Boners*, a children’s game show on ABC, with Ralph Edwards.

Throughout the 1950s and 60s, Weldon and Webster moved between television stations in California, including a stint at KFRE-TV in Fresno, a brief period replacing Shari Lewis on the *Hi, Mom* show in New York, and a return to Channel 13 in Hollywood. They frequently travelled throughout the San Joaquin Valley, performing shows in cities like Salinas and Bakersfield, utilizing Weldon’s own airplane for transportation.

Beyond his work with Webster, Weldon had a successful voice acting career, most notably as Yakky Doodle. He also provided the voice of Solomon Grundy for Hanna-Barbera’s *Challenge of the Superfriends*. He also made appearances as an actor in live-action television shows including *Dragnet*, *Alfred Hitchcock Presents*, *The Waltons*, *Dallas*, and *Diff'rent Strokes*. Additionally, he contributed to the radio drama *Adventures in Odyssey* and was a member of the Premiere Speakers Bureau. In later life, he maintained a YouTube channel called Jimmy's Lecture where he shared stories from his time serving in WWII.

title: Mohamed Abdi Mohamed
text:
Mohamed Abdi Mohamed, known as “Gandhi,” was a prominent Somali figure who died on April 18, 2021. He was a multifaceted individual, working as a geologist, anthropologist, historian, politician, and scholar with two doctoral degrees. He was a candidate in the 2021 Somali presidential election and had been a member of the Somali Parliament since 2009. Prior to this, he served as Minister of Defense and also as Minister of Air and Transportation within the Transitional Federal Government. 

Gandhi’s academic journey began with memorizing the Koran in his youth and excelling in school. He attended Jamal Abdelnazer High School in Mogadishu, graduating as an honor student in 1970 and earning a full scholarship to study in France. He earned a B.A. in geology from Besançon University in 1976, followed by a Master of Science in Geology in 1979, and a Ph.D. in applied geology in 1983, focusing his dissertation on the geology and hydrogeology of central Somalia. He later obtained a second Ph.D. in history and civilization of antiquity in 1990, continuing to lecture at Besançon University throughout the decade. He also earned a certificate in Anthropology of Space in Portugal and a Higher Degree in Research from Besançon.

Beyond his formal education, Gandhi remained deeply connected to Somalia, returning annually to teach at the University of Mogadishu in the departments of History and Geology. He worked with the National Museum of Somalia, starting in 1987, to catalog ancient manuscripts. He was actively involved in the Somali peace process, leading committees and consultations at peace conferences in Arta, Djibouti and Kenya. He co-founded the Association Somali Peace Line in Paris and consulted with organizations like Doctors Without Borders and UNESCO. He authored 12 books and over 50 scientific articles, and edited three studies, focusing on topics such as Somali poetry, women's involvement in peacebuilding, and a dictionary of peoples.

Gandhi held several significant political positions. As Minister of Defense, beginning in 2009, he advocated for rebuilding Somalia's security forces and proposed a 36,000-strong army. He also served as the first President of Azania (Jubaland), an autonomous region in southern Somalia, from 2011 to 2013, aiming to remove the Al-Shabaab militant group from the area. In 2014, he was appointed Somalia’s Ambassador to Canada, reopening the Somali embassy in Ottawa after a 20-year hiatus. He was also involved in establishing associations dedicated to Somali studies in France and Europe, fostering research and cultural exchange.

title: Steve Cummins
text:
Steven Cummins, born on March 29, 1992, is an Australian professional rugby union player who currently plays for the Melbourne Rebels in Super Rugby. He is a versatile forward, typically playing as a lock, but also capable of covering the blind-side flanker position. 

Cummins’ rugby journey began in Sydney, where he excelled as a schoolboy player. He captained the first XV at The Hills Sports High in 2010, and received further recognition that same year by being named captain of both the New South Wales All Schools team and the Australian Schoolboy team. His leadership continued into the following year, as he captained the Australia Under-19 side in 2011. He also participated in the 2012 IRB Junior World Championship as a member of the Australia Under-20 team.

Before reaching the professional ranks, Cummins played for Eastwood in the Shute Shield competition, where his work ethic and contributions to the tackle and breakdown were noted by coach John Manenti. In 2013, he gained experience with the Waratahs’ development side, Gen Blue, competing in the Pacific Rugby Cup.

His professional career began in 2014 with a short-term contract with the Eastern Province Kings in South Africa, joining them for the Currie Cup Premier Division season. He made his debut for the Kings as a substitute against Wales during a tour match, playing the final six minutes of a 34-12 defeat. Cummins also started in the opening game of the Currie Cup, and featured in a total of eight matches for the Kings, including their only win of the season against the Pumas, a narrow 26-25 victory. 

Notably, on the very same day he was announced by the Eastern Province Kings, Cummins also signed a contract with the Melbourne Rebels, joining their Extended Playing Squad for the 2015 Super Rugby season. He subsequently re-signed with the Rebels for another two years in early 2015.

Following his time in Australia, Cummins moved to Wales in November 2017, signing with the Scarlets. As of June 12, 2021, he continues to be a professional rugby player, currently playing with the Melbourne Rebels.

title: Adnan Sami
text:
Adnan Sami Khan, born on August 15, 1969, is an Indian singer, musician, composer, actor and pianist known for performing in multiple languages including Hindi, Urdu, English, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam. He received the Padma Shri, India’s fourth highest civilian award, in 2020 for his contributions to music. Recognized for his piano skills, he’s been lauded as “the first musician to have played the santoor and Indian classical music on the piano” and was hailed by *Keyboard* magazine as the fastest keyboard player in the world in the 1990s. He is often referred to as the “Sultan of Music” by the Indian media.

Sami was raised and educated in the United Kingdom, and became a naturalized Indian citizen in 2016. His father, Arshad Sami Khan, was a Pakistani Air Force veteran and diplomat of Pashtun origin with Afghan roots, having served as Pakistan’s ambassador to fourteen countries. His mother, Naureen Khan, is from Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir. His paternal lineage includes figures like General Ahmed Jan, a military advisor to an Afghan king, and Agha Mehfooz Jan, a governor of Afghan provinces.

From a young age, Sami demonstrated musical talent, playing the piano from age five and composing his first piece at nine. He studied Indian classical music with Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and was encouraged by Asha Bhosle after performing at a concert in London at the age of ten. He pursued formal education, earning a law degree from King’s College London and qualifying as a barrister from Lincoln’s Inn.

His musical career began with the English single "Run for His Life" in 1986, which topped charts in the Middle East. He followed this with further successful singles before releasing his debut album, *The One & Only* in 1989, featuring tabla maestro Zakir Hussain.  His first vocal album, *Raag Time*, came in 1991. A significant breakthrough arrived with the collaboration with Asha Bhosle on *Kabhi To Nazar Milao* (2000), selling an estimated 4 million copies in India. *Tera Chehra* (2002) became India’s best-selling album that year and the next, and the best-selling Indian album ever in the US and Canada, featuring Bollywood stars in its music videos. 

Sami has also composed music for numerous Hindi films, including *Lucky: No Time for Love* and *Dhamaal*. His foray into acting began with the 1995 Pakistani film *Sargam*, where he starred and Asha Bhosle provided playback, achieving box office success. He gained recognition for the song “Tu Sirf Mera Mehboob” from *Ajnabee* in 2001. More recently, he sang “Bhar Do Jholi Meri” for *Bajrangi Bhaijaan* (2015) and appeared in the film.

Throughout his 32-year career, Sami has received several awards, including the Nigar Award, Bolan Academy Award, and a special award from UNICEF for a song written for Ethiopia. He also received a United Nations Peace Medal and, in 2008, the Naushad Music Award for Excellence in Music.  He has performed for royalty and heads of state worldwide, and in 2003 became the first South Asian artist to sell out Wembley Stadium for two consecutive nights.

Sami experienced health challenges in 2005 with lymphoedema, but underwent a significant weight loss, dropping 130 kg. His personal life includes multiple marriages and divorces, and he became an Indian citizen in 2016 after his Pakistani passport was not renewed. He has been outspoken about his experiences, particularly regarding difficulties in visiting his mother’s funeral due to visa issues and has been critical of the Pakistani government.

title: Theophilus Annorbaah
text:
Theophilus Annorbaah is a Ghanaian professional footballer born on September 17, 1989. He currently plays his club football for Medeama SC, a team based in Tarkwa, Ghana, and also represents the Ghana national football team. Annorbaah’s professional career includes playing for Ashanti Gold SC before joining Medeama SC in May 2011. 

A significant achievement in his club career came on July 14, 2013, when Medeama SC secured a 1-0 victory over Asante Kotoko in the final of the Ghanaian FA Cup. This win marked Annorbaah’s first title with the club. 

His involvement with the Ghana national team began in November 2013, when coach Maxwell Konadu selected him for the 2013 WAFU Nations Cup squad. He played a role in the team’s success, culminating in a first-place finish for Ghana after defeating the Senegal national football team with a score of 3-1. 

Annorbaah continued to represent his country and was also selected for the 2014 African Nations Championship. While the team performed well, they ultimately finished as runners-up in that tournament. The article does not detail any specific goals scored by Annorbaah for the national team, only listing a section dedicated to potential international goals.

Throughout his career, Annorbaah has accumulated several honors. At the club level, he is a Ghanaian FA Cup winner with Medeama SC, having achieved this in 2013.  On the international stage, he is a WAFU Nations Cup winner with Ghana, also from 2013, and was part of the team that reached the final of the 2014 African Nations Championship.

title: Charmion King
text:
Charmion King, a Canadian actress, was born in Toronto, Ontario on July 25, 1925, and passed away there on January 6, 2007, at the age of 81. Her career blossomed during the growth of Canada’s theatre and television scene in the 1950s. She began her acting journey immediately after completing her studies at Hart House at the University of Toronto. 

King quickly gained recognition for her appearance and talent, securing roles at the Crest Theatre and participating in the Straw Hat Players’ summer performances in the Muskoka Lake region. This early work served as a springboard for larger opportunities, leading to her involvement with the prestigious Stratford Festival. During her time at Stratford, she performed in several significant productions, including *The Winter’s Tale*, *Three Sisters*, and *Uncle Vanya*.  

Her career extended beyond Canada, as she made an appearance on Broadway, performing in Tyrone Guthrie’s production of *Love and Libel*. King also became a familiar face on television, landing roles in several well-known productions. She portrayed Josephine Barry in the classic television film *Anne of Green Gables* and took on the role of Rose Fitzgerald Kennedy in *Jackie, Ethel, Joan: The Women of Camelot*. 

Furthermore, she starred in two Canadian television series, *Wind at My Back* and *House of Pride*, demonstrating her consistent presence in the Canadian entertainment industry.  In 1988, she also appeared in the film *Shadow Dancing*.

Beyond her individual accomplishments, Charmion King’s life was deeply intertwined with that of another prominent Canadian actor, Gordon Pinsent, whom she married. Their marriage lasted for 44 years. Their family connection to the arts continued with their daughter, Leah Pinsent, who also became a recognized actress in Canadian television. According to reports, King’s death was due to complications stemming from emphysema.

title: Bhuma Nagi Reddy
text:
Bhuma Nagi Reddy was an Indian politician born on January 8, 1964, and died on March 12, 2017, from a heart attack at the age of 53. His entry into politics followed the death of his brother, Bhuma Sekhar Reddy, an MLA representing Allagadda in Kurnool district; Nagi Reddy won the resulting by-election in 1992. He was the youngest son of Bhuma Bali Reddy and Eeswaramma, and his father’s murder spurred his decision to pursue a political career in the Rayalaseema region. 

Reddy served as a Member of Parliament in the 11th, 12th, and 13th Lok Sabhas. In 1996, he notably contested against then-Prime Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao in the Nandyal Lok Sabha constituency, narrowly losing but gaining significant recognition. He subsequently won a by-election for the same seat, defeating Rangaiah Naidu. He also secured victories in the 1998 and 1999 elections, the latter by a margin of 72,600 votes, defeating Gangula Prathapa Reddy in both instances.

Reddy’s political affiliations shifted over time. Initially with the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), he and his wife, Shobha Nagi Reddy, joined the Praja Rajyam Party in 2008. Following a merger of the Praja Rajyam Party with the Indian National Congress, they opposed the decision and aligned themselves with Y. S. Jaganmohan Reddy's YSR Congress Party.  Later, in 2016, Nagi Reddy and his daughter, Akhila Priya Reddy, who was an MLA for Allagadda, returned to the TDP.

Beyond elections, Nagi Reddy was involved in parliamentary committees, including those focused on finance, external affairs, transport, tourism, energy, and urban development. He was also recognized for his contribution to the construction of a railway line connecting Yerraguntla and Nandyal. 

He held strong views on regional identity, stating in 2007 that Rayalaseema should join Telangana rather than remain with Andhra Pradesh, citing cultural and economic similarities and a history of drought and poverty in Rayalaseema.

His wife, Shobha Nagi Reddy, was also a politician who tragically died in a car accident in 2014 while campaigning for re-election. Together they had three children, including Akhila Priya Reddy, who continued her father’s political legacy as the MLA for Allagadda.

title: Pallavi Joshi
text:
Born in Mumbai on April 4, 1969, Pallavi Joshi is an Indian actress, writer, and film producer working primarily in Hindi cinema and television. Her career began at the remarkably young age of four with a small role in the 1973 film *Naag Mere Sathi*, and continued with appearances in films like *Badla* (1976) and *Aadmi Sadak Ka* (1977). She gained recognition for playing a blind child who positively influences a gangster in *Dada* (1979).

Joshi’s career took a significant turn with her involvement in the parallel cinema movement of the 1980s and early 1990s. She starred in critically acclaimed films such as *Bhujangayyana Dashavathara*, *Rihaee*, *Rukmavati Ki Haveli*, and *Woh Chokri*, earning a National Film Award – Special Jury Award for her performance in the latter. She also appeared in several mainstream commercial films including *Insaaf Ki Awaaz*, *Andha Yudh* – for which she received a Filmfare Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress – *Mujrim*, and *Saudagar*. 

Beyond Hindi films, Joshi has also worked in regional cinema, playing the central character of Shantha in the Malayalam film *Ilayum Mullum* and appearing in a significant role in the Kannada film *Bhujangayyana Dashavathara*. She also took on a lead role in the Marathi film *Rita*. 

In television, Joshi found success with popular Doordarshan shows including *Talaash*, *Aarohan*, *Alpviram*, and *Justujoo*. She also hosted the music show *Zee Antakshari* for five years and the singing competition *Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Marathi Li'l Champs*. More recently, she has frequently collaborated with her husband, director Vivek Agnihotri, producing and acting in *The Tashkent Files* (2019) and *The Kashmir Files* (2022), winning two National Film Awards for Best Supporting Actress for these roles.

Joshi has received further recognition for her work, including the Excellence In Cinema Award at the Global Film Festival, Noida. She was initially nominated to the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) society but declined the position in solidarity with student protests. She is currently serving as the Vice-President of FTII, Pune, alongside President Ranganathan Madhavan. Her upcoming project is *The Delhi Files*. She is also a producer of Marathi serials, including *Asambhav* and *Anubandh*. She married Vivek Agnihotri in 1997 and they have two children, and she is the sister of former child actor Master Alankar Joshi.

title: Andreea Marin
text:
Andreea Violeta Marin, born on December 22, 1974, is a prominent figure in Romanian television, working as a presenter and personality. Her academic background is diverse, having pursued studies in Journalism, Public Relations & Advertisement, Computer Programming, and Mathematics & Physics during her time in college. She began her career in television in 1994, initially working as an emcee at TVR Iași. 

Marin’s success in the Romanian media landscape led to recognition as the most successful female media person in the country. She gained further exposure through her involvement with the Eurovision Song Contest, presenting the Romanian votes during the finals in 2000, 2004, 2006, and 2007. A significant moment in her hosting career was when she hosted the 2006 Junior Eurovision Song Contest on December 2nd of that year.

For an extended period, beginning in 1999, Marin has been the host and director of the television program *Surprize, Surprize* ("Surprises, Surprises") which airs on TVR1. The show focuses on sharing the life stories of individuals facing various hardships, including those with disabilities, financial difficulties, or those separated from family members who have moved away.

Beyond her on-screen work, Marin also holds positions in media management. She currently serves as the communications director for Prime Time World Broadcast, a company based in Madrid. Additionally, she is the editorial director for the Romanian edition of *Business Woman Magazine*. 

Marin’s personal life has been public, marked by two marriages and subsequent divorces. In 2006, she married Romanian singer Ștefan Bănică Jr., taking the name Andreea Marin Bănică. They have one daughter together, Ana Violeta Bănică, born on December 15, 2007. This marriage ended in divorce in 2013.  She then married physician Tuncay Öztürk in 2014, but they announced the end of their relationship in October 2016, with the divorce being finalized on February 13, 2017.

title: Raffaele Maiello
text:
Raffaele Maiello is an Italian professional football player born on July 10, 1991. He currently plays as a midfielder for the club Casarano. While currently with Casarano, his career has involved playing in multiple levels of Italian football, including a brief appearance in Serie A. 

Maiello’s first taste of top-flight football came with Napoli, where he made his Serie A debut on May 16, 2010. This appearance occurred during a match against Sampdoria, and he entered the game as a substitute in the 86th minute, replacing Luca Cigarini. This marks his only recorded Serie A appearance according to the available information. 

More recently, in January 2022, Maiello joined Bari, a club competing in Serie C, on a loan deal. This loan agreement included a specific condition: Bari had an obligation to permanently acquire his playing rights should they achieve promotion to Serie B. This ultimately came to fruition, as Bari was promoted and subsequently purchased Maiello’s contract.

Maiello’s time with Bari proved successful, as he was part of the team that won the Serie C championship for the 2021–22 season, specifically within Group C. This represents a significant achievement in his career, marking a league title win. The information available is current as of June 2, 2023, and details his career statistics up to that date, although the specific statistics themselves are not included in the provided text. 

Resources for further information on his career are available online. He is listed on TuttoCalciatori.net, a website dedicated to Italian football, and details regarding his registration can be found on the official website of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC). These links provide a means to access more comprehensive details regarding his playing history and statistics.

title: Sofiane Feghouli
text:
Sofiane Feghouli, born December 26, 1989, is a professional footballer who plays for the Algerian national team, primarily as a midfielder, but also capable of playing as a winger or attacking midfielder. He was born in Levallois-Perret, France, to Algerian parents originating from Tiaret and Ghazaouet, and is one of five brothers.

Feghouli began his club career with Grenoble, signing his first professional contract in 2007 after a trial with Paris Saint-Germain didn’t result in a deal. He made his debut for Grenoble at age 17 and helped the team achieve promotion to Ligue 1, scoring three goals in 27 matches during the promotion season. A knee injury in 2009, and a subsequent disagreement with Grenoble officials regarding his recovery and potential transfer, led to his move to Valencia CF in 2010. 

At Valencia, Feghouli initially struggled for consistent playing time, spending a loan period at UD Almería where the team was relegated. Upon his return, he became a regular starter, scoring a brace against Getafe in 2011 and earning Algerian Player of the Year awards in 2012 – the Le Buteur’s Algerian Ballon d’Or and the DZFoot d’Or. He amassed 202 appearances for Valencia, scoring 31 goals and providing 40 assists before a suspension in 2016 led to his departure.

In June 2016, Feghouli joined West Ham United, making his debut in the Europa League qualifiers and scoring his first goal for the club in their first match at the London Stadium. A controversial red card against Manchester United in 2017 was later rescinded. He moved to Galatasaray in August 2017 for a €4.25 million transfer fee, where he won the Süper Lig twice, the Turkish Cup and the Turkish Super Cup. More recently, in November 2022, he joined Fatih Karagümrük on an eighteen-month contract.

Feghouli was eligible to represent both France and Algeria internationally. Though initially leaning towards France and appearing in youth squads, he ultimately chose to play for Algeria. He made his debut for Algeria in 2012, scoring the winning goal in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier. He represented Algeria in the 2013, 2015, 2019 (winning the tournament) and 2021 Africa Cup of Nations, and the 2014 FIFA World Cup, where he scored Algeria’s first World Cup goal since 1986. He was surprisingly left out of the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations squad but was named in the squad for the 2023 tournament. 

Throughout his career, Feghouli has received individual accolades, including the LFP Award for Best African Player in 2014–15 and the DZFoot d'Or in 2012, as well as being named Algerian Footballer of the Year in 2012.

title: Ahn Jae-hyun
text:
Ahn Jae-hyun, born on July 1, 1987, is a South Korean actor and model who first began his career in the entertainment industry as a fashion model in 2009. He worked in runway shows, magazines, and commercials before gaining wider public recognition in 2011 with an appearance on the cable variety show *Lee Soo-geun and Kim Byung-man's High Society*, where he played a delivery man. He further built his presence through appearances in music videos for artists like Baek A-yeon, K.Will, and Sistar19.

His breakthrough as an actor came in 2013 when he played the younger brother of Jun Ji-hyun in the popular drama *My Love from Another Star*. This role opened the door for further acting opportunities, including parts in the police comedy *You're All Surrounded* and the film *Fashion King* in 2014. That same year, he became the MC for the music program *M Countdown* on Mnet.

Ahn took on his first leading role in 2015, portraying a vampire doctor in the drama *Blood*, and also appeared in the short drama *Snow Lotus Flower*. In 2016, he starred in the romantic comedy *Cinderella with Four Knights*, playing a wealthy and carefree character, for which he received a Top Excellence Award at the Korea Drama Awards. He also joined the cast of the travel reality show *New Journey to the West*, and appeared in the Chinese film *Perfect Imperfection*.

He continued to take on diverse roles in subsequent years, including a second lead in the fantasy romance *Reunited Worlds* (2017) and a role in the romance melodrama *The Beauty Inside* (2018). In 2019, he led the romantic comedy *Love with Flaws* alongside Oh Yeon-seo. 

Beyond acting, Ahn ventured into publishing, releasing his first photo essay, *List of Things to Remember*, in June 2022. Demonstrating his philanthropic side, he donated 10 million won from profits from a 2022 exhibition to aid orphans affected by the coronavirus in February 2023.

Ahn’s personal life garnered significant media attention when his relationship with actress Koo Hye-sun, his *Blood* co-star, became public in March 2016, revealing they had been dating since April 2015. They married in May 2016, choosing to donate funds to a hospital pediatric ward instead of holding a wedding ceremony and documenting their early married life on the reality show *Newlywed Diary*. However, the marriage faced difficulties, and in August 2019, news broke of Ahn requesting a divorce, which was filed in court in September of that year. He subsequently deleted all photos from his Instagram account in October 2019 amidst the divorce proceedings.

title: Rory Tapner
text:
Rory Tapner, born on September 30, 1959, is a British businessman with a long career in financial services. He is best known for his leadership roles at UBS and Coutts. Tapner received his education at Radley College and King’s College London, where he earned an LLB degree in 1982. 

The majority of Tapner’s career, spanning from 1983 to 2009, was spent with UBS AG and its preceding companies – SG Warburg, SBC Warburg, and UBS Warburg. Throughout his time at UBS, he progressed through a series of increasingly senior positions. He began as Joint Head of UK Corporate Finance and Head of the UK Capital Markets Team, then became Global Head of Equity Capital Markets. He later served as Joint Global Head of Investment Banking and then Chairman of Investment Banking. Ultimately, he reached the position of Chairman and CEO of UBS Asia Pacific, a role he held from May 2004 until June 2009. During portions of this time, from 1996 to 2004 and again from 2006 to 2009, he was a member of the UBS Investment Bank and Group Executive Boards respectively.

Following his departure from UBS in 2009, Tapner returned to the UK and, in September 2010, was appointed CEO of Coutts, the wealth management division of Royal Bank of Scotland Group. He led Coutts for just over four years, stepping down in February 2015 and being succeeded by Alison Rose. 

Since leaving Coutts, Tapner has taken on several chairmanships. In June 2019, he was appointed Chair of the Board at Brown Shipley Holdings Limited, and in May 2020, he became Chairman of the Board of Directors of Quintet Private Bank, the parent company of Brown Shipley. He has also served as Chairman of organizations including GB Snowsport, the national governing body for British Snowsports, and SPS Technology.

Beyond his corporate roles, Tapner has maintained a strong connection to his alma mater, King’s College London. He was the Honorary Treasurer and Chairman of the Financial Committee of the Council of King’s College London for nine years and served as Deputy Chairman of the “World Questions; King’s Answers” fundraising campaign. He is currently a Fellow of King’s College, London.

Tapner’s children are also successful in their respective fields. His eldest son, Freddie Tapner, founded The London Musical Theatre Orchestra and serves as its principal conductor, while his younger daughter, Rosie Tapner, is a TV presenter and model.

title: John Craven
text:
John Craven, born on August 16th, 1940, is a British journalist and television presenter who is widely recognised for his work on programmes such as Newsround, Countryfile, and Beat the Brain. He was born in Leeds, West Riding of Yorkshire, and received his education at Leeds Modern School. His early life was impacted by his father’s experience as a prisoner of war in Japan during World War II, where he was held for three years.

Craven began his career after leaving school at the age of 16, initially undertaking an apprenticeship at Yorkshire Copperworks and contributing to their company magazine. He then transitioned into print journalism, starting as a junior reporter for the Harrogate Advertiser, followed by work with the Yorkshire Post and freelance writing for various national newspapers. 

He joined the BBC in Newcastle upon Tyne, working in both radio and television, before relocating to the BBC in Bristol in 1970. His most prominent role began in 1972 when he became the original presenter of *John Craven's Newsround*, a children’s news programme which was the first of its kind in British television. The programme utilized the extensive journalistic resources of the BBC and gained recognition for breaking news stories, one notable example being the coverage of the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster in 1986, which occurred just before the programme was due to air. 

Craven's association with children’s television extended beyond Newsround, including appearances delivering news segments on programmes like *Multi-Coloured Swap Shop* and *Saturday Superstore*. He later returned to Newsround in an editorial capacity. After presenting over 3,000 episodes, he left the programme in 1989 and subsequently became a presenter on *Countryfile*, focusing on countryside news. In 2015, he broadened his presenting experience by hosting the BBC Two game show *Beat the Brain*.

Outside of his regular presenting work, Craven participated in Gareth Malone’s All Star Choir in 2014, contributing to a cover version of “Wake Me Up” to benefit BBC’s Children in Need. The choir’s activities were documented in a two-part series, *Gareth's All Star Choir*, broadcast on BBC One in November 2014.  

Craven is actively involved in several charitable organisations, serving as one of nine presidents of the Young People's Trust for the Environment, vice-president of the Waterways Trust, and a Patron of SPANA. He was appointed President of Radio Horton, a hospital radio station serving Banbury’s Horton General Hospital, in July 2016.

Craven is married with two daughters and currently resides in Oxfordshire. He has expressed a desire to continue working as long as possible, enjoying his career immensely. Throughout his career, he has received several accolades, including election to the Royal Television Society in 1996 and the RTS Baird Medal in 2002. He was awarded an OBE in the 2000 New Year Honours for his contributions to children's and rural broadcasting, and is a Fellow of the Linnean Society of London. Newsround itself received a Special Award at the British Academy Children's Awards in 2011, which Craven collected in recognition of the programme’s impact.

title: Rafael Nadal
text:
Rafael Nadal, born in 1986 in Mallorca, Spain, was a highly successful professional tennis player who reached the world No. 1 ranking and held it for 209 weeks, finishing the year as No. 1 five times. Throughout his nearly two-decade career, he amassed 92 ATP Tour singles titles, including a record 14 French Open championships, 36 Masters titles, and an Olympic gold medal. He is one of only three men to achieve the career Golden Slam – winning all four major titles and an Olympic gold. Nadal retired from the sport after playing in the 2024 Davis Cup Finals.

Nadal rose to prominence alongside Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic, forming the “Big Three” who dominated men’s tennis for years. He quickly achieved success as a teenager, winning 16 titles and reaching No. 2 in the world before turning 20, highlighted by his first major title at the 2005 French Open. He first became world No. 1 in 2008 after a historic Wimbledon final victory over Federer, becoming the first to win a Grand Slam outside of clay. He followed this with Olympic gold at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. In 2010, he achieved a career Grand Slam at the young age of 24 by winning the US Open, making him the youngest man in the Open Era to do so, and the first to win majors on three different surfaces in the same year.

Nadal demonstrated remarkable consistency, winning major singles titles in ten consecutive years (2005-2014) and again across a four-year span (2017-2020). He also secured 11 doubles titles, including another Olympic gold at the 2016 Rio Olympics. He surpassed Federer and Djokovic’s shared record for most Grand Slam singles titles at the 2022 Australian Open and became one of only four men to complete the double career Grand Slam.

Known for his powerful left-handed forehand with heavy topspin, Nadal excelled in return games and break points. Clay courts were particularly suited to his game, where he won 63 of his 92 singles titles. Beyond his on-court achievements, Nadal was recognized for his sportsmanship, receiving the Stefan Edberg Sportsmanship Award five times and being named Laureus World Sportsman of the Year in 2011 and 2021. *Time* magazine included him in their list of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2022.

Nadal’s early life was shaped by his family, particularly his father, a businessman, and his uncle, Toni Nadal, a tennis coach who began training him at age three. Initially favoring football, Nadal was encouraged to focus on tennis by his uncle, who implemented rigorous training methods. He excelled in junior competitions, winning multiple Spanish junior championships and reaching the final of the U14 Spanish championship. He turned professional in 2001 at the age of 14 and quickly rose through the ranks, winning his first ATP title in 2004 and leading Spain to a Davis Cup victory that same year. He continued to ascend, winning his first major title at the 2005 French Open and establishing himself as a dominant force in the sport. He also established a tennis academy in Mallorca and actively participates in philanthropic endeavors.

title: Bobo Baldé
text:
Bobo Baldé, born Dianbobo Baldé in Marseille, France in 1975, was a professional footballer who primarily played as a defender. His club career began in 1995 with Marseille, but he moved to Mulhouse in 1997 seeking more playing time. A loan spell at Cannes followed, where he made 29 appearances and scored four goals, before joining Toulouse and contributing to their promotion.

The most significant period of Baldé’s career was with Celtic, where he played from 2001 to 2009. He amassed 232 appearances for the club, scoring six goals in his first season, including one in the Scottish Cup final against Rangers. He was a key player in Celtic’s successes, winning five Scottish Premier League titles, three Scottish Cups, and two Scottish League Cups. He was also part of the team that reached the 2003 UEFA Cup Final, though he was sent off during the match which they lost 3-2 to Porto. In 2003, he was voted Celtic Player of the Year by the fans, becoming the inaugural winner of the award, and also won the SPL Player of the Month for April. Later seasons saw him struggle with form and injuries, including a broken leg in 2006, and he faced criticism and a decline in his first-team opportunities. He ultimately saw out his contract with Celtic but didn’t play competitively in his final season.

After leaving Celtic, Baldé moved to Valenciennes in France in 2009 before joining Arles-Avignon in 2011. Alongside his club career, Baldé represented the Guinea national team 52 times, scoring two goals and participating in the 2002, 2004 and 2006 Africa Cup of Nations tournaments, and 2006 FIFA World Cup qualifying. 

Following his playing career, Baldé transitioned into coaching, beginning as a sports coordinator for the Guinea national team in 2013. He then took on a playing assistant manager role with his former youth club, Gombertois, in 2014, before becoming the manager of Guinea’s national U20 team in 2019. Baldé's younger half-brother, Yasser, is also a professional footballer. Throughout his career, he faced instances of racial abuse from opposing fans, which led to convictions and bans for those involved.

title: Chacho Gaytán
text:
Gonzalo “Chacho” Gaytán is a multifaceted Mexican musician with a career spanning composition, production, arrangement, direction, and conducting. He is perhaps most widely recognized as the co-founder and keyboardist of the popular Mexican pop band Sentidos Opuestos, a group he formed alongside Alessandra Rosaldo. Beyond his work with the band, Gaytán enjoys a significant family connection to the entertainment industry, being the brother of actress and singer Bibi Gaytán and brother-in-law to actor and singer Eduardo Capetillo.

Gaytán’s talents extend beyond performance and band leadership into the realm of music production. He received a Latin Grammy Award nomination in 2000, recognized in the category of Best Latin Children's Album for his work on *Ellas Cantan a Cri-Cri*. His skills as a musical director have been showcased in large-scale productions, most notably his direction of *West Side Story*. He is also highly regarded for his orchestral work within Mexico, encompassing musical arrangement, orchestration, and conducting. 

He has demonstrated his conducting abilities by presenting work with the National Philharmonic Orchestra at the prestigious Palace of Fine Arts in Mexico City. This showcases his capacity to work with and elevate established and respected musical institutions. Further demonstrating his versatility, Gaytán collaborated with Fernando de la Mora in a concert setting, accompanied by the Campeche Philharmonic Orchestra.

In addition to his work with established productions and artists, Gaytán founded the Mexican jazz band, Manzana Jazz Band, indicating a personal passion for and involvement in the jazz genre. Currently, he holds the position of director at Azteca Music, a television network in Mexico, signifying a move into music administration and broadcasting. 

Furthermore, Gaytán is a co-founder of MYST, where he continues to contribute as both musical producer and director. His solo discography includes the album *Un día después*, released in 2007, showcasing his individual artistic output. Throughout his career, Chacho Gaytán has established himself as a prominent figure in Mexican music, displaying a broad range of skills and a dedication to various musical forms.

title: Flávio Rocha
text:
Flávio Gurgel Rocha, born on February 14, 1958, is a Brazilian businessman and former politician currently serving as the CEO and Chairman of Lojas Riachuelo, a major retail company in Brazil. He also leads Midway Financeira, the financial services arm of the Riachuelo group. His family’s business interests extend beyond retail to include Confecções Guararapes, the manufacturing component of the group, and Transportadora Casa Verde, which handles the group’s logistics. Riachuelo itself is a significant employer in Brazil, boasting over 40,000 employees as of 2017.

Rocha’s political career began in 1986 when he was elected as a federal deputy representing the state of Rio Grande do Norte, running under the banner of the National Reconstruction Party (PRN). He successfully defended his seat in 1990, this time as a member of the Liberal Party (PL). In 1994, he sought the presidency of Brazil, also under the PL, but ultimately shifted his support to Fernando Henrique Cardoso and the Brazilian Social Democracy Party (PSDB), who went on to win the election. He served as a federal deputy from 1987 to 1995.

Throughout his career, Rocha has consistently advocated for free market principles, viewing them as a vital tool in combating corruption. He is a prominent advocate for economic liberalism within Brazil and champions the idea of a smaller, more efficient government. 

In 2016, Rocha was recognized for his business achievements with the “Entrepreneur of the Year” award from *Isto É Dinheiro* magazine, specifically in the retail sector. He was also an early and vocal supporter of the impeachment proceedings against former president Dilma Rousseff, and publicly backed João Doria’s candidacy for mayor of São Paulo. 

Further demonstrating his political and economic convictions, Rocha spearheaded the launch of the “Brasil 200” manifesto in January 2018. This manifesto promotes a liberal economic agenda coupled with socially conservative values, with the name referencing the bicentennial of Brazil’s independence. 

Alongside his professional and political endeavors, Flávio Rocha and his wife are members of the Comunidade Evangélica Sara Nossa Terra, a neo-Pentecostal church.

title: Erich Hartmann
text:
Erich Alfred Hartmann, born in 1922, was the most successful fighter ace in the history of aerial warfare, amassing 352 aerial victories during World War II while flying for the Luftwaffe. He completed 1,404 combat missions and engaged in 825 aerial combats, shooting down 345 Soviet and 7 American aircraft. Remarkably, Hartmann was never shot down himself, though he was forced to crash-land his fighter 16 times due to mechanical failures or damage from enemy fire.

Hartmann’s journey began with gliding, a passion fostered by his parents, both of whom were involved in aviation. He joined the Luftwaffe in 1940 and completed his fighter pilot training in 1942, subsequently being assigned to the highly experienced Jagdgeschwader 52 (JG 52) on the Eastern Front. There, he learned from veteran pilots, developing his tactical skills. He steadily increased his kill count, earning the Knight’s Cross of the Iron Cross in October 1943 for 148 victories, then the Oak Leaves to the Knight’s Cross in March 1944 for 202 victories. In August 1944, he received the Swords to the Knight's Cross with Oak Leaves, culminating in the Knight’s Cross with Oak Leaves, Swords and Diamonds for 301 victories – Germany’s highest military decoration at the time.

Hartmann’s early combat experience was marked by a lack of discipline, resulting in a temporary grounding after recklessly pursuing an engagement and crashing due to fuel exhaustion. He learned from his mistakes and adopted a tactical approach emphasizing observation, decisive action, and close-range attacks, influenced by experienced pilots like Paule Roßmann. He became known as "Bubi" (kid) by his colleagues. He proved particularly successful during the intense fighting around Kursk in July 1943, becoming an “ace-in-a-day” multiple times, claiming as many as seven victories in a single day. By August 1943, he had accumulated 90 victories and was appointed Staffelkapitän (squadron leader).

Hartmann’s success stemmed from a combination of skill and a pragmatic assessment of Soviet pilot capabilities and equipment. He initially believed Soviet pilots were poorly trained and equipped, with rudimentary gunsights, and he learned valuable techniques from captured airmen to address problems like cold-weather engine starting. He emphasized careful assessment of the combat situation over aggressive maneuvering. 

His final victory came on May 8, 1945, just hours before Germany’s surrender. He and his unit surrendered to US forces, but were handed over to the Soviets. Accused of war crimes in an attempt to coerce him into joining the Soviet-aligned East German air force, he was sentenced to 25 years of imprisonment and spent ten years in Soviet prison camps and gulags before being released in 1955. He was posthumously exonerated by Russia in 1997.

After his release, Hartmann joined the newly formed West German Air Force in 1956 and became the first Geschwaderkommodore (wing commander) of Jagdgeschwader 71 “Richthofen”. He retired in 1970 due to disagreements over the procurement of the F-104 Starfighter, over safety concerns, and later worked as a civilian flight instructor. He died in 1993 at the age of 71. His early life was impacted by his family’s move from Germany to China and back, and his brother also served in the Luftwaffe during the war.

title: Bastian Schweinsteiger
text:
Bastian Schweinsteiger, born in 1984, was a German professional footballer who primarily played as a midfielder, evolving from a wide position to a central role. Considered one of Germany’s greatest players by former national team manager Joachim Löw, he enjoyed a distinguished 17-year career with Bayern Munich, appearing in 500 matches across all competitions and scoring 68 goals. During his time at Bayern, he secured eight Bundesliga titles, seven DFB-Pokal titles, a Champions League title, a FIFA Club World Cup, and a UEFA Super Cup. He later played for Manchester United for a year and a half and finished his career with Chicago Fire. He announced his retirement in October 2019 and now works as a football analyst for German television.

Schweinsteiger joined Bayern Munich’s youth system in 1998, having previously been a talented ski racer. He progressed through the ranks, earning a place in the reserves and making his first-team debut in 2002 against RC Lens in the Champions League, immediately impacting the game with an assist. He quickly established himself, initially playing as a left-back, and contributed to a league and cup double in his first season. Though briefly sent back to the reserves by a new coach, he soon regained his place and became a consistent performer for Bayern over the next several years. He scored the first Bundesliga goal of the 2008-09 season and extended his contract with the club multiple times, eventually signing a deal that ran until 2016. A pivotal moment came in 2012 when he scored a penalty against Real Madrid, sending Bayern to the Champions League final, though they ultimately lost to Chelsea. He was a key figure in Bayern’s treble-winning season of 2012-13, earning the German player of the year award and receiving praise from his manager as the world's best midfielder. 

For the German national team, Schweinsteiger earned 121 caps and scored 24 goals between 2004 and 2016, making him the fourth-most capped player in the nation’s history. He participated in four European Championships and three World Cups, culminating in victory at the 2014 FIFA World Cup. In that tournament, he played a vital role, particularly in containing Lionel Messi in the final. After Philipp Lahm’s retirement, Schweinsteiger was named captain of the national team, a role he held until his international retirement following a match against Finland in 2016. 

His time at Manchester United was less successful, marked by injury and a period of being excluded from the first team under José Mourinho, which drew criticism from former teammates. He eventually found success with Chicago Fire, helping them return to the playoffs and earning a contract extension. Throughout his career, Schweinsteiger was known for his leadership, versatility, and commitment, becoming a fan favourite at Bayern Munich, where he was affectionately nicknamed “Fußballgott” (football god).

title: Maya Yoshida
text:
Maya Yoshida, born in Nagasaki, Japan in 1988, is a professional footballer currently captaining and playing as a centre-back for LA Galaxy.
