He amassed over 120 appearances for the Japan national team, participating in the FIFA World Cups of 2014, 2018, and 2022, as well as the AFC Asian Cup in 2011 (winning the tournament), 2015, and 2019 (where they were runners-up). He also represented Japan’s Olympic team in 2008, 2012, and 2020.

Yoshida’s football journey began with Nanling FC while in elementary school, spurred by his older brother who discovered Nagoya Grampus’s U-15 team. He relocated to Nagoya to join the youth academy and was eventually promoted to the first team in 2007. Initially playing as a defensive midfielder, he was transitioned to centre-back. He debuted for Nagoya Grampus against Oita Trinita, becoming a regular in the team, and scored his first goal against Thespa Kusatsu in the Emperor’s Cup. He earned the "Rookie of the Year" award in 2008 after a successful season where Nagoya Grampus finished third in the league. In 2009, he scored eight goals in all competitions and helped the team reach the Emperor’s Cup final, ultimately losing to Gamba Osaka.

In December 2009, Yoshida transferred to Dutch club VVV-Venlo, fulfilling his ambition to play in Europe. However, his start was hampered by a fractured foot which sidelined him for the remainder of the 2009-10 season. He made his debut in October 2010, quickly becoming a key player. After winning the AFC Asian Cup with Japan in 2011, he helped VVV-Venlo retain their Eredivisie status through the relegation play-offs. He continued to be a prominent figure in the 2011-12 season, scoring five goals and winning the “Goal of the Season” award for a spectacular bicycle kick. He again helped the club avoid relegation via the play-offs.

In August 2012, Yoshida joined Southampton in the Premier League. He became a regular in the starting lineup, forming a strong partnership with José Fonte. He played in various defensive positions, contributing to Southampton’s improvement and their avoidance of relegation in his first season. While his playing time fluctuated in subsequent seasons due to competition and injuries, he remained a valuable squad member, extending his contract in 2015. He helped Southampton qualify for the UEFA Europa League on multiple occasions, experiencing a period of both starting roles and time on the bench. He captained Southampton for the first time in an FA Cup match and reached the EFL Cup final with the team in 2017, though they ultimately lost.

title: Lupe Vélez
text:
Lupe Vélez, born María Guadalupe Villalobos Vélez in San Luis Potosí, Mexico in 1908, was a prominent actress, singer, and dancer during Hollywood’s Golden Age. She began her performing career in Mexican vaudeville in the early 1920s, initially performing under her father’s surname. After a disagreement with her father about her career choice, she adopted her mother’s maiden name, Vélez, as her stage name. She quickly gained recognition for her energetic performances and ability to attract publicity, even facing rivalry with other vedettes.

In 1926, she moved to Los Angeles, hoping for a role in a play but was replaced upon arrival. However, she soon landed a small role in a Laurel and Hardy short, progressing to more significant parts in silent films like *The Gaucho* (1927) and *Lady of the Pavements* (1928). Vélez successfully transitioned to sound films, becoming one of the first Mexican actresses to achieve success in Hollywood. During the 1930s, she became known for her comedic roles in films like *Hot Pepper* and *Strictly Dynamite*, capitalizing on her vibrant and boisterous screen persona.

The 1940s saw the peak of her popularity with the *Mexican Spitfire* series, where she played the fiery Carmelita Fuentes in eight films. This role cemented her “Mexican Spitfire” nickname, given to her by the media, and was created to exploit her on-screen energy. Beyond her professional life, Vélez was known for her colorful personal life, filled with highly-publicized romances with actors like Gary Cooper and a turbulent marriage to Johnny Weissmuller. She was known for her outspoken nature and willingness to engage with the press, often sharing details about her relationships. 

Vélez’s childhood included a period of study at Our Lady of the Lake University in San Antonio, Texas, where she learned English and dance. While she enjoyed dancing, she considered herself a poor student otherwise. She briefly returned to Mexico in 1938 to star in *La Zandunga*, a critical and financial success, before returning to Hollywood. Later in her career, she appeared in films like *Six Lessons from Madame La Zonga* and *Redhead from Manhattan*. 

Despite her success, Vélez struggled with portraying a consistent image – often typecast as “exotic” or “volatile” women. She felt she was simply being herself, and valued authenticity. She also had a public feud with Libby Holman during a Broadway production of *You Never Know* in 1938, ending the show prematurely. Tragically, Lupe Vélez died in December 1944 at the age of 36 from an intentional overdose of Seconal, a barbiturate drug. Her death and the surrounding circumstances were shrouded in speculation and controversy, marking a sad end to a vibrant and influential career.

title: Zewde Gebre-Sellassie
text:
Zewde Gebre-Sellassie, born on October 12, 1926, and passing away on December 15, 2008, was a significant figure in Ethiopian history, serving as a nobleman, historian, and former Deputy Prime Minister. He was born in the village of Galdu, near Addis Ababa, where his father had been relegated. His lineage connected him to prominent Ethiopian nobility; his father was Dejazmatch Gebre Selassie Baria Gabr, governor of Adwa, and his mother was Leult Wolete Israel Seyoum. He was a grandson of Ras Seyum Mengesha and was married to Woizero Alem Tsehai Araya. His sister was Leult Ijigayehou Asfa Wossen.

Zewde received his initial education from a private tutor in Addis Ababa. During the Italian occupation of Ethiopia, his mother took him to continue his schooling in Jerusalem and Cairo. Following liberation, he attended Haile Selassie I secondary school in Addis Ababa before pursuing higher education in England. He initially studied English literature at the University of Exeter and then undertook legal training at St. Anthony's College, Oxford, becoming a senior member there from 1963 to 1971. He was called to the Bar at Lincoln’s Inn in London and later returned to Oxford to earn a PhD focusing on history, politics, and economics.

Upon returning to Ethiopia in the early 1950s, Zewde embarked on a distinguished career in public service. He held a variety of important governmental positions over the next two decades. These included roles as an Economic Attaché, later Head of Press, Information and Administration at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Director-General of Maritime Affairs, and Deputy Minister of Public Works, Transport and Civil Aviation. He served as Mayor and Governor of Addis Ababa from 1957 to 1959, and then as Ambassador to Somalia in 1959-1960. He later became Minister of Justice from 1961 to 1963 and was appointed Permanent Representative to the United Nations in 1972, serving until 1974. In the final months of the imperial government in 1974, he held the posts of Minister of the Interior and then Minister of Foreign Affairs.

The 1974 revolution and the subsequent summary executions carried out by the Derg forced Zewde into exile. He later became Vice-President of the United Nations Economic and Social Council and worked as an advisor to the UN secretariat for several years. Throughout his career, he was recognized with national honors from at least seven countries, including West Germany. In 1998, he participated in mediation efforts between Ethiopia and Eritrea alongside other prominent Ethiopians.

Zewde Gebre-Sellassie was also a published author. His works include *Yohannes IV of Ethiopia: A Political Biography* (1975), *The process of re-unification of the Ethiopian Empire, 1868-1889* (1971), *The blue Nile and its basins : an issue of international concern* (2006), and *የኢትዮጵያ እና የኤርትራ ግጭት መንሥኤ እና መፍትሔ (The Conflict of Ethiopia and Eritrea: Causes and Solutions)* (2015).

title: Kevin De Bruyne
text:
Kevin De Bruyne, born on June 28, 1991, is a Belgian professional footballer considered one of the best players in the world at his peak, often described as a “complete” footballer. He currently plays as a midfielder for Napoli and captains the Belgian national team, having earned 110 caps and scoring 30 goals for his country. He participated in the 2014 FIFA World Cup, reaching the quarter-finals, as well as Euro 2016, the 2018 World Cup where he was named in the Fan Dream Team, Euro 2020, the 2022 World Cup, and Euro 2024.

De Bruyne began his youth career at Gent before joining Genk, where he became a regular player and helped them win the 2010–11 Belgian Pro League. In 2012, he moved to Chelsea, but saw limited playing time and was subsequently loaned to Werder Bremen. His performances in the Bundesliga earned him a transfer to VfL Wolfsburg in 2014 for £18 million, where he quickly established himself as a key player, winning the 2014–15 DFB-Pokal. 

In the summer of 2015, Manchester City signed De Bruyne for a then-club record £54 million. Over 422 appearances for City, he achieved significant success, including winning the UEFA Champions League, six Premier League titles, five League Cups, and two FA Cups. He played a crucial role in City’s record-breaking 2017–18 season, where they became the only Premier League team to reach 100 points. He equaled the record for most assists in a Premier League season in 2019–20, earning the Premier League Player of the Season award, a feat he repeated in 2021–22. He was central to City’s historic treble-winning season in 2022–23.

Throughout his career, De Bruyne has received numerous individual accolades. He has been named in the UEFA Champions League Squad of the Season and IFFHS Men's World Team six times each, the ESM Team of the Year and FIFA FIFPRO World 11 five times each, the UEFA Team of the Year three times, and the France Football World XI and Bundesliga Team of the Year once each. He’s also a three-time Premier League Playmaker of the Season, a two-time PFA Players’ Player of the Year, and a four-time Manchester City Player of the Year. He's also been honoured as the Bundesliga Player of the Year, Germany’s Footballer of the Year, and Belgium’s Sportsman of the Year. He was nominated for the Ballon d'Or several times, finishing third in 2022 and fourth in 2023. 

De Bruyne's early development was heavily influenced by coaches Jan Troos and Charly Musonda at Gent, who focused on his fundamental skills. He grew up as a Liverpool fan and admired Michael Owen. Throughout his career, he's demonstrated a consistent ability to create opportunities and score goals, solidifying his reputation as one of the world’s most impactful midfielders.

title: Noel Malicdem
text:
Noel Malicdem, born on January 10, 1977, is a professional darts player from the Philippines who competes in events organized by the Professional Darts Corporation, commonly known as the PDC. He has twice qualified for the PDC World Championship, achieving notable results in both appearances. 

Malicdem first earned a spot in the 2019 World Championship. His debut saw him face Jeffrey de Graaf in the first round, a match he won with a score of 2-3. He then progressed to the second round where he was defeated by Kyle Anderson, losing by a score of 1-3. 

He successfully qualified for the 2020 World Championship through the Asian Tour, finishing in fourth place overall on the tour standings. This qualification marked his second appearance at the prestigious tournament. In his opening match, Malicdem demonstrated strong form, securing a convincing 3-0 victory against Rowby-John Rodriguez. His second-round match against Peter Wright was a particularly close and dramatic contest. Malicdem held a lead and even had opportunities to win the match, possessing match darts, but ultimately was unable to close out the game. The match went to a sudden-death leg, where Peter Wright ultimately prevailed, winning the game 3-2.

Beyond individual championship performances, Malicdem has also represented his country, the Philippines, in team competition. In 2019, he partnered with Lourence Ilagan to compete in the PDC World Cup of Darts. Their participation ended in the first round, as they faced and lost to the team representing England. 

To date, Malicdem’s World Championship record reflects these two appearances. In 2019, he reached the second round before being defeated by Kyle Anderson. He repeated this achievement in 2020, again reaching the second round but losing a closely fought match against Peter Wright. Information regarding his broader PDC performance timeline is available, though the article provides only his World Championship results. Further details about his career statistics and profile can be found on the Darts Database website.

title: Ezechiel N'Douassel
text:
Ezechiel Aliadjim N’Douassel, born in 1988, is a Chadian professional footballer currently playing as a striker for Bekasi City. He began his career in 2006 with Tourbillon before moving to Algeria, joining MC Oran and then USM Blida in 2007. It was at USM Blida where he first gained recognition, scoring a brace on his debut and finishing the season with five goals in fifteen appearances. During his time there, he attracted interest from several European clubs, including Olympique de Marseille and Arsenal, but a move to Belgian club FCV Dender in 2009 ultimately fell through due to contractual issues, forcing his return to USM Blida.

In 2011, N’Douassel signed a four-year contract with Tunisian side Club Africain, where he participated in the CAF Confederation Cup, reaching the final in 2011 and the fourth round in 2012, even scoring a hat-trick in the latter competition. A proposed loan move to Paris FC in 2014 was cancelled due to financial difficulties, leaving him seeking a new club.

He then moved to Israel in 2016, initially signing a three-year contract with Ironi Kiryat Shmona, but departed for Hapoel Tel Aviv after only a few months. His time at Hapoel was short-lived, ending in March 2017 due to behavioral concerns. Later that year, he joined Persib Bandung in Indonesia, initially on a half-year deal which was then extended. He quickly became a key player, scoring his first league goal for the club in August 2017 and becoming their top scorer in the 2018 season with 17 goals, including a four-goal performance against PSM Makassar in 2019.

In January 2020, N’Douassel transferred to Bhayangkara, where he made his debut in a pre-season cup, helping the team win the tournament after scoring in a match against Petaling Jaya City. He continued to contribute in the league, scoring his first goal against Persija Jakarta. He further showcased his scoring ability in the 2021 Liga 1 season, achieving braces against Persiraja Banda Aceh and Barito Putera.

Throughout his career, N’Douassel has been a consistent presence in the Chad national team, debuting in 2005. He is the national team's most capped player and all-time leading goalscorer, and has participated in numerous Africa Cup of Nations and World Cup qualifying campaigns, as well as CEMAC Cup tournaments. He was also recognized with the Liga 2 Player of the Half Season and Player of the Month awards for November 2024-25.

title: Rebecca Romijn
text:
Rebecca Romijn was born in Berkeley, California, in 1972 to an English teacher mother and a Dutch furniture maker father. Her maternal grandfather was a Presbyterian minister. While she is known for her glamorous image, Romijn has spoken about feeling insecure as a teenager and even suffering from scoliosis during a growth spurt, a story she initially claimed was fabricated as a joke. She studied music at the University of California, Santa Cruz before launching a successful modeling career in 1991, appearing on covers for numerous international editions of magazines like Elle, Cosmopolitan, and Sports Illustrated, and walking runways for designers such as Giorgio Armani. She also hosted MTV’s *House of Style* from 1998 to 2000 and was frequently included on lists of the world’s most beautiful women.

Romijn transitioned into acting with her breakout role as Mystique in the *X-Men* film series, appearing in *X-Men* (2000), *X2* (2003), and *X-Men: The Last Stand* (2006). The role required extensive makeup and prosthetics. She continued to build her film career with roles in films like *Femme Fatale*, *Rollerball*, *The Punisher*, and *Godsend*. 

On television, she gained prominence for her role as Alexis Meade, a transgender character, on the ABC series *Ugly Betty* beginning in 2007, though her role later became recurring. She also appeared on shows such as *Carpoolers*, *Eastwick*, and *NTSF:SD:SUV::*. More recently, Romijn starred as Eve Baird in *The Librarians* and voiced Lois Lane in the DC Animated Movie Universe. She also played Una Chin-Riley in *Star Trek: Discovery* and subsequently in *Star Trek: Strange New Worlds*, beginning in 2022, and currently co-hosts *The Real Love Boat* with her husband. She is slated to reprise her role as Mystique in a future Marvel Cinematic Universe film. 

Romijn was married to John Stamos from 1998 to 2005. In 2007, she married actor Jerry O'Connell, and they have twin daughters born in 2008. While she uses her maiden name professionally, she revealed she never legally changed her name back from Romijn-Stamos following her first divorce. Beyond acting and modeling, Romijn has also contributed to music, providing vocals for cover songs and collaborating with RuPaul.

title: Dennis Andersson
text:
Dennis Andersson, born on June 3, 1991, is a retired motorcycle speedway rider hailing from Sweden. His professional career encompassed riding in both Polish and British speedway leagues, alongside success in junior European and Swedish championships. 

Andersson began his involvement with the Polish Ekstraliga league by riding for Atlas Wrocław, a commitment that lasted until the conclusion of the 2012 season. He continued to compete in Poland for two further seasons, first with Stal Rzeszów in 2013 and then with Polonia Bydgoszcz, marking the end of his time riding professionally in the country. 

His introduction to British speedway occurred in 2011 when he joined the Poole Pirates. He remained with the Pirates for a total of three seasons, establishing a presence in the British league. 

However, Andersson’s most significant achievements came during his time as a junior competitor. He reached the pinnacle of Under-19 European Speedway competition by winning the Individual U-19 European Championship in 2010, held in Goričan, where he scored 14 points plus 3 bonus points. This victory followed previous attempts in the same competition, achieving 7th place in Stralsund in 2008 with 9 points, and again in Tarnów in 2009 with 8 points. 

He also demonstrated dominance within Sweden, securing the Swedish U-21 Championship not once, but twice, in both 2010 and 2012. Further demonstrating his skill in team events, Andersson was a runner-up in the Team U-19 European Championship in 2009, held in Holsted, contributing 8 points to his team’s total. 

Although the article does not detail the reasons for his retirement, it is stated definitively that Andersson is a *former* speedway rider. His career highlights centre around his European and Swedish junior titles, combined with his experience riding for prominent clubs in Poland and the United Kingdom. He is linked to both the Sweden national speedway team and the broader history of speedway in Sweden.

title: John Forbes Nash Jr.
text:
John Forbes Nash Jr., born in 1928 in West Virginia, was a highly influential American mathematician whose work profoundly impacted several fields, including game theory, real algebraic geometry, differential geometry, and partial differential equations. He received the 1994 Nobel Prize in Economics, shared with John Harsanyi and Reinhard Selten, and in 2015 was awarded the Abel Prize alongside Louis Nirenberg for their contributions to partial differential equations. Nash’s career began at Princeton University, where as a graduate student he developed core concepts like the Nash equilibrium and Nash bargaining solution, now fundamental to game theory.

His mathematical contributions extended beyond game theory. In the 1950s, he proved the Nash embedding theorems, resolving complex problems in Riemannian geometry through the analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations. This work also contained an early form of the Nash–Moser theorem.  He collaborated with Ennio De Giorgi, and independently, they developed methods that resolved Hilbert’s nineteenth problem concerning the smoothness of solutions to elliptic and parabolic partial differential equations – a challenge that had remained open for nearly six decades. 

Despite his brilliance, Nash experienced a significant period of mental illness beginning in 1959, diagnosed as schizophrenia, and spent years in psychiatric hospitals. His condition gradually improved after 1970, allowing him to return to academic work by the mid-1980s.  

Nash’s early life saw encouragement from his parents to pursue advanced studies.  He initially studied chemical engineering at Carnegie Institute of Technology on a scholarship, then shifted to chemistry before ultimately focusing on mathematics under the guidance of John Lighton Synge. He was accepted to multiple prestigious universities but chose Princeton due to a fellowship offer and its proximity to his family.  At Princeton, he was described as a “mathematical genius” by a former professor, Richard Duffin.

While not a prolific publisher, Nash’s papers were consistently groundbreaking.  He made significant contributions to real algebraic geometry in 1949, presenting a theorem at the International Congress of Mathematicians, later refined and published.  His work demonstrated that smooth manifolds could be approximated by polynomials, a surprising and impactful result.  During his post-doctoral work at MIT, he tackled problems in differential geometry, culminating in the Nash embedding theorems, considered a major achievement of 20th-century mathematics.

Later in his career, Nash explored cryptography, proposing an encryption-decryption machine in letters to the National Security Agency in the 1950s that anticipated concepts central to modern cryptography. He also contributed to the understanding of partial differential equations, extending Morrey’s work and collaborating with Nirenberg, ultimately resolving a long-standing conjecture and contributing to the De Giorgi–Nash–Moser theory. His work in this area, along with De Giorgi’s, proved crucial in addressing Hilbert’s nineteenth problem. 

Nash’s life story gained wider recognition through Sylvia Nasar’s biography, *A Beautiful Mind*, and the subsequent film adaptation directed by Ron Howard, starring Russell Crowe, which portrayed his struggles with mental illness and his eventual recovery. He passed away in 2015, leaving behind a legacy of profound mathematical innovation.

title: Celâl Bayar
text:
Mahmut Celâl Bayar was born in 1883 in Bursa, Ottoman Empire, to a family of religious scholars who had migrated from Bulgaria. His early career involved work in various administrative and banking roles, including positions at the Gemlik Régie Company, Ziraat Bank, and Deutsche Orientbank. He received education at the Collège Français de l'Assomption and in silk production. Bayar became involved in the Committee of Union and Progress (CUP) in 1907, establishing branches in Bursa and İzmir, and participating in the 1913 coup. During this period, he was involved in organizing the deportation of Ottoman Greeks and contributed to the foundation of several schools and a sports club in İzmir.

Following World War I and the Armistice of Mudros, Bayar was initially tried as a war criminal but acquitted. He then actively participated in the Turkish War of Independence, forming associations to resist Allied occupation of İzmir and fighting alongside nationalist forces. He was elected to the Ottoman Parliament in 1919 and later joined Mustafa Kemal (Atatürk) in Ankara, becoming a deputy in the newly established Grand National Assembly of Turkey. He served as Minister of Economy between 1921 and 1937, playing a key role in the development of Turkey’s early financial institutions, including the founding of İş Bankası. 

Bayar served as Prime Minister from 1937 to 1939, appointed by Atatürk to liberalize the economy. After Atatürk’s death and a change in leadership, he resigned due to disagreements with İsmet İnönü.  Remaining within the Republican People’s Party (CHP) until 1946, he then co-founded the Democrat Party (DP) alongside Adnan Menderes and others, marking a crucial shift towards multi-party politics in Turkey. The DP won the 1950 elections, and Bayar was subsequently elected as Turkey’s third president, a position he held for ten years, being re-elected in 1954 and 1957. 

During his presidency, Turkey aligned more closely with the West, joining NATO in 1952, and experienced significant social and economic changes. However, the latter part of the DP’s rule saw a drift towards authoritarianism.  In 1960, Bayar was overthrown in a military coup and imprisoned. He was initially sentenced to death, but his sentence was commuted to life imprisonment due to his age and health.  He was released in 1964 due to ill health, but faced periods of re-arrest and house arrest before finally being fully released. He spent his later years advocating for the restoration of rights for former DP politicians. 

Celâl Bayar was noted for his longevity, being the longest-lived former head of state for many years, and died in 1986 at the age of 103. His career represents a significant period in Turkish political history, from the final years of the Ottoman Empire through the establishment of the Republic and the introduction of a multi-party system.

title: Michael Coulson (barrister)
text:
James Michael Coulson, born in 1927 and passing away in 2002, was a British barrister and judge who also spent five years as a Member of Parliament. He came from a prosperous background in the East Riding of Yorkshire, his father being a wool merchant. Coulson was educated at Fulneck School in Leeds and Merton College, Oxford, and completed his national service with the East Riding Yeomanry.

He was called to the Bar at the Middle Temple in 1951, practicing on the North Eastern Circuit while also taking on cases in London. Simultaneously, he became involved in Conservative politics, actively reorganizing the Young Conservatives in the north of England and even drafting their constitution. He also continued his military service, achieving the rank of Major in the Queen’s Own Yorkshire Yeomanry.

In 1955, Coulson married Dilys Adair Jones, gaining a 400-acre farm near Tadcaster as part of the marriage. He enjoyed farming, even training at the Royal Agricultural College, though a turkey farming venture proved disastrous, requiring him to house the birds in an airing cupboard and ultimately ending in their mass poisoning. He was also a keen equestrian and huntsman, serving as secretary for local point-to-point races.

Coulson’s political career took off when he was selected as the Conservative candidate for Kingston upon Hull North in 1958. He won the seat in the 1959 general election, increasing the previous slim majority, and delivered a well-received and witty maiden speech. As an MP, he was a supporter of the Conservative leaders of the time and successfully introduced a Private Member’s Bill to abolish the farthing as legal tender. He also served as Parliamentary Private Secretary to the Solicitor General and was involved with the Conservative Commonwealth Council.

Losing his parliamentary seat in 1964, Coulson focused on his legal career. He became an Assistant Recorder of Sheffield in 1965, followed by roles as Deputy Chairman of the Northern Agricultural Land Tribunal and Regional Chairman of Industrial Tribunals. Personal difficulties led him to relocate to the East Midlands in the 1970s to become a full-time chairman of Industrial Tribunals. He remarried in 1977 to Barbara Chambers, a hunting acquaintance significantly younger than himself. 

He progressed through the judiciary, becoming a Recorder of the Crown Court in 1981 and a Circuit Judge on the Midland and Oxford Circuit in 1983, earning the nickname "the hunting Judge" in his village. In 1990, he was appointed a Deputy Circuit Judge. A significant judgment in 1994 saw him award damages to Trevor McAuley for unfair dismissal based on racial discrimination, establishing a precedent for enhanced damages in such cases. Coulson retired in 1998 at the age of 70.

title: Khalid Mahmood Mithu
text:
Khalid Mahmood Mithu, a Bangladeshi film director and painter, was born in Dhaka in 1960 and passed away on March 7, 2016, after being struck by a falling tree while riding in a rickshaw in Dhanmondi, Dhaka. He left behind his wife, Kanak Chanpa Chakma, who is also a painter, and their two children, a son named Arjo Srestha and a daughter named Shiropa Purna. 

Mithu came from a family with connections to the Bangladeshi film industry; his mother, Begum Momtaz Hossain Mithu, was a scriptwriter and he was the nephew of renowned film director Alamgir Kabir. He pursued formal artistic training, earning a Master of Fine Arts degree from the Faculty of Fine Arts at the University of Dhaka in 1986. Before transitioning to film, Mithu demonstrated his theatrical talents by directing a play titled *Dhusor Album* in 1993.

His career as a filmmaker gained significant recognition with the release of *Gohine Shobdo* in 2010. This film proved to be a critical success, earning him the Bangladesh National Film Award for Best Director. He continued his filmmaking endeavors with *Jonakir Alo*, released in 2014. This second feature film achieved international attention as it was selected to represent Bangladesh as its entry for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film that same year, though it ultimately did not receive a nomination.

Beyond his work in cinema, Mithu maintained a consistent presence in the art world as a painter. By 2004, he had already established himself as an artist with a notable exhibition history, having presented his work in eleven solo exhibitions. This demonstrates a parallel dedication to both visual storytelling through film and the creation of visual art through painting, showcasing a multifaceted artistic talent throughout his life. His filmography consists of these two works: *Gohine Shobdo* and *Jonakir Alo*.

title: Daniel Bedingfield
text:
Daniel Bedingfield, born in Auckland, New Zealand in 1979, is a singer, songwriter, record producer, and actor who has achieved significant success in the music industry. He is the older brother of singers Natasha Bedingfield and Nikola Rachelle. He first gained prominence in 2001 with his single “Gotta Get Thru This”, which rose to number one in the UK after building momentum within the UK garage scene. This success was followed by two further number-one singles, “If You're Not the One” and “Never Gonna Leave Your Side,” as well as three additional top ten hits. His debut album, *Gotta Get Thru This*, recorded using home software, sold over 4 million copies worldwide and peaked at number two in the UK.

In 2004, Bedingfield received a BRIT Award for Best British Male Artist before releasing his second album, *Second First Impression*, on Polydor Records. While it reached number eight in the UK, it did not achieve the same sales figures as his first album. The album produced two Top 20 singles, including “Nothing Hurts Like Love,” but a later single, “The Way”, failed to reach the top 40. 

Following a four-year period where he reportedly had three albums recorded but unreleased, Bedingfield continued to work within the music industry, writing songs for other artists. He co-wrote “Works for Me!” for *American Idol* finalist David Archuleta and collaborated with Pixie Lott, as well as contributing vocals to a track featuring a former member of The Roots. He also spent time in Jamaica, writing and recording with artists like Tessanne Chin and Busy Signal. Further collaborations included work with The Raw Men Empire in Israel and recording on the “Overproof Riddim” in Jamaica.

In 2012, Bedingfield released the single "Rocks Off" and the EP *Stop the Traffik – Secret Fear*, the latter of which supported the anti-slavery coalition of the same name. He then served as a judge on the first season of *The X Factor New Zealand* in 2013, mentoring the Girls category and ultimately leading his act, Jackie Thomas, to victory. He also appeared as a judge on *X Factor Around the World* that same year. 

Bedingfield’s songwriting continued to be successful; he co-wrote “I Wanna Feel” by SecondCity, which reached number one on the UK Singles Chart in 2014, marking his fourth UK number-one song. He also worked with the K-pop group Spica, co-producing their first English single and serving as their vocal director. He contributed to *The X Factor UK* winner Ben Haenow’s debut album with the song "Testify". In 2016, he transitioned to acting, appearing in the West End production of *The War of the Worlds* as The Artilleryman. 

In 2024, Bedingfield announced a UK tour. Throughout his life, he survived a serious car accident in 2004 that left him with head and neck injuries, and he has publicly shared that he is autistic. He is also involved in charitable work with his mother’s organization, Global Angels, and supports the Stop the Traffik coalition.

title: Rachel Weisz
text:
Rachel Weisz is an English actress born in London in 1970, known for her work in both independent and mainstream films. She’s received numerous accolades throughout her career, including an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, a Golden Globe, and a Laurence Olivier Award.

Weisz began her acting career in the early 1990s with stage and television roles, making her film debut in 1994 with *Death Machine*. A breakthrough came with her performance in the 1994 revival of Noël Coward’s *Design for Living*, for which she won a Critics' Circle Theatre Award. Her film career gained momentum with the blockbuster *The Mummy* (1999) and its sequel, *The Mummy Returns* (2001). Throughout the 2000s, she appeared in a diverse range of films including *Enemy at the Gates*, *About a Boy*, *The Constant Gardener*, and *The Fountain*. 

Her performance as an activist in *The Constant Gardener* (2005) earned her the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress. She continued to balance independent projects with larger productions, appearing in films like *The Bourne Legacy* and *Oz the Great and Powerful* in the 2010s. Critical acclaim followed for roles in *The Deep Blue Sea*, *Denial*, and particularly *The Favourite* (2018), for which she won the BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role and received another Academy Award nomination. More recently, she portrayed Melina Vostokoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s *Black Widow* (2021) and starred in the thriller miniseries *Dead Ringers* (2023).

Weisz’s parents were Jewish immigrants to the United Kingdom, fleeing Nazi Germany before World War II. Her father was a mechanical engineer and her mother a teacher-turned-psychotherapist. She has a younger sister, Minnie, who is a visual artist. Her upbringing emphasized independent thought and appreciation for the arts. She attended several schools, including Benenden School, and ultimately graduated from Trinity Hall, Cambridge with an upper second-class honours degree in English. While at Cambridge, she was involved in student theatre, co-founding a drama group and winning an award at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe for an improvised piece she wrote.

Before becoming a professional actress, Weisz did some modelling, famously turning down a role in *King David* with Richard Gere at the age of 14.  She trained at École Philippe Gaulier, studying under master clown Philippe Gaulier. Her early television work included roles in *Advocates II*, *Inspector Morse*, and *Scarlet and Black*. She’s maintained a consistent stage presence throughout her career, winning a Laurence Olivier Award for her portrayal of Blanche DuBois in a 2009 revival of *A Streetcar Named Desire*.



Weisz was in a long-term relationship with director Darren Aronofsky, with whom she has a son, before marrying actor Daniel Craig in 2011. They have a daughter together. She has worked with major fashion houses and remains a prominent figure in the entertainment industry. She became a naturalised American citizen in 2011, while retaining her British citizenship.

title: Aditya Kalyanpur
text:
Aditya Kalyanpur, born in Mumbai, India on July 21, 1978, is a highly accomplished Tabla player rooted in the traditions of the Punjab gharana. He began his intensive musical training at the exceptionally young age of five, receiving tutelage from two of the most respected figures in Tabla performance: the late Alla Rakha Khan and his son, the renowned Zakir Hussain. Despite his dedication to music, Kalyanpur also pursued formal education, graduating with a commerce degree from Mithibai College.

Kalyanpur first gained public recognition at the age of eleven with a notable performance alongside his guru, Zakir Hussain, in the commercial for “Wah Taj!”. This early exposure marked the beginning of a distinguished career characterized by a distinctive playing style. His technique is described as possessing a bold and clear articulation of rhythmic syllables, combined with remarkable precision and a vast collection of compositions. He is also known for his improvisational skills.

Throughout his career, Kalyanpur has collaborated with a truly impressive array of prominent musicians across various genres. He has frequently accompanied masters of Hindustani classical music, including Shivkumar Sharma, Amjad Ali Khan, Prabha Atre, N. Rajam, Sultan Khan, Shahid Parvez, Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, Satish Vyas, Shujaat Khan, and Nayan Ghosh. Demonstrating his versatility, he has also performed with leading figures in Carnatic music such as T. N. Krishnan, N. Ramani, U. Shrinivas, and Lalgudi Krishnan. 

His reach extends beyond the realm of classical Indian music. Kalyanpur joined A.R. Rahman on the “JAI HO World Tour!” and has contributed to popular Western music, appearing on Katy Perry’s song “Legendary Lovers” from her album *Prism*. He has also recorded with Keith Richards, the guitarist from The Rolling Stones, showcasing his ability to seamlessly integrate into diverse musical settings.

Kalyanpur’s accomplishments have been recognized with numerous awards and accolades. He is a “TOP” Grade Artist of All India Radio, and has received the ‘Taal – Mani’ award from the Sur Singar Samiti. He is also a recipient of the Vidyasagar Award from ITC, and holds the title of Sangeet Visharad. He was granted a National Scholarship for Advanced Training by the Government of India, and was an awardee of the Pandit Jasraj Competition hosted by the Vedic Heritage Center in Long Island, New York. 

His performances have taken him to international stages, including appearances at the Orient Arts Festival in Estonia, the Edinburgh Festival in Scotland (2003), the Earagal Arts Festival in Ireland, Jazz Yatra in Mumbai, the Great Lakes Folk Festival in Lansing, Michigan, and the Saptak Festival.

title: Jashubhai Dhanabhai Barad
text:
Jashubhai Dhanabhai Barad was an Indian politician from the state of Gujarat who served prominently in both state and national politics until his death in 2016. Born on September 15, 1955, Barad represented the Junagadh constituency in the 14th Lok Sabha, the lower house of India’s Parliament, and held a ministerial position within the Gujarat state government. He was widely known and respected, earning the nicknames “lion of Saurashtra” and “lion of Sorath.”

Barad’s political career spanned several decades and included multiple terms as a Member of the Legislative Assembly. He first entered the Gujarat Legislative Assembly in 1990, winning election from the Somnath constituency. He was re-elected from Somnath in 1995, and during this period, he served as a Cabinet Minister responsible for Water Resources and Irrigation. His work as minister involved significant contributions to the development of major water projects within Gujarat, specifically the Narmada and Ukai Dam Projects. 

He later shifted his focus to the Talala Gir constituency, successfully contesting and winning elections there in both 1998 and 2012.  He was actively serving his fourth term as a Member of the Legislative Assembly representing Talala Gir at the time of his passing. In 2004, Barad expanded his political reach to the national level, being elected to the Lok Sabha – the Parliament of India – representing Junagadh. 

Jashubhai Barad’s life was cut short on January 25, 2016, when he died in Ahmedabad due to a brain tumour. His death prompted a by-election in the Talala Gir constituency, which was won by his brother, Bhagvanjibhai Barad. Bhagvanjibhai secured his victory with a substantial margin of 31,000 votes over his opponent, Govindbhai Parmar of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). 

Barad came from the Yadav, also known as Ahir, community and his family originated from Badalpara village, located near Veraval. Throughout his career, he established himself as a significant figure in Gujarat’s political landscape, leaving a legacy through his involvement in crucial infrastructure projects and his continued representation of his constituents.

title: Cierre Wood
text:
Cierre Wood, born February 21, 1991, is a former American football player who ultimately received a life sentence for murder. He built a promising athletic career beginning in high school at Santa Clara High School in Oxnard, California, where as a senior he rushed for 1,632 yards and 20 touchdowns, and was named a USA Today All-American in 2008. He was highly recruited, eventually choosing to play college football at Notre Dame over several other prominent universities. 

At Notre Dame, Wood redshirted his first year in 2009. He became a significant part of the team in 2010, starting the last six games after an injury to the primary running back, gaining 603 rushing yards and three touchdowns. He continued to improve, becoming the starting running back in his junior year and recording 1,102 rushing yards with nine touchdowns. His senior year was marked by a two-game suspension for violating team rules, but he still managed 742 rushing yards in the remaining eleven games. 

Wood decided to enter the 2013 NFL draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility. He went undrafted but was signed by the Houston Texans as a free agent. His time with the Texans was brief, as he was released in October 2013 due to unspecified team rule violations. He subsequently had short stints with the New England Patriots, Baltimore Ravens, Seattle Seahawks, and Buffalo Bills, spending time on practice squads and briefly being promoted to active rosters. He even played Canadian football with the Hamilton Tiger-Cats and Montreal Alouettes before being released in 2018.

However, Wood’s life took a tragic turn. In April 2019, he and his girlfriend, Amy Taylor, were arrested in connection with the death of Taylor’s five-year-old daughter, La’Rayah Davis. The child was found with extensive injuries. Wood was accused of subjecting the child to harsh physical punishments, including forced, extreme exercise. In August 2024, Wood was sentenced to life in prison, with the possibility of parole after over twelve years, after entering an Alford plea to charges of second-degree murder and child abuse.

title: Diana Ivanova
text:
Diana Ivanova is a Bulgarian journalist, author, and documentary filmmaker whose work centers on intercultural dialogue, particularly between Bulgaria and Germany, and the exploration of individual and collective traumas stemming from political circumstances. Born in Montana, Bulgaria (formerly Mihajlovgrad), she received her education at the University of Sofia, earning a Master’s degree in Journalism in 1991. She subsequently worked as a journalist for Bulgarian National Television and later as a radio journalist at Radio Free Europe in Prague until 2003, also completing training as a cultural manager in Salzburg that same year. She further qualified as a group analyst in 2014.

Ivanova’s professional life is split between Bonn and Sofia. Her journalism, described as “slow journalism,” prioritizes authenticity and in-depth exploration of her subjects. She contributes to various publications including *n-ost*, *Dnevnik*, *Capital* (Bulgaria), *Abitare*, and *Foreign Policy*. Beyond journalism, she manages the New Culture Foundation and has undertaken research into the archives of the Bulgarian secret services.  Her dissertation examines the experiences of elderly Italian caregivers employed by Bulgarian women who have migrated for work, and the resulting disruption of their ties to their homeland.

A significant part of Ivanova’s work involves addressing trauma, drawing on the theories of Angela Kühner and Kai Erikson. She uses cultural exchange and encounter groups as tools to confront these traumas and foster a path towards healing.  This approach is evident in several of her projects, including “I lived Socialism,” a collaborative effort with a poet and psychiatrist to document the lasting impact of socialism on Bulgarian lives, resulting in a collection of 171 stories. 

Perhaps her most prominent ongoing project is “Goatmilk,” an annual international cultural festival held in the village of Gorna Bela Rechka in northwestern Bulgaria. This festival brings together local residents and artists from various nations, creating a space for shared stories, memories, and understanding.  A notable achievement of the festival was the successful fundraising and replacement of a stolen village bell, supported by the Goethe-Institut.

Ivanova has also created several film projects, scripting *The Town of Badante Women* and contributing to *Father*. Her directorial debut, the 2014 documentary *Listen*, focuses on the history and impact of Radio Free Europe, where she previously worked, and has been screened internationally, earning her the Best Director award as best first film.  She is currently researching the film archive of the Bulgarian State Security with a grant from the Federal Foundation for the Reappraisal of the SED Dictatorship. 

Alongside these projects, Ivanova leads self-awareness groups in Bonn and Sofia, utilizing group analysis to provide a space for individuals to address trauma related to political circumstances. She is a published author, with several books to her name, including *How to make a bell*, *My Street: Cuban Stories*, and *Trauma und Wunder*, a collection of portraits and stories from a particularly economically challenged region of Bulgaria.  Throughout her career, she has received several awards, including the Writing for Central and Eastern Europe prize and the Hostwriter Prize for Collaboration in Journalism.

title: Kerwin Bell
text:
Kerwin Bell is an American football coach and former player, currently the head coach of Western Carolina University’s football team, a position he’s held since 2021. Born in Live Oak, Florida in 1965, Bell enjoyed a 14-year professional career spanning the Canadian Football League (CFL), World League of American Football (WLAF), and the National Football League (NFL) before transitioning to coaching. He grew up on a tobacco farm in Mayo, Florida and excelled in multiple sports at Lafayette County High School, leading the football team to their only state championship.

Despite his high school success, Bell was lightly recruited and walked on at the University of Florida in 1983. He quickly rose to prominence, becoming the starting quarterback in 1984 after injuries to other players. In his first collegiate start against defending national champion Miami, he demonstrated poise, throwing a late touchdown pass despite ultimately losing a close game. He led the Gators to a 9-1-1 record that season, earning SEC Player of the Year honors, although the team was later penalized for NCAA violations. Bell continued to excel at Florida for three more seasons, solidifying his place as a standout quarterback and graduating in 1987.

Bell’s professional career was marked by success in the CFL and WLAF, though he never became a consistent starter in the NFL. He played for several teams, including the Miami Dolphins, Atlanta Falcons, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Orlando Thunder, Sacramento Gold Miners, Edmonton Eskimos, Indianapolis Colts, Toronto Argonauts, and Winnipeg Blue Bombers. Remarkably, he holds the highest career passer rating in NFL history, completing all five of his attempted passes for 75 yards and a touchdown during a brief stint with the Colts, albeit in a very limited sample.

Following his playing career, Bell moved into coaching, starting at the high school level with Trinity Catholic High School in Ocala, Florida, where he led the team to their first state championship in 2005. He then transitioned to collegiate coaching, becoming the head coach at Jacksonville University in 2007. During nine seasons there, he led the Dolphins to three conference championships. He continued his success at Valdosta State University, leading the Blazers to an undefeated season and the NCAA Division II national championship in 2018 with a high-powered offense. A brief stint as offensive coordinator at the University of South Florida under Charlie Strong ended with both being dismissed after one season. 

In 2021, Bell accepted the head coaching position at Western Carolina, where he has begun to turn around a struggling program, leading them to their first winning season in six years in 2022. He is known for his offensive philosophies, which were heavily influenced by his time working under Steve Spurrier at the University of Florida.

title: André Le Nôtre
text:
André Le Nôtre was a prominent French landscape architect, born in Paris on March 12, 1613, and passing away on September 15, 1700. He is best known as the principal gardener of King Louis XIV, and is considered the defining figure of the French formal garden style, known as the *jardin à la française*. His family had a long history of involvement with the royal gardens; his grandfather, Pierre Le Nôtre, and father, Jean Le Nôtre, both held positions at the Tuileries Garden. 

Growing up within the Tuileries, André received both practical and theoretical training in gardening. He also benefitted from a broader education, studying mathematics, painting, and architecture, even working in the atelier of painter Simon Vouet and later under architect François Mansart. This diverse background proved crucial to his approach to garden design, which emphasized classical art, perspective, and artistic integration.

Le Nôtre’s career began with a position as principal gardener for Gaston, Duke of Orléans in 1635, followed by inheriting his father’s role at the Tuileries in 1637. He subsequently worked for Anne of Austria and modernized the gardens at Fontainebleau from 1645 to 1646. Eventually he became Controller-General of the Royal Buildings in 1657, overseeing all royal gardens in France. Though he rarely documented his ideas in writing, he expressed his vision directly through his garden designs and became a trusted advisor to Louis XIV, ultimately being ennobled by the king in 1675.

One of Le Nôtre’s earliest major projects was at Vaux-le-Vicomte, undertaken in collaboration with Louis Le Vau and Charles Le Brun. This garden showcased grand symmetry, parterres, and pools, making innovative use of the landscape’s levels and forced perspective.  This success led to his most famous commission: the gardens of the Palace of Versailles.  He transformed the existing hunting lodge into a magnificent palace and surrounding park, including the expansive Avenue de Paris, influencing later city planning like Pierre Charles L'Enfant’s plan for Washington, D.C. 

Beyond Versailles, Le Nôtre designed gardens for numerous other French estates, including Fontainebleau, Saint-Cloud, Saint-Germain-en-Laye, and Chantilly. He also extended the axis of the Tuileries Garden, creating the Champs-Élysées. His work wasn’t limited to France, with designs for Bicton Park in England, Greenwich Park in London, and projects in Italy like the Castle of Racconigi and the Palace of Venaria. He continued working until late in his life, contributing to the gardens of Château de Meudon and the Hôtel de Saint-Aignan.

title: Carmelo Anthony
text:
Carmelo Anthony, born May 29, 1984, enjoyed a 19-season career in the NBA, becoming a ten-time All-Star and six-time All-NBA Team member. He is widely considered one of the greatest scorers in NBA history and will be inducted twice into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2025, both as an individual and as part of the 2008 U.S. Olympic team. His basketball journey began at Syracuse University, where he led the Orange to a national championship as a freshman in 2003, earning the NCAA Tournament’s Most Outstanding Player award.

Anthony was drafted third overall by the Denver Nuggets in 2003 and quickly became a cornerstone of the franchise. He led the Nuggets to the playoffs for six consecutive years, from 2004 to 2010, securing two division titles and reaching the Western Conference Finals in 2009 – their first appearance since 1985. In 2011, he was traded to the New York Knicks, where he famously scored a career-high 62 points against the Charlotte Bobcats in 2014, setting both a Knicks single-game record and a Madison Square Garden record. 

Following his time in New York, Anthony had stints with the Oklahoma City Thunder and Houston Rockets before joining the Portland Trail Blazers for two seasons and ultimately finishing his career with the Los Angeles Lakers. Throughout his NBA career, Anthony also excelled on the international stage, representing the United States in a record four Olympic Games. He won a bronze medal in 2004 and gold medals in 2008, 2012, and 2016, becoming the U.S. Olympic team's all-time leading scorer, rebounder, and games played as of 2016. He currently ranks tenth in NBA career scoring.

Born in Brooklyn, New York City, Anthony experienced a challenging early life, losing his father to cancer at the age of two. He later moved to Baltimore at age eight and attended Towson Catholic High School, where he experienced a significant growth spurt and emerged as a highly-rated basketball prospect.  He was named The Baltimore Sun's metro player of the year in 2001. After a period of academic challenges, he transferred to Oak Hill Academy in Virginia for his senior year.  He demonstrated his potential by averaging 21.7 points, 8.1 rebounds, and 4.0 assists, earning numerous All-American honors.

Anthony’s decision to attend Syracuse University, rather than enter the NBA directly after high school, was a deliberate choice. He thrived during his single season with the Orangemen, averaging 22.2 points and 10.0 rebounds, and leading them to an NCAA championship.  His exceptional performance in the tournament, including a 33-point outburst in the Final Four, solidified his reputation as a future NBA star.  He declared for the draft after his freshman year, with the blessing of his coach, feeling he had accomplished his goals in college.

title: Asafa Powell
text:
Asafa Powell, born in 1982 in Jamaica, is a retired sprinter renowned for his dominance in the 100 metres. He twice held the world record for the event, first with a time of 9.77 seconds in 2005, then 9.74 seconds in 2007. His personal best of 9.72 seconds ranks fourth all-time, and as of 2016, he had broken the 10-second barrier a record 97 times. Beyond the 100m, Powell also holds the world record for the 100-yard dash with a time of 9.09 seconds, set in 2010. He achieved Olympic gold in the 4x100m relay in 2016.

Powell’s Olympic journey included participation in the 100m at the 2004, 2008 and 2012 games, achieving fifth place finishes in the first two. He suffered a groin injury during the 2012 race, finishing eighth. He secured a bronze medal in the 100m and a silver in the 4x100m relay at the 2007 World Championships. He also experienced success at the Commonwealth Games, winning two golds and a silver medal. In 2009, he earned a bronze in the 100m at the World Championships, followed by a gold in the relay. Throughout his career, Powell won the IAAF World Athletics Final five times and was, for a period, the official 100m world record holder.

A challenging period arose in 2013 when Powell tested positive for the stimulant oxilofrine, alongside teammate Sherone Simpson. Both athletes maintained their innocence, claiming they unknowingly consumed a contaminated supplement. Initially facing an 18-month suspension, their bans were ultimately lifted in 2014 by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which determined the positive tests were due to the undisclosed presence of oxilofrine in the supplement.

Born into a family of runners – his father clocked 10.2s, his mother 11.4s, and his brothers 9.5s for 100 yards – Powell initially aspired to be a mechanic. He began training seriously while studying in Kingston, and in 2001 joined the MVP Track & Field Club, coached by Stephen Francis. Francis utilized an unusual training method, incorporating a 10% sloped stretch of road to improve starts. 

Powell’s early career saw limited success at the ISSA High School Championships, but he quickly improved under Francis’ guidance. He quickly climbed the ranks, achieving a personal best of 10.26s at the 2002 Commonwealth Games and winning the Jamaican 100m National Championship in 2003. He experienced a controversial moment at the 2003 World Championships, being disqualified for a false start alongside Jon Drummond. His breakthrough came in 2004 with his first sub-10 second run (9.99s) and a fifth-place finish at the Athens Olympics. He continued to break records in 2005, culminating in a new world record of 9.77 seconds, beating the previous mark held by Tim Montgomery. He continued his success into 2006 and 2007, winning multiple Grand Prix events and achieving a second world record of 9.74 seconds in 2007. Despite consistent success, injuries plagued his 2008 and 2009 seasons, including groin and pectoral muscle injuries, ultimately impacting his individual performances at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

title: Jacques Cousteau
text:
Jacques-Yves Cousteau, born in France in 1910 and passing away in 1997, was a multifaceted figure renowned as a naval officer, oceanographer, filmmaker, and author. He is best known for co-inventing the Aqua-Lung, the first successful open-circuit self-contained underwater breathing apparatus, which revolutionized underwater exploration and enabled him to create groundbreaking underwater documentaries. Cousteau’s passion for the ocean developed after an automobile accident curtailed his ambitions of becoming a naval pilot.

Throughout his career, Cousteau dedicated himself to exploring and documenting the underwater world. His first book, *The Silent World*, published in 1953, detailed his undersea discoveries and notably surmised the existence of echolocation in porpoises. This book was later adapted into a critically acclaimed documentary film of the same name, co-directed with Louis Malle. *The Silent World* film won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival in 1956, a distinction it held as the only documentary to do so for nearly fifty years, and also received the Academy Award for Best Documentary in 1957. 

Cousteau further shared his explorations through television, hosting *The Undersea World of Jacques Cousteau* from 1966 to 1976, and *The Cousteau Odyssey* from 1977 to 1982. These series brought the mysteries of the ocean into homes worldwide. Early underwater experiments took place in Toulon, aided by a friend lending him early swimming goggles. Later, during World War II, Cousteau and Marcel Ichac collaborated on underwater films, including *Par dix-huit mètres de fond* and *Épaves*, utilizing early Aqua-Lung prototypes developed with Émile Gagnan. During this period, he also aided the French Navy, and was involved in a commando operation against Italian espionage services.

After the war, Cousteau established the GERS (Underwater Studies and Research Group) of the French Navy. He continued to refine the Aqua-Lung, making extended underwater exploration possible. He embarked on numerous expeditions, including archaeological work in the Mediterranean, with the *Élie Monnier*, and later, with the research vessel *Calypso*, which he leased for a symbolic one franc a year. These voyages led to discoveries such as the wrecks of the HMHS *Britannic* and the French ship *La Therese*. 

Cousteau’s commitment to ocean conservation led to the creation of the Cousteau Society for the Protection of Ocean Life in 1973. Throughout his life, he received numerous accolades, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom and election to the Académie française. He was involved in projects like the Conshelf underwater habitats, aiming to allow humans to live and work on the seafloor. His later years were marked by personal tragedy with the loss of his son, Philippe, in a plane crash in 1979, and his wife Simone to cancer in 1990, after which he remarried.  Jacques-Yves Cousteau ultimately left a lasting legacy as a pioneering explorer and advocate for marine conservation.

title: Levi Roots
text:
Levi Roots, born Keith Valentine Graham in Jamaica in 1958, is a businessman and chef who achieved widespread recognition after appearing on the British television show *Dragons’ Den*. He is now estimated to be worth £30 million, according to the Sunday Times Rich List. Roots spent his early years being raised by his grandmother in Jamaica before joining his parents in the United Kingdom at the age of eleven. He was initially raised Christian, but later converted to the Rastafari faith at eighteen.

Before his culinary success, Roots had a career in music, performing with artists like James Brown and Maxi Priest. He received a MOBO nomination for Best Reggae Act in 1998 and famously performed “Happy Birthday Mr. President” for Nelson Mandela in 1996. His breakthrough moment came with his Reggae Reggae Sauce, a jerk barbecue sauce which he initially sold at the Notting Hill Carnival in 2006.

Roots secured investment for his sauce on *Dragons’ Den* in 2007, receiving £50,000 from Peter Jones and Richard Farleigh for a 40% stake in the business, although he initially overstated the size of an existing order. This led to a deal with Sainsbury’s, who began stocking the sauce in 600 stores. While he initially claimed the recipe was a family heirloom passed down from his grandmother, he later admitted it was a marketing tactic and that he invented it himself.

He ventured into the restaurant business, opening the Papine Jerk Centre in London in 2010, which was staffed with his children and catered to a local school. A franchise restaurant followed in Westfield Stratford City in 2015 but closed in 2019. Roots has also authored cookbooks, including *Levi Roots' Reggae Reggae Cookbook* (2008) and *Caribbean Food Made Easy* (2009), the latter of which accompanied a BBC2 television series of the same name. He has made numerous television appearances, including *Ready Steady Cook*, *Celebrity Mastermind*, *Big Brother*, and *Death in Paradise*. Most recently, he participated in *Celebrity Big Brother* in 2024, being evicted after eleven days.

Roots’ personal life has included challenges. He has eight children with seven different mothers and served time in prison twice, once as a teenager for assault and later for drug offences. He has since become involved in supporting rehabilitation, acting as Patron of RIFT Social Enterprise which assists people with convictions into self-employment. He also holds honorary doctorates from the University of the West of England and the University of Westminster, and served as Chair of St Pauls Carnival in Bristol from 2021.

title: Jorge Enríquez
text:
Jorge Enríquez García, born on January 8, 1991, is a former Mexican professional footballer who played as a defensive midfielder. He is best known for being an Olympic gold medalist, a feat he achieved representing Mexico. His professional career began with C.D. Guadalajara, where he debuted on February 5, 2010, in a match against Pachuca CF, entering the game as a substitute for Adolfo Bautista during the Bicentenario tournament. He later scored his first professional goal in a quarter-final match against Monarcas Morelia, striking from outside the penalty area.

In December 2015, Enríquez was loaned from Guadalajara to Club León for a period of six months. Later in his career, in June 2018, he was transferred to the Cypriot club Omonia. 

Enríquez’s international career began with appearances for the Mexico national team at the 2011 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, where Mexico ultimately emerged victorious, securing qualification for the 2011 Pan American Games. He also participated in the 2011 Copa América with the U-22 Mexico squad, although they were eliminated in the group stage, finishing last in their group. 

He was a key player in the 2011 FIFA U-20 World Cup, where Mexico reached the semi-finals before being defeated by Brazil. They recovered to win the third-place match against France, and Enríquez was recognized for his performance, receiving the Bronze Ball award as the third-best player in the tournament. 

He further contributed to Mexico's success at the Pan American Games, winning a gold medal as a member of the team that defeated Argentina in the final. His most significant achievement came at the 2012 Summer Olympics, where he played a vital role in Mexico's journey to the gold medal, providing crucial passes and scoring the opening goal against Senegal in the quarter-finals. 

Throughout his career, Enríquez earned several accolades. With Guadalajara, he won the Copa MX Apertura in 2015. Representing Mexico’s youth teams, he won the 2011 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, the 2011 Pan American Games, the 2012 CONCACAF Olympic Qualifying Championship, and the Toulon Tournament in 2012, culminating in the Olympic gold medal later that year. His individual achievements include the FIFA U-20 World Cup Bronze Ball award in 2011. As of July 25, 2013, his international career statistics were recorded.

title: Earl Garrison
text:
Earl Garrison was an Oklahoma state senator who represented District 9 from 2004 until 2016. This district encompassed Muskogee and Wagoner counties within the state. His entrance into the Senate came about as a result of term limits preventing his predecessor, Ben Robinson, often known as “Bulldog” Ben Robinson, from running for reelection. Garrison effectively filled the position left vacant by Robinson’s departure.

During his twelve years in the Oklahoma Senate, Garrison held several leadership positions within the minority party. From 2011 to 2014, he served as Minority Whip, a role focused on party discipline and communication. He also functioned as Assistant Minority Leader, indicating a further level of responsibility in guiding the legislative agenda of his party. 

Beyond his political career, Garrison had a background in both education and agriculture. The article notes he worked as an educator, suggesting a commitment to the field of learning and potentially teaching. He also worked as a rancher, indicating involvement in agricultural practices and land management. Prior to these pursuits, Garrison served in the United States Air Force, demonstrating a period of service to the country.

Information regarding Garrison’s family is briefly provided, centering around his daughter, Jessica Jean Garrison. In November 2021, Jessica Jean Garrison announced her candidacy for a United States Senate seat, initially challenging incumbent James Lankford. She later shifted her focus and instead filed to run for the open seat created by the retirement of Senator Jim Inhofe. This indicates a continuation of the family’s interest in public service and political engagement at the federal level. 

The article also provides links to external resources detailing further information about Garrison’s career. These include an archived version of his official State Senate website, a profile on Project Vote Smart, and records of his campaign contributions from the years 2004, 2006, and 2008 through the "Follow the Money" resource. These links offer avenues for further research into his legislative activities and financial backing during his time in office.

title: Santiago Vergini
text:
Santiago Vergini, born in 1988, is an Argentine professional footballer who plays as a centre-back. He began his career in the youth system of Vélez Sársfield, but didn’t make a senior appearance for them before moving to Club Olimpia in Paraguay in 2009. He quickly established himself there, making 12 appearances and scoring one goal in his first professional season.

In 2010, Vergini was loaned to Italian side Verona, where he played 15 matches and scored once. He returned to Argentina in 2011, signing for Newell's Old Boys and becoming a regular starter. Over two seasons with Newell’s, he played 32 matches, netting three goals, and was a key player in their run to the semi-finals of the 2013 Copa Libertadores.

A move to Estudiantes followed in 2013, where he featured in 17 games and scored a single goal. In January 2014, he joined Sunderland in the English Premier League on loan, making his debut as a substitute after a red card to a teammate. He eventually secured a starting position, initially at centre-back, then later at right back due to injuries within the squad, and helped Sunderland avoid relegation. This led to a season-long loan extension in 2014, which then became a two-year permanent contract following another successful relegation battle. During his time at Sunderland, he unfortunately scored a memorable own goal against Southampton, described as spectacular but contributing to an 8-0 defeat.

Following a loan spell with Spanish La Liga side Getafe in 2015, Vergini returned to Argentina, joining Boca Juniors in 2016. He later moved to Turkey, signing a two-year deal with Bursaspor in 2018. He then returned to Argentina again in 2019, signing a three-year contract with San Lorenzo.

Internationally, Vergini earned three caps for the Argentinian national team between 2012 and 2014, including appearances in a Superclásico de las Américas against Brazil and friendlies against Hong Kong and Croatia. He was part of the Sunderland team that lost the 2014 Football League Cup Final. With Newell’s Old Boys, he was a runner-up in both the Torneo Final and Torneo Inicial of the Primera División in 2013.

title: Huang Xing
text:
Huang Xing was a pivotal figure in the founding of the Republic of China, second in prominence only to Sun Yat-sen, and together they were known as Sun-Huang during the Xinhai Revolution. Born Huang Zhen in 1874 in what is now Changsha, Hunan, he adopted several names throughout his life, including Huang Keqiang and Li Youqing. A descendant of the Song dynasty artist Huang Tingjian, he distinguished himself academically, earning a Jinshi degree at age 22 and graduating from Wuchang Lianghu College before being selected to study in Japan in 1902.

His time in Japan proved formative, fostering a dedication to military affairs and providing training in modern warfare. It was also there that he began his revolutionary activities, organizing the Anti-Russia Volunteer Army in 1903 to protest Russian influence in Outer Mongolia and Manchuria. This led to the founding of the Huaxinghui, a secret society dedicated to overthrowing the Qing Dynasty, with Huang Xing as its elected president. He later collaborated with Sun Yat-sen, becoming a key leader in the Tongmenghui, another revolutionary organization, serving as General Affairs Officer.

Huang actively participated in a series of uprisings against the Qing, including those in Qinzhou, Fangcheng, Zhen Nanguan, and Guangzhou. While these early attempts, notably the Huanghuagang Uprising in 1911 where he lost two fingers to a gunshot wound, were unsuccessful, they laid the groundwork for the Wuchang Uprising that ultimately toppled the dynasty. He then commanded revolutionary forces in the Battle of Yangxia. 

Following the establishment of the Nanjing Interim Government in 1912, Huang Xing held a leadership position and later became the director of the Kuomintang (KMT). He became a key opponent of Yuan Shikai, who sought to consolidate power and ultimately orchestrated the assassination of KMT chairman Song Jiaoren. Huang attempted to organize resistance against Yuan, establishing the South Army, but was forced to retreat to Shanghai due to a mutiny caused by a lack of funds.  He later participated in the Second Revolution and briefly controlled Jiangsu province before being forced to flee to Japan.

Huang spent time in exile, even traveling to the United States, raising funds for an army to oppose Yuan Shikai. After Yuan’s death in 1916, he returned to China but succumbed to cirrhosis in Shanghai shortly thereafter, at the age of 42. He received a state funeral and was buried on Yuelu Mountain in Changsha. He left behind five children, who went on to have prominent careers. Today, Huang Xing is commemorated through street names, parks, a museum at his birthplace, and was portrayed by Jackie Chan in the 2011 film *1911*.

title: Felix Newman
text:
Felix Newman, born in 1993, is a rower representing Great Britain. His rowing career began during his education at Abingdon School, where he achieved a high level of recognition, earning “colours” and ultimately becoming captain of the Abingdon School Boat Club. He completed his time at Abingdon in 2012 before moving on to higher education at Selwyn College, Cambridge. 

While studying at Selwyn College, Newman continued to pursue rowing and was recognized for his academic achievements, receiving a British Education Award in 2018. However, it is his accomplishments in rowing that define his profile as an athlete.

Newman’s involvement in the prestigious Boat Race began with selections for the Goldie crew, the Cambridge reserve team, in both 2014 and 2015. This demonstrated his developing skill and potential within the Cambridge rowing program. In 2016, he achieved a significant milestone by earning a seat – specifically the bow seat – in the main Cambridge boat for the Boat Race against Oxford. That year, Cambridge emerged victorious, making Newman a member of a winning crew in this historic competition.

Beyond the Boat Race, Newman has also found success at the Henley Royal Regatta, a highly regarded rowing event. He has been a part of winning crews on three separate occasions. He twice won the Princess Elizabeth Cup, a competition for women’s eights, and once secured victory in the Thames Cup, which is for men’s club crews. 

Prior to his university rowing, Newman represented Great Britain on the international stage. In 2011, he competed for Great Britain’s men’s coxed four at the World Rowing Junior Championships, held at Eton in England. This early representation signifies his talent and promise as a young rower and established a foundation for his later successes. 

Newman is also noted as an Old Abingdonian, meaning he is a former student of Abingdon School, and is listed amongst those alumni.

title: Rohit Sharma
text:
Rohit Sharma, born on April 30, 1987, is an Indian international cricketer renowned as one of the greatest opening batters of all time. He currently captains the India national team in One Day Internationals (ODIs) and has previously led the team in Test matches and Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is), retiring from the latter format after the 2024 Men's T20 World Cup victory. He represents Mumbai Indians in the Indian Premier League (IPL) and Mumbai in domestic cricket.

Sharma holds numerous batting records, including the most runs in T20 Internationals, the most sixes in international cricket, and the most double centuries in ODI cricket – a remarkable three. He also boasts the most centuries in Cricket World Cups (seven) and is tied for the most hundreds in Twenty20 Internationals (five). He holds the world record for the highest individual score in an ODI, with 264, and scored a record-breaking five centuries in a single Cricket World Cup, earning him the ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year award in 2019. Notably, he is the first captain to lead a team to the final of all ICC tournaments. 

As captain of the Mumbai Indians, Sharma led the team to five IPL titles in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, and 2020, sharing the record for most successful IPL captain with MS Dhoni. He is one of only two players to have participated in every edition of the T20 World Cup, from its inception in 2007 to 2024, and the only Indian player to win the tournament twice. He became the second Indian captain to secure a T20 World Cup title. He has been recognized with the Arjuna Award in 2015 and the Khel Ratna Award in 2020 by the Government of India. Under his leadership, India also won the 2018 and 2023 Asia Cups, and the 2018 Nidahas Trophy.

Sharma's early life was marked by modest beginnings in Nagpur, Maharashtra. Raised largely by his grandparents and uncles due to his father’s financial circumstances, he joined a cricket camp in 1999 with his uncle’s financial support. His coach, Dinesh Lad, facilitated a scholarship to Swami Vivekanand International School to improve his access to cricket facilities, recognizing his batting potential after initially identifying him as an off-spinner.

His personal life includes marriage to Ritika Sajdeh in 2015, and they have two children. He follows the Sahaj Marg meditation technique and maintains an eggetarian diet. He has numerous commercial endorsements with brands like CEAT, Hublot, Maggi, and Adidas.

Sharma’s domestic career began with List A debut for West Zone in 2005 and First-Class debut for India A in 2006. He quickly established himself with impressive scores, including a 309 not out in the Ranji Trophy in 2009, and was appointed captain of Mumbai in 2013. 

His international career began with an ODI debut against Ireland in 2007. Despite facing periods of inconsistent form, he eventually solidified his place in the team, becoming a key player in India’s victories in the 2013 Champions Trophy and subsequent World Cups. He was appointed Test captain in February 2022, succeeding Virat Kohli, but retired from Test cricket in May 2025 after a period of poor form and team performance. He was also appointed captain for the 2023 Cricket World Cup, becoming the oldest player to captain India in the tournament and surpassing Sachin Tendulkar’s record for most centuries in World Cup history.

title: Jean-Claude Van Damme
text:
Jean-Claude Van Damme, born Jean-Claude Camille François Van Varenberg in 1960 in Brussels, Belgium, rose to international fame as a martial artist and action film star. From a young age, his father enrolled him in karate, leading him to achieve a 2nd-dan black belt and success in competitions, including winning the European Professional Karate Association middleweight championship in 1979 and the Mr. Belgium bodybuilding title in 1978.
