Driven by a desire to act in Hollywood, he moved to the United States in 1982, taking on various jobs while pursuing his goal, including work as an extra, a bouncer, and a limousine driver.

His breakthrough came with the lead role in *Bloodsport* (1988), a martial arts film that became a box office hit. This launched a string of commercially successful action films throughout the late 1980s and early 1990s, including *Cyborg*, *Kickboxer* (both 1989), *Lionheart*, *Death Warrant* (both 1990), *Double Impact* (1991), and *Universal Soldier* (1992). He achieved “sex symbol” status during this period. He collaborated with several Hong Kong filmmakers—John Woo, Tsui Hark, and Ringo Lam—who made their Western cinema debuts working with him between 1993 and 1998. Films like *Hard Target* (1993) and *Street Fighter* (1994) further cemented his stardom. 

After a decline in popularity in the late 1990s and early 2000s, Van Damme experienced a career resurgence with *JCVD* (2008), a critically acclaimed film in which he played a fictionalized version of himself. He regained prominence in the action genre with a villainous role in *The Expendables 2* (2012), alongside Sylvester Stallone. He continued to appear in action films such as *Enemies Closer* (2013), *Kickboxer: Retaliation* (2018), and *Darkness of Man* (2024), alongside voice work in animated films like *Minions: The Rise of Gru* (2022). He also starred in the television series *Jean-Claude Van Johnson* (2016–2017), produced by Ridley Scott.

Throughout his career, Van Damme’s films have collectively grossed over $3.3 billion worldwide, establishing him as a highly successful action star.  Before his Hollywood success, he competed extensively in karate and kickboxing, compiling a record of 44 wins and 4 losses. He even had a short, though memorable, stint as an early version of the Predator in the 1987 film of the same name before being replaced.  He opened a gym in Brussels called California Gym in 1979 to help finance his move to America. Beyond his film career, Van Damme has been a vocal advocate for conservation and animal rights causes.

title: Karl Eliasberg
text:
Karl Eliasberg was a Soviet conductor born in Minsk in 1907 and passing away in Leningrad in 1978. He initially trained as a violinist, graduating from the Leningrad Conservatory in 1929, and began his conducting career with the Leningrad Theatre of Musical Comedy before moving to Leningrad Radio. Though he was only the second conductor of the Leningrad Philharmonic, Eliasberg became a pivotal figure during the siege of Leningrad in World War II.

He is most renowned for conducting the premiere of Dmitri Shostakovich’s Seventh Symphony, dedicated to the city during the siege, on August 9th, 1942. This performance was particularly remarkable because only fifteen musicians were available, many having perished from starvation or joined the military. Eliasberg worked tirelessly to gather musicians from various orchestras and military bands, and also ensured they received food during the desperate circumstances, effectively saving lives. The broadcast performance significantly boosted the morale of the city’s surviving population.

Despite this heroic act and being awarded the title of Meritorious Artist of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic in 1944, Eliasberg’s career in Leningrad was hampered by the return of Yevgeny Mravinsky, who effectively sidelined him. He spent much of his post-war career as a travelling, provincial conductor, only appearing in Leningrad three more times. These appearances were all connected to performances of Shostakovich’s Seventh Symphony, using the reserve orchestra. 

A particularly poignant reunion occurred in 1964, when Eliasberg conducted the first movement of the symphony with 22 of the original musicians, in the presence of Shostakovich himself, twenty-two years after their historic performance. He dedicated that concert to those who had participated in the 1942 performance but had since died. He later reflected on the experience, acknowledging both the joy and the sorrow of remembering the past.

Eliasberg’s contributions were largely forgotten after his death in 1978, and he was initially buried in an unremarkable grave. However, after the fall of Communism, his legacy was revived by Yuri Temirkanov, and his remains were moved to a more prominent location at the Volkovo Cemetery. He left behind a number of recordings including works by Brahms, Mahler, Shostakovich, Taneyev, and Bach. His 1942 performance of Shostakovich’s Seventh Symphony has been the subject of a novel and featured in both films and radio documentaries.

title: Yordanka Donkova
text:
Yordanka Lyubchova Donkova, born on September 28, 1961, is a retired Bulgarian hurdling athlete who achieved significant success throughout her career, culminating in Olympic and European championship medals, as well as a long-standing world record. She distinguished herself as a dominant force in the 100-meter hurdles, earning a total of sixteen medals from major athletics tournaments. 

Donkova’s career highlights include winning a gold medal and a bronze medal at the Olympic Games. She was particularly celebrated for her performance in 1986, a year in which she broke the 100-meter hurdles world record not once, but four times. She initially equaled the existing record with a time of 12.36 seconds in August, then improved upon it to 12.35 seconds just days later. Further improvements followed, with times of 12.29 and 12.26 seconds also achieved during that same year. 

Her most enduring record was set on August 20, 1988, when she recorded a time of 12.21 seconds. This record stood as the world’s best for almost 28 years, finally being surpassed by Kendra Harrison in 2016.  Throughout her career, Donkova also demonstrated consistent national success, achieving the title of Bulgarian National Champion in the 100-meter hurdles five times – in 1980, 1982, 1984, 1986, and 1994.

Beyond her athletic achievements, Donkova faced a personal challenge early in life, having lost two fingers on her right hand due to a childhood accident. Later in life, she became a mother to three children: a son, Zhivko Atanasov, who became a professional football player currently playing for Cherno More, and twin daughters, Daniela and Desislava, born in 1996. 

Despite receiving an offer to compete for the United States after the 1988 Seoul Olympics, Donkova chose to remain loyal to her home country and continued to represent Bulgaria throughout her career. Recognition of her achievements came in 1986 when she was named Bulgarian Sportsperson of the Year, and also received the title of BTA Best Balkan Athlete of the Year, furthering her legacy as a celebrated athlete both nationally and regionally.

title: Jeffrey Viggiano
text:
Jeffrey Viggiano, born on July 24, 1984, is a retired professional basketball player who held both American and Italian citizenship. He concluded his career playing for Umana Reyer Venezia in Italy’s Lega Basket Serie A. Viggiano began his basketball journey at Suffield High School in West Suffield, Connecticut, where he achieved significant recognition. In 2000, he was named Connecticut’s Gatorade Player of the Year, and he also contributed to his team winning the Connecticut State Championship alongside teammate Dan Presser. 

Following his high school success, Viggiano went on to play college basketball for four seasons at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, competing as a UMass Minuteman. After completing his college career, he began playing professionally in Europe, initially with the Norrköping Dolphins in Sweden and then with Soproni Sördögök KC in Hungary. 

In 2008, Viggiano was signed by Nuova Pallacanestro Pavia, a team in the Italian LegADue league. His performance with Pavia, averaging 14.1 points and 4.2 rebounds per game, earned him a move to the more prominent Armani Jeans Milano. He then spent a year on loan to Angelico Biella in August 2010.  

Viggiano continued to move between Italian teams, signing with Benetton Treviso in December 2011 and then with Enel Brindisi in July 2012, where he agreed to a one-year contract.  In August 2013, he joined Montepaschi Siena for the 2013–14 season. His commitment to Umana Reyer Venezia began in July 2014 with a deal for the 2014–15 season. Demonstrating his value to the team, he re-signed with Venezia on multiple occasions, first in July 2015 for another season, and again on July 1, 2016, continuing his tenure with the club. Information available online includes a profile on Euroleague.net and a profile on Legabasket.it, although the latter is archived from September 8, 2010.

title: Tacko Fall
text:
El Hadji Tacko Sereigne Diop Fall, born in Dakar, Senegal in 1995, is a professional basketball player currently playing for the Nanjing Monkey Kings of the Chinese Basketball Association. He previously played in the NBA for the Boston Celtics and Cleveland Cavaliers. Fall’s journey to professional basketball began in Senegal, where coach Ibrahima N'Diaye discovered his exceptional height at age 15. N’Diaye convinced Fall’s mother to allow him to attend his basketball academy, leading to a move to the United States at age 16. He initially trained in Houston, Texas with NBA Hall-of-Famer Hakeem Olajuwon and attended multiple high schools, including Jamie’s House Charter and Liberty Christian Prep, where he became the tallest high school player in the country. 

Throughout his high school career, Fall was a highly scouted recruit, averaging 20 points, 15 rebounds, and 5.1 blocks per game as a senior. He ultimately committed to the University of Central Florida, playing for the UCF Knights as a center. While at UCF, he participated in a historic matchup against fellow Senegalese center Mamadou N'Diaye, creating the tallest tip-off and face-off in U.S. college basketball. He was named American Athletic Conference Defensive Player of the Year in 2017 and declared for the NBA draft that same year, but ultimately returned for his junior and senior seasons. His college career was marked by a shoulder injury during his junior year, but he helped lead the Knights to their first NCAA tournament victory in his senior year.

Despite going undrafted in the 2019 NBA draft, Fall signed with the Boston Celtics. He quickly became a fan favorite during his two seasons with the team, known for his incredible size – 7 feet 6 inches (2.29 meters) – and impressive measurements at the 2019 NBA Draft Combine, setting records for height with shoes, wingspan, and standing reach. He signed a two-way contract, splitting time between the Celtics and their G League affiliate, the Maine Red Claws. After Boston, he played for the Cleveland Cavaliers, even earning a start in one game, and their G League team, the Cleveland Charge.

Following his time in the NBA, Fall played for the Xinjiang Flying Tigers in the Chinese Basketball Association, the Milwaukee Bucks during the 2023 NBA Summer League, and most recently signed with the Nanjing Monkey Kings in August 2023. He also briefly joined the New Zealand Breakers of the Australian National Basketball League. Known for his exceptional shot-blocking ability, Fall is a devout Muslim and chose jersey number 99 as a reference to the 99 names of Allah. Remarkably, he maintained a 4.0 GPA in high school and was a computer science major at UCF, aspiring to become an engineer. His family is also unusually tall, though none match his extreme height.

title: Timothy Evans
text:
Timothy John Evans was a Welsh lorry driver executed in 1950 for the murder of his infant daughter, Geraldine. The case became notorious as a major miscarriage of justice, as evidence later revealed his neighbour, John Christie, was a serial killer responsible for the deaths of Beryl Evans, Geraldine, and several other women. Evans, born in 1924 in Merthyr Tydfil, Wales, had a difficult childhood marked by his father’s abandonment, learning difficulties, and a chronic foot condition that disrupted his education. He worked various jobs, including painting and decorating, and coal mining, before moving to London with his mother in 1939.

In 1947, Evans married Beryl Thorley, and in 1948 they moved into a flat at 10 Rillington Place in Notting Hill, sharing the property with John and Ethel Christie. Their marriage was troubled by frequent arguments stemming from financial difficulties and Evans’s drinking. When Beryl became pregnant with their second child, she decided to have an abortion, and Evans initially agreed. Following this, Evans reported his wife’s death to police, initially claiming it was accidental during an attempted abortion facilitated by an unknown man. He later changed his story, implicating Christie as the one who offered to perform the abortion.

The subsequent police investigation was flawed. Despite finding inconsistencies in Evans's statements and overlooking crucial evidence, such as skeletal remains in the garden, he confessed to strangling both his wife and daughter, influenced by lengthy and emotionally draining interrogations and a fear of police violence. He was convicted of Geraldine’s murder in a swift trial, with Christie providing key testimony against him. 

Three years after Evans’s execution, Christie was exposed as a serial killer following the discovery of multiple bodies hidden within 10 Rillington Place. He confessed to murdering Beryl Evans while awaiting his own execution. A 1966 inquiry confirmed Christie’s responsibility for Geraldine’s death, leading to a posthumous pardon for Evans. Despite acknowledging Evans’s innocence, the High Court refused to formally quash his conviction in 2004 due to cost concerns. 

The Evans case sparked significant public outcry and contributed to reforms in the British legal system, including restrictions on capital punishment, the introduction of diminished responsibility as a defense, and the eventual abolition of hanging for murder. The case highlighted the dangers of relying on questionable confessions obtained through coercive interrogation tactics and the importance of thorough forensic investigation. Crucially, evidence later emerged – including testimony from workmen – that directly contradicted the prosecution’s case and supported Evans’s claim of Christie’s involvement, but this evidence was ignored or suppressed during the original investigation and trial.

title: Tony Bellew
text:
Anthony Bellew, born in Liverpool in 1982, was a professional boxer who competed between 2007 and 2018, later transitioning into boxing analysis and commentary. He achieved the WBC cruiserweight title in 2016, adding to his earlier regional successes including the British and Commonwealth light-heavyweight titles held from 2010 to 2014, and the European cruiserweight title from 2015 to 2016. Before turning professional, Bellew was a three-time ABA heavyweight champion as an amateur. Beyond the ring, he is known for portraying boxer Ricky Conlan in the films *Creed* and *Creed III*.

Bellew began his professional career in 2007 with a second-round TKO victory and quickly built a record of early wins. He claimed the vacant Commonwealth light-heavyweight title in 2010, defending it twice, including a hard-fought victory over Ovill McKenzie where both fighters suffered knockdowns. In 2011, a scheduled fight for the WBO light-heavyweight title against Nathan Cleverly fell through due to Bellew missing weight, but he later secured the British light-heavyweight title with another win over McKenzie.

His first encounter with Cleverly in 2011 resulted in a majority decision loss for Bellew. He continued to climb the ranks, defeating Danny McIntosh and Edison Miranda, before securing a WBC Silver title win over Roberto Bolonti in a bruising twelve-round contest. A controversial draw with Isaac Chilemba led to a rematch, which Bellew won by unanimous decision, positioning him as a mandatory challenger for the WBC light-heavyweight title. However, Adonis Stevenson defeated him by TKO in 2013, prompting Bellew to consider moving up to cruiserweight.

Bellew successfully transitioned to cruiserweight, achieving a twelfth-round knockout of Valery Brudov to win the vacant WBO International title in 2014. He then secured a highly anticipated rematch with Nathan Cleverly, this time at cruiserweight, winning by split decision. Following further victories over Ivica Bačurin and Artūrs Kuļikauskis, he challenged for and won the vacant WBC cruiserweight title in 2016, knocking out Ilunga Makabu at Goodison Park. He defended this title with a knockout win over BJ Flores in 2017.

Bellew then moved up to heavyweight for two lucrative fights against David Haye. He defeated Haye in their first encounter in 2017 by TKO after Haye suffered an ankle injury, and again in a rescheduled bout in 2018, winning by TKO in the fifth round after knocking Haye down three times. These fights were significant financial successes, generating substantial pay-per-view revenue and establishing Bellew as a major draw in British boxing.

title: Winston Churchill
text:
Winston Leonard Spencer Churchill, born in 1874 at Blenheim Palace, was a British statesman, military officer, and writer who served as Prime Minister twice – from 1940 to 1945 during World War II, and again from 1951 to 1955. He held a seat in Parliament for 62 years, representing five different constituencies, initially as a Conservative, then a Liberal, and eventually returning to the Conservatives.  His political ideology leaned towards economic liberalism and imperialism.

Churchill’s early life was shaped by his aristocratic background and mixed English-American heritage. He joined the British Army in 1895, seeing action in India, the Mahdist War, and the Second Boer War, establishing a reputation as a war correspondent and authoring books based on his experiences.  Elected as a Conservative MP in 1900, he switched allegiance to the Liberal Party in 1904, serving under H.H. Asquith as President of the Board of Trade and later Home Secretary, where he advocated for prison reform and workers’ welfare.  He held the position of First Lord of the Admiralty during World War I, but faced criticism following the disastrous Gallipoli campaign and briefly resigned, serving on the Western Front before returning to government under David Lloyd George in various roles including Minister of Munitions, Secretary of State for War, and Secretary of State for Air. He was involved in the Anglo-Irish Treaty and British policy in the Middle East. 

After a period out of Parliament, Churchill served as Chancellor of the Exchequer in Stanley Baldwin’s Conservative government, controversially returning Britain to the gold standard in 1925, which negatively impacted the economy.  During the 1930s, often referred to as his “wilderness years”, he became a prominent voice warning against the growing threat of Nazi Germany and advocating for rearmament.  He was reappointed First Lord of the Admiralty at the war's outset, and in May 1940, became Prime Minister, forming a national government that led Britain through World War II to victory in 1945.  

Following the Conservative defeat in the 1945 election, Churchill served as Leader of the Opposition. He then became a vocal critic of the Soviet Union during the Cold War, famously warning of an "iron curtain" descending across Europe and promoting European unity. He continued writing extensively, documenting his wartime experiences. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953. Though losing the 1950 election, he returned as Prime Minister in 1951, focusing on foreign affairs, strengthening Anglo-American relations, and managing the decline of the British Empire, including India’s independence.  His second term also prioritised a large-scale housebuilding program. Churchill resigned in 1955 due to declining health, remaining an MP until 1964, and received a state funeral upon his death in 1965.

Throughout his life, Churchill was a prolific writer, with writing serving as a refuge during periods of depression. He is remembered as a significant figure of the 20th century, particularly for his wartime leadership and defense of liberal democracy against fascism. While widely celebrated, he has also faced criticism for some of his views on race, and certain decisions made during the war, such as area bombing. Despite these controversies, historians generally consider Churchill to be one of Britain’s greatest Prime Ministers.

title: Alexandre Hohagen
text:
Alexandre Hohagen is a Brazilian executive with more than two decades of experience working with Fortune 500 companies throughout Latin America. His career began in 1995 with Dow Chemical Brazil, where he managed public relations, and subsequently included roles in Human Resources at Boehringer Ingelheim and ABN Amro Bank. He then spent several years at UOL, holding positions such as Human Resources Director, Vice-President of advertising and e-commerce, and Director of Electronic Commerce. Before joining Google, Hohagen served as General Manager of HBO Brazil, overseeing operations for HBO Premium Channel and Warner Channel. In 2008, he was recognized by the Brazilian newspaper *Valor Economico* as a “Top Executive” in the IT and service sectors.

A significant part of Hohagen’s career was spent with Google, beginning in 2005 as General Manager for Brazil. He quickly rose through the ranks, becoming the Managing Director of Google Latin America in 2008, a role that encompassed operations in over eight countries. During his time at Google, he addressed the issue of child pornography on the popular social network Orkut by signing a term of behavior adjustment with federal prosecutors and implementing a filter that reportedly reduced such content by over 70%. He also spearheaded the implementation of Google Public Transport for Rio de Janeiro on Google Maps in 2009 and launched the “Doodle for Google” contest in 2010, which combined a creative competition with environmental responsibility through tree planting.

In 2011, Hohagen transitioned to Facebook as its first employee and Vice President for Latin America and US Hispanics. He spent five and a half years building Facebook’s presence in these markets, opening operations in more than five countries and leading a team of 500 employees. He left the corporate world in 2015. 

Currently, Hohagen is the CEO of Nobox and an investor and partner in several companies including Ampfy, Botmaker, and MarketUP. He also holds investment positions in Hyper, Busbud, and Everypost, alongside other venture capital funds and real estate holdings in Brazil, the US, and Europe. 

Hohagen’s educational background includes a degree in communications from Faculdades Integradas Alcantara Machado, a master’s degree in people management from the University of São Paulo, and post-graduate degrees in Business Administration from both the International Institute for Management Development (IMD) in Switzerland and IIHR in the Netherlands.

title: Marcus Aurelius
text:
Marcus Aurelius, born in Rome on April 26th, 121, reigned as Roman Emperor from 161 to 180 AD, and is renowned as a Stoic philosopher. He was the last emperor of the Nerva–Antonine dynasty and the final ruler during the Pax Romana, a period of relative peace lasting nearly two centuries. His lineage connected him, through marriage, to previous emperors Trajan and Hadrian. Orphaned at a young age, Marcus was raised by his mother and grandfather, receiving an education under prominent tutors like Herodes Atticus and Marcus Cornelius Fronto, focusing on both Greek and Latin. 

His path to the throne was carefully orchestrated by Hadrian. After a series of adoptive arrangements, including Hadrian adopting Antoninus Pius, who then adopted Marcus alongside Lucius, the son of a previous heir, Marcus found himself designated as successor. Upon Antoninus Pius’s death in 161, Marcus jointly ruled with Lucius Verus. 

Marcus’s reign was marked by significant military challenges. He faced conflict in the East against a resurgent Parthian Empire and rebellions in Armenia, while simultaneously dealing with incursions from Germanic tribes like the Marcomanni, Quadi, and Sarmatians along the northern borders. These conflicts proved a considerable strain on the empire.  Internally, he oversaw a debasement of the Roman currency, reducing the silver content of the denarius. The Antonine Plague, a devastating epidemic breaking out in 165 or 166, ravaged the empire’s population, potentially claiming five to ten million lives, and may have contributed to Lucius Verus’s death in 169. While persecution of Christians seemingly increased during his rule, there’s little evidence directly implicating Marcus himself, and he even received praise from early Christian writers like Justin Martyr and Tertullian.

Despite the demands of empire, Marcus Aurelius dedicated himself to his philosophical pursuits, writing *Meditations*, a deeply personal work outlining his Stoic beliefs. This work remains a cornerstone of Stoic philosophy and continues to be widely studied today. His reign was followed by that of his son, Commodus, a succession that sparked debate among historians. 

Our understanding of Marcus Aurelius’s life and reign is primarily built upon sources like the *Historia Augusta*, though its reliability is questioned, and the writings of Cassius Dio.  Correspondence with his tutor, Fronto, as well as accounts from physicians like Galen and orators like Aelius Aristides, also provide insights. Physical remnants of his time, like the Column and Equestrian Statue of Marcus Aurelius in Rome, stand as enduring testaments to his legacy. His early life was steeped in aristocratic tradition, marked by a disciplined upbringing focused on intellectual and physical development, and shaped by the expectations placed upon a future leader of Rome.

title: Jamie Cripps
text:
Jamie Cripps, born on April 23, 1992, is an Australian rules footballer currently playing for the West Coast Eagles in the Australian Football League (AFL). He has familial ties to the sport, being a cousin to both Patrick Cripps, who plays for Carlton, and the late Chris Mainwaring, a former West Coast player.

Cripps began his football journey in Northampton, Western Australia, participating in the Auskick program before progressing to play junior football for the East Fremantle Football Club in the Western Australian Football League (WAFL). He made his senior debut for East Fremantle in 2009 and continued to develop, playing a further six games in 2010. That same year, he represented Western Australia in the 2010 AFL Under 18 Championships, showcasing his talent on a larger stage. 

He entered the AFL system through the 2010 AFL Draft, being selected with the 24th pick by St Kilda. However, shortly after being drafted, Cripps experienced a health scare and was hospitalized due to an illness related to diabetes. It was reported that St Kilda was not aware of his condition prior to drafting him.

Cripps made his AFL debut for St Kilda in Round 6 of the 2011 season, appearing as a substitute player in a match against Adelaide at AAMI Stadium. He made a strong initial impact, immediately scoring two goals with his first two kicks in the game. 

After three seasons with St Kilda, Cripps was traded to the West Coast Eagles at the end of the 2012 season. The trade involved the exchange of draft selections, with the Eagles also sending draft pick 46 to St Kilda in return for picks 41 and 44. He has remained with the West Coast Eagles since this trade, becoming a consistent member of their team.

Outside of his football career, Jamie Cripps married his long-term partner, Olivia Cripps, in October 2021. The wedding ceremony was held at a brewery located in the Margaret River wine region of Western Australia. 

Information available within the article indicates his playing statistics were current to the end of Round 20, 2019, and links are provided to external resources for those interested in further details regarding his career, including his official West Coast Eagles profile, AFL statistics from AFL Tables, and WAFL playing statistics from WAFLFootyFacts.net, as well as a profile on AustralianFootball.com.

title: Aleksandar Kolarov
text:
Aleksandar Kolarov, born in Belgrade, Serbia in 1985, was a professional footballer who primarily played as a left back. He is currently an assistant coach with Inter Milan, following a playing career spanning over fifteen years. Kolarov began his youth career at Red Star Belgrade before moving to Čukarički and then OFK Beograd. He first gained prominence in Italy with Lazio, joining the club in 2007 and winning the Coppa Italia and Supercoppa Italiana in 2009. 

In 2010, Kolarov transferred to Manchester City where he enjoyed significant success, securing two Premier League titles (2011-12, 2013-14), an FA Cup in 2010-11, and two League Cups (2013-14, 2015-16), along with the 2012 Community Shield. After seven years in Manchester, he returned to Italy, spending five seasons with Roma and Inter Milan before retiring in June 2022. At Roma, he scored on his debut and notably found the net in a Rome derby against Lazio, having previously played for them. He finished his career with Inter Milan, winning a Serie A title and Supercoppa Italiana.

Kolarov was a long-time member of the Serbian national team, earning 94 caps and representing his country at the 2008 Olympics, the 2010 and 2018 FIFA World Cups. He was named Serbian Player of the Year in 2011. He was a key player in Serbia’s qualification for the 2018 World Cup, captaining the team during the tournament and scoring their only goal in their opening match against Costa Rica. 

Known for his powerful left foot and ability to deliver accurate crosses and free kicks, Kolarov was a versatile player capable of playing as a centre back or anywhere along the left flank. Despite lacking exceptional pace, he was recognized for his attacking runs and solid defensive contributions. 

Following his retirement, Kolarov briefly served as sporting director of Italian Serie B club Pisa, but left the position after a short period. He is also involved in business, owning and investing in Bor Retail Park in Serbia. He comes from a footballing family, with his older brother, Nikola, also a former professional footballer.

title: Sun Wenguang
text:
Sun Wenguang, born on August 26, 1934, in Rongcheng City, is a Chinese activist known for his outspoken criticism of the Chinese government. His early life included service in the Navy, as his father was a naval officer in the National Government. He later transitioned to academia, becoming a professor of Physics at Shandong University in Jinan, a position he held from 1982 until his retirement in 1994.

Following his retirement, Sun became a prominent voice of dissent. He was among the initial signatories of Charter 08, a manifesto calling for political reform and greater freedoms in China, and consequently experienced harassment due to his associations with other critics of the Communist Party. This opposition to the government has repeatedly led to direct repercussions.

In April 2009, while attempting to visit the grave of former Premier Zhao Ziyang at Heroes’ Mountain cemetery in Jinan, Sun was violently attacked by a group of four or five individuals. The assault resulted in severe injuries, including three broken ribs and damage to his spine, head, back, arms, and legs, requiring hospitalization.  

Further demonstrating the government's response to his activism, Sun’s passport application was denied in 2010, shortly before the Nobel Peace Prize ceremony recognizing Liu Xiaobo. This prevented him from potentially attending events surrounding the award. 

A particularly concerning incident occurred on August 1, 2018, during an interview with Voice of America. While discussing Chinese Communist Party General Secretary Xi Jinping and government spending, Sun was interrupted when Chinese security forces raided his home and detained him. Two Voice of America journalists who attempted to contact Sun shortly after were also briefly detained for several hours. As of the reporting of this incident, Sun remained in custody.

Sun Wenguang has authored several books detailing his political views and criticisms, all published in Hong Kong. These include *Against the Wind for 33 Years: Dictatorship after 1977 versus Constitutional Democracy*, *Essays from Within and Without of Prison*, *Calling for Freedom*, *A Country in a Century of Trouble: From Mao Zedong to Jiang Zemin*, and *Essays on Chinese Central Government and CCP from Prison*.

In 2022, reports surfaced suggesting Sun Wenguang may have died in 2021 at the age of 87. However, Chinese authorities have neither confirmed nor denied these reports, leaving his current status uncertain.

title: Emcee N.I.C.E.
text:
Emcee N.I.C.E., born Aulsondro Hamilton, is a multifaceted American artist with a career spanning music, film, radio, and entrepreneurship. He first gained recognition as the lead vocalist and rapper for the duo KansasCali, contributing to six motion picture soundtracks including those for *Crash*, *Mr. & Mrs. Smith*, and *Haven*. Earlier in his career, from 1994 to 1999, he was a member of A Lighter Shade of Brown. 

Beyond performing, Emcee N.I.C.E. has significant production credits, notably co-producing the acoustic versions of 2Pac’s “Thugz Mansion” and Nas’s “Thugz Mansion (N.Y.).” He transitioned into a solo Christian hip hop career, releasing his debut album *Praise* in 2017, which reached No. 1 on both the Billboard Top Gospel Albums and Billboard Gospel Album Sales charts. *Praise* spawned five No. 1 hit records, including “I Got Angels” which charted twice, and “Glory to God” featuring Fred Hammond.

Emcee N.I.C.E.’s accomplishments have garnered awards and nominations. He won a Stellar Award for Gospel Hip Hop Radio Station of the Year for God’s House of Hip Hop Radio, a station he co-founded and which is powered by Dash Radio. He has received numerous accolades from The Gospel Spin Awards, totaling 17 nominations and 12 wins, including being honored as “Radio Man of the Year” in 2021. He was also nominated for a MTV Video Music Award in 2003 for Best Rap Video for the "Thugz Mansion" music video.

He is also a creative entrepreneur. He co-created the animated music series *Da Jammies* in 2015, voicing the character “Novelist.” He is the president of two non-profit organizations, The iTL Foundation and Urbanomics 101, and serves as the Managing Editor for *RYZE Magazine*, a Christian hip hop lifestyle publication. Furthermore, he is a published author. His book, *Music Release University*, became an Amazon Books New Release Best Seller, achieving No. 1 in the “Music Recording & Sound” category and a Top 10 spot in “Music Business.” He also authored *50 Shades of L.O.V.E.* and *Songwriting Secrets*.  Emcee N.I.C.E. is also described as an American Inventor.

title: León Dujovne
text:
León Dujovne was an Argentine writer, philosopher, essayist, and journalist who lived from November 15, 1898, to January 16, 1984. His origins lie in Eastern Europe; he was born in the village of Kurilovich, located near Mohyliv-Podilskyi in the Russian Empire, a region bordering Bessarabia, which is now part of Moldova. Dujovne’s family was Jewish, and they emigrated to Argentina when he was just one year old. 

The family chose to settle in Basavilbaso, a town within the province of Entre Ríos, Argentina. This location was significant as it was one of the Jewish agricultural colonies established by Baron Maurice de Hirsch. These colonies were created to provide opportunities for Jewish people facing persecution and limited prospects in Eastern Europe. 

Throughout his career, Dujovne produced a number of notable written works. One of his most substantial projects was a four-volume exploration of the philosopher Baruch Spinoza, titled *Spinoza. Su vida, su época, su obra, su influencia*. This work, published between 1941 and 1945 by the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters of the University of Buenos Aires, thoroughly examined Spinoza’s life, the historical context in which he lived, his philosophical work, and the lasting impact of his ideas.

Later in his life, Dujovne published *El judaísmo como cultura* in 1980, through Ediciones Nueva Presencia. This book focused on exploring Judaism as a cultural phenomenon, likely delving into its traditions, history, and societal impact.

Dujovne also contributed to the accessibility of important philosophical texts through his translations. He undertook the translation of Maimonides' *The Guide for the Perplexed*, a significant work of medieval Jewish philosophy. His translation, titled *Guía de los perplejos*, was published in three volumes in 1955. Importantly, his translation was based on the French version created by Salomon Munk. A revised edition of Dujovne’s translation, enhanced with an introduction and notes by Angelina Muñiz-Huberman, was later published in Mexico City by Conaculta in 2001, demonstrating the continued relevance and scholarly interest in his work.

title: Jeff Beukeboom
text:
Jeff Beukeboom, born in 1965, is a Canadian former professional ice hockey player and current coach. He enjoyed a successful 13-year NHL career as a defenceman, primarily with the Edmonton Oilers and New York Rangers, culminating in four Stanley Cup championships – three with Edmonton (1987, 1988, 1990) and one with the Rangers (1994).

Beukeboom was initially drafted by the Oilers in 1983 and spent his first few professional seasons honing his skills in junior hockey with the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds before joining the Oilers’ roster. Known for his hard-hitting style, he was traded to the New York Rangers in 1991, becoming a key component of their defense alongside Brian Leetch. He served as an alternate captain and was recognized for his stay-at-home defensive play, freeing Leetch to contribute offensively. During his time with the Rangers, he led the team in penalty minutes for three seasons (1992-93, 1993-94, 1995-96) and was also noted for his charitable work, receiving the Rangers’ Crumb Bum Award in 1996 for his service to local youth. He even became known for a memorable on-air incident involving ESPN’s Steve Levy.

Unfortunately, Beukeboom’s career was cut short due to concussions. A particularly severe blow from Matt Johnson of the Los Angeles Kings in 1998 led to a 12-game suspension for Johnson, but more significantly, triggered long-lasting health problems for Beukeboom. Further head trauma in 1999 forced his retirement, as he was diagnosed with post-concussion syndrome and advised against continuing to play. He finished his NHL career with 804 games played and 1,890 penalty minutes, ranking second all-time in penalty minutes for the Rangers.

Following his playing career, Beukeboom transitioned into coaching. He served as an assistant coach in the American Hockey League with the Toronto Roadrunners and later with the Connecticut Whale/Hartford Wolf Pack. He also held positions with various Ontario Hockey League teams, including the Lindsay Muskies, Barrie Colts, and Sudbury Wolves, and even coached Team Canada Red at the World Jewish Hockey Tournament. He returned to the NHL as an assistant coach for the New York Rangers in 2016. 

Beukeboom comes from a hockey family. His son, Brock, was drafted by the Tampa Bay Lightning and later played overseas, while his daughter, Tyson, excelled in rugby, earning CIS Female Athlete of the Year honors and representing Canada internationally. He is related to several other former hockey players, including Joe Nieuwendyk. He was also ranked 50th in the book *100 Ranger Greats*.

title: Karyn Pugliese
text:
Karyn Pugliese, also known by her Anishinaabemowin name Pabàmàdiz, is an accomplished investigative journalist with a significant impact on Canadian journalism and press freedom. A citizen of the Algonquins of Pikwàkanagàn First Nation and a status Indian, she notably became the first Indigenous person to be elected President of the Canadian Association of Journalists, serving from 2018 to 2020 and remaining on the board until 2024. She has intervened in over three cases before the Supreme Court of Canada.

Pugliese was raised in Ottawa, Ontario, with frequent visits to Pikwàkanagàn, though most of her family lived off-reserve. She began her career with short-term contracts at CBC Radio Ottawa and CTV, later working as a technical writer for the federal government while completing a Master's degree in history at Carleton University. Her thesis focused on the history of Ottawa-Gatineau’s urban Indigenous communities. She holds a combined honours degree in Journalism and History from Carleton University (1998) and a Master’s degree in History (2006), and was selected as the twenty-fifth Martin Wise Goodman Canadian Nieman Fellow at Harvard University, graduating in 2020.

Throughout her career, Pugliese has held several key positions. She first joined the Aboriginal Peoples Television Network (APTN) in 2000 as their first Parliamentary Correspondent, a role she held until 2006, winning three Native American Journalism Awards during her tenure. She briefly worked at Vision TV’s 360 Vision and then the Assembly of First Nations, rising to Communications Director before leaving in 2010. She then returned to journalism, hosting and producing programs for ichannel, including the innovative #FAQMP, which allowed viewers to select MPs for interview and submit questions via social media. 

Pugliese later returned to APTN in 2012 as Executive Director of News and Current Affairs, launching new programs like *Nation to Nation* and *InFocus*. Under her leadership, APTN National News secured interviews with national party leaders during the 2015 federal election. From 2021, she served as Managing Editor Investigative at the CBC, overseeing *The Fifth Estate* and *Marketplace*. She also held the position of Executive Editor at Canada’s National Observer, a climate change focused online news service.

Pugliese’s dedication to journalism and press freedom has been widely recognized. She has received two Charles Bury Awards from the Canadian Association of Journalists (2016 and 2023), the Gordon Sinclair Award from the Academy of Canadian Cinema and Television (2018), the Hyman Solomon Award for Public Policy Journalism (2019), and the Elias Boudinot Free Press Award from the Native American Journalists Association (2019), shared with Justin Brake. She also won a National Newspaper Award in 2021.  She is an ambassador for Journalist for Human Rights and has provided journalism training internationally, including in South Sudan, and is a board member of Canadian Journalists for Free Expression. She is a single mother; her son, Zackery Liberty, is a musician.

title: Ingo Titze
text:
Ingo R. Titze is a prominent voice scientist currently serving as Executive Director of the National Center for Voice and Speech and an Adjunct Professor in the Department of Otolaryngology/Head and Neck Surgery at the University of Utah. He also holds a position as a Distinguished Professor at the University of Iowa’s Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders and teaches at the Summer Vocology Institute, both at the University of Utah.

Titze’s academic background began with a Bachelor of Science in electrical engineering from the University of Utah, followed by a Master of Science in the same field with a minor in physics, also from the University of Utah. He then earned a Ph.D. in physics from Brigham Young University in 1972. His career launched with engineering roles at Argonne National Laboratory, the National Reactor Test Station, and North American Aviation before moving to Boeing in 1968-1969. He later transitioned into academic research, beginning at Gallaudet University in 1976 where he received his first National Institutes of Health grant.

Over the years, Titze has held numerous academic positions, including roles at King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals in Saudi Arabia, the University of Maryland, and the University of Iowa – beginning at Iowa in 1990 and jointly with the University of Utah starting in 2009. He also served as Director of Research and later Chief Scientist and Executive Director for the National Center for Voice and Speech, initially located at the Denver Center for the Performing Arts. He was an adjunct professor at Westminster Choir College in Princeton, New Jersey from 1989-1994.

A key contribution to the field is the development of ‘vocology,’ a discipline he conceived as parallel to audiology, born from his university courses on voice production, acoustics, and related subjects developed starting in 1979. His extensive research on voice health and disorders has been supported by multiple grants from the National Institutes of Health, resulting in over 160 research articles listed with the NIH. 

Titze’s work has garnered significant recognition, including numerous awards from organizations such as the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, the Acoustical Society of America, and the German Ear, Nose, Throat Association. He has also been featured in various media outlets, including BBC Radio 3, Reuters, and CNN, as well as documentaries produced by NDR in Germany and the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. 

He is a prolific author, having written and edited several books on the human voice, including “Fascinations with the Human Voice,” “Vocology: The Science and Practice of Voice Habilitation,” and “The Myoelastic-Aerodynamic Theory of Phonation," many of which have been translated into multiple languages.

title: Phil Vickery (rugby union)
text:
Philip John Vickery, born in 1976, is a former English rugby union player renowned as a tighthead prop. He earned 73 international caps for England and was a key member of the 2003 World Cup winning team, participating in all seven matches of the tournament. Known as “Raging Bull”, he also represented the British & Irish Lions, touring Australia and South Africa, and captained England during the 2007 Rugby World Cup.

Vickery’s upbringing was rooted in farming; he is the son of Cornish dairy farmers and remains a qualified cattle inseminator. He began playing rugby at age 12 and quickly progressed, gaining his first national representative honour at 16 with the England Schools U16s group. After leaving school, he worked on his parents’ farm before embarking on his professional career. He has two tattoos, one on each shoulder, with the left one translating to “I’ll fight you to the death”.

His club career began with Cornish clubs Bude and Redruth, before he joined Gloucester Rugby in 1995, where he earned his nickname. During his eleven years with Gloucester, he started in the 2002 Zurich Championship Final, winning the title. In 2006, he moved to London Wasps for a three-year deal, achieving success there by winning the Heineken Cup in 2007 and the Guinness Premiership title in 2008.  His career was cut short by recurring neck injuries, forcing his retirement in 2010, following a final game against his former club, Gloucester. He briefly served as Assistant Forwards (Scrum) coach at Worcester Warriors in 2012, but was released after a season.

Vickery’s international debut came in 1998 against Wales, rapidly rising through the England ranks. He endured a difficult period with England during the 1998 tour of the Southern Hemisphere, dubbed “The Tour from Hell”, but emerged as a future star alongside players like Jonny Wilkinson. He continued to represent England, overcoming injuries, and toured with the British & Irish Lions in 2001, playing in all three tests. He captained England on tour to Argentina in 2002, leading them to victory. Despite missing the 2003 Six Nations through injury, he played a vital role in England’s 2003 World Cup triumph, even captaining against Uruguay and scoring his first international try against Samoa. He later captained the side during the 2007 Six Nations Championship and the 2007 Rugby World Cup, becoming one of only four players to start in both the 2003 and 2007 World Cup Finals. He also toured South Africa with the 2009 British & Irish Lions, starting in the first and third tests.

Beyond rugby, Vickery has enjoyed success in other ventures. He was a co-commentator for ITV’s 2011 Rugby World Cup coverage and won the 2011 series of Celebrity Masterchef. In 2015, he was appointed a Deputy Lieutenant of Gloucestershire.

title: Will Keane
text:
William David Keane, born in 1993 in Stockport, is a professional footballer currently playing as a forward or attacking midfielder for Preston North End and the Republic of Ireland national team. His footballing journey began at Manchester United, where he joined the academy at age 11. Despite showing promise through the youth ranks – including being a key player in their 2010-11 FA Youth Cup winning team and receiving the Jimmy Murphy Young Player of the Year award – he only made three senior appearances for the club.

To gain experience, Keane embarked on a series of loan spells during his time with Manchester United, joining Wigan Athletic, Queens Park Rangers, Sheffield Wednesday, and a second spell with Preston North End. In 2016, he made a permanent move to Hull City, but after a loan return to Ipswich Town in 2019, he was released. He rejoined Ipswich permanently later that year, scoring six goals in 29 appearances before departing in 2020.

Keane then experienced a successful period back at Wigan Athletic, initially on a short-term contract in 2020. His scoring form – five goals in 12 appearances – earned him an extended deal, and he ultimately signed a two-year contract. He became a prolific goalscorer for Wigan, finishing as their top scorer in the 2021-22 EFL League One campaign with 26 goals, helping the team achieve promotion.

Having previously represented England at various youth levels, including winning the 2010 UEFA European Under-17 Championship, Keane declared his intention to play for the Republic of Ireland in 2019, qualifying through his father. He received his first call-up to the Irish squad in 2021 and made his debut later that year.

In July 2023, Keane moved to Preston North End, where he quickly established himself as a key player, becoming their top scorer in the 2023-24 season with 13 goals and earning a contract extension until 2026. Throughout his career, Keane has faced setbacks, including two serious knee ligament injuries, but has consistently demonstrated resilience and a knack for finding the net, earning him individual accolades such as the EFL League One Golden Boot in 2022 and a place in the PFA Team of the Year.

title: Jennifer Sevilla
text:
Jennifer Sevilla-Go, born on May 14, 1974, is a Filipino actress who has worked extensively in both film and television. Her career began very early, at the age of seven, with a commercial for Jack 'n Jill snack foods in the early 1980s. This led to her first film role in 1984’s *Kapitan Inggo*, for which she received a nomination for Best Child Actress at the Filipino Academy of Movie Arts and Sciences Awards (FAMAS).

Throughout the 1980s, Sevilla became a recognizable face through her appearances on the popular youth-oriented variety show *That's Entertainment*, alongside other young actors like Vina Morales, Keempee de Leon, and Ian Veneracion. She also appeared in numerous television commercials, including those for Colgate toothpaste and Newtex Napkins sanitary pads. She became associated with Seiko Film Productions, Inc., often appearing in films as a supporting character in loveteams featuring Sheryl Cruz and Romnick Sarmenta. Some of these films include *Puso Sa Puso* (1988), *Langit At Lupa* (1989), and *Guhit Ng Palad* (1988). 

Her filmography is extensive, spanning several decades and encompassing over 50 titles. Notable films include *Kung Ako Na Lang Sana* (2003) with Sharon Cuneta and Aga Muhlach, and *Gawad Kalinga Paraiso: Tatlong Kwento Ng Pag-asa* (2007) with Maricel Soriano.

Sevilla has been recognized for her work with multiple FAMAS and Gawad Urian nominations for Best Supporting Actress. She was nominated for *Kay Tagal Kang Hinintay* (1998), *Kahapon, May Dalawang Bata* (1999) – receiving nominations for both FAMAS and Gawad Urian for this role – and *Muling Umawit Ang Puso* (1995). Her most recent nomination was in 2000 for *Kahapon, May Dalawang Bata*.

Beyond films, Sevilla has had a prolific television career, appearing in numerous series including *Lovingly Yours*, *Young Love Sweet Love*, *Abangan ang Susunod na Kabanata*, and more recent shows like *Hawak-Kamay* (2014), *Strawberry Lane* (2014), *Love Thy Woman* (2020), *La Vida Lena* (2020) and *Ang Probinsyano* (2021). She continues to work in television as of 2023, with an appearance in *Teen Clash*.

title: Settimo Mineo
text:
Settimo Mineo, born in Palermo on November 28, 1938, is a prominent figure in the Sicilian Mafia, specifically within the Pagliarelli mandamento. Often referred to as “Tonton Settimo,” he is considered one of the oldest current bosses in the organization. While officially operating a jewelry shop in Palermo, his true influence lies within the criminal underworld. 

Mineo’s life has been marked by violence and involvement in Mafia conflicts. He survived an assassination attempt in 1982 that resulted in the death of his brother, Giuseppe, and his brother Antonino was murdered in 1981. His initial involvement with the Mafia brought him to the attention of *pentito* (informant) Tommaso Buscetta, whose testimony led to Mineo’s conviction and a five-year prison sentence during the Maxi Trial. He was again arrested in 2006 and convicted in the “Gotha” trial, but was released in 2013 following a decision by the Supreme Court of Cassation.

Throughout his career, Mineo has demonstrated a shifting allegiance within the complex power structures of the Cosa Nostra. He was formerly associated with Antonio Rotolo and the Corleonesi clan, but later forged alliances with rivals of both—Franco and Tommaso Inzerillo of the Inzerillo clan—and counted Salvatore Sorrentino as a close associate. This shift indicates a deliberate change in sides within the Mafia’s internal dynamics.

In a significant development, Mineo was elected as the new head of the Sicilian Mafia Commission in May 2018, following the death of Salvatore Riina. However, this position was short-lived, as he was re-arrested in December 2018 during the “Cupola 2.0” operation conducted by the Carabinieri, charged with leading the “Dome” of Cosa Nostra. After his most recent arrest, Giuseppe Calvaruso, previously Mineo’s most trusted lieutenant, assumed leadership of the Pagliarelli mandamento. Calvaruso is noted for his modern approach to managing the mandamento’s criminal activities, demonstrating a more entrepreneurial attitude.

Prior to his arrests, Mineo was known for his personal charisma and ability to mediate conflicts. Notably, he eschewed modern technology, refusing to use mobile phones for fear of surveillance, and frequently travelled on foot, even when meeting with other Mafia leaders. Despite his criminal lifestyle, Mineo and his wife were actively involved in their local community, regularly attending mass at the Church of San Giovanni Decollato in Ballarò, Palermo, and participating in a year-long volunteer program supporting an after-school program for children at the church.

title: Chris Woakes
text:
Chris Woakes, born in Birmingham in 1989, is a prominent English cricketer who represents England in all international formats and plays domestic cricket for Warwickshire. Initially a promising footballer, playing as a winger for Walsall F.C. until the age of 14, he transitioned to cricket, beginning with Aston Manor Cricket Club at age seven and later Walmley Cricket Club. He progressed through Warwickshire’s youth system, playing for their under-15, under-17, academy, and Second XI teams before making his first appearance for the Warwickshire First XI in 2008, where he quickly became a key bowler, taking 42 wickets that season.

Woakes debuted for England in Twenty20 Internationals in 2011 against Australia, notably scoring the winning runs, and followed this with a successful ODI debut, claiming 6 wickets. He gradually established himself in the England ODI side, and made his Test debut in 2013 during the Ashes series. He became a reliable member of the ODI team, particularly during a 2014 tour of Sri Lanka where he stepped up in the absence of senior bowlers. A standout performance during that tour was a spell of 6/47, considered among the best ODI bowling performances of the year.

Woakes experienced a career highlight in 2018, scoring his maiden Test century (137 not out) against India at Lord’s, and achieving his best match figures with the ball (11/102) against Pakistan at the same venue. This led to his name being added to the Lord’s honours board, an achievement only accomplished by ten players, and him becoming one of five to be honoured for both bowling and batting achievements at the ground. 

He was a crucial part of England’s victories in both the 2019 Cricket World Cup and the 2022 T20 World Cup, earning the Player of the Match award in the 2019 semi-final against Australia for taking three vital wickets. He also contributed significantly to the 2022 T20 World Cup win, playing in every match. He is one of only six players to have been part of both of England’s World Cup winning squads. 

Beyond his international career, Woakes has participated in the Indian Premier League (IPL), representing Kolkata Knight Riders, Royal Challengers Bangalore, and Delhi Capitals, although he opted out of the 2020 season to focus on England’s Test schedule. He also played for the Birmingham Phoenix in The Hundred in 2022. He reached significant milestones in his career, including taking his 100th Test wicket and 150th ODI wicket in 2021 and was recalled for the 2023 Ashes, where he was named England’s Player of the Series following a strong bowling performance and hitting the winning runs in the 3rd Test.

title: Diosdado Cabello
text:
Diosdado Cabello Rondón, born in 1963, is a prominent Venezuelan politician and current Minister of Interior, Justice and Peace, with a long and controversial career deeply intertwined with the country’s political landscape. He began his involvement in politics through his close relationship with Hugo Chávez, assisting in Chávez’s return to power after the 2002 coup attempt and becoming a key figure in the Movimiento V República (MVR), later the United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV). 

Cabello’s career has included roles in the military, where he holds the rank of captain, and numerous high-level political positions. He served as Governor of Miranda state from 2004 to 2008, losing the election to Henrique Capriles Radonski, after which he became Public Works & Housing Minister. He later simultaneously headed the National Commission of Telecommunications in 2009, a position traditionally independent of his ministerial role.  He was elected to the National Assembly in 2010 and became its President in 2012, holding the position until 2016, and later served as president of the 2017 National Constituent Assembly.

During a brief period in April 2002, following a coup attempt against Chávez, Cabello briefly held the office of President of Venezuela, for only a few hours, making his presidency one of the shortest in history. He also served as Vice President earlier that year. Throughout his career, he has risen to become a highly influential figure, described in 2013 as the second most powerful man in Venezuela, possessing considerable sway within the military and among lawmakers.

However, Cabello’s career has been plagued by numerous accusations. He has been repeatedly linked to the “Cartel of the Suns,” an alleged drug trafficking organization, and accused of using his power for personal enrichment through corruption, nepotism benefiting family members, and directing illicit payments to pro-government groups.  Formal corruption allegations were lodged against him in Venezuela as early as 2013. In 2020, the U.S. Department of State offered a $10 million reward for information leading to his arrest or conviction on charges of drug trafficking and narco-terrorism.

Beyond corruption allegations, Cabello hosts a weekly television program, *Con el Mazo Dando*, where he discusses political issues and often makes accusations against the opposition, raising concerns about intimidation from organizations like the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights and Amnesty International. He has also been the subject of security concerns, with reports in 2017 alleging a possible assassination plot targeting U.S. Senator Marco Rubio. 

Internationally, Cabello has been sanctioned by the United States, Canada, the European Union, Switzerland, Panama, and Argentina, with asset freezes and travel bans imposed due to his alleged human rights violations, involvement in corruption, and undermining of democratic processes. He is also banned from entering Colombia.  A recent development saw a federal court in Argentina issue an arrest warrant against him and other Venezuelan officials for crimes against humanity in September 2024.

title: Pablo Ganet
text:
Pablo Ganet Comitre, born on November 4, 1994, is a professional footballer currently playing as a midfielder for Persita Tangerang, a club in the Indonesian Super League. Though born in Málaga, Andalusia, Spain, he represents the Equatorial Guinea national team internationally.

Ganet’s football journey began within the youth system of Real Betis. He progressed through their ranks before moving to Málaga CF’s reserve team in the summer of 2013. It was with Málaga’s reserve side that he made his first appearances in senior football, competing in the Tercera División, which represents the fourth tier of Spanish football. 

In August 2014, Ganet continued his career by joining UD San Sebastián de los Reyes, remaining at the fourth level of Spanish football. Details of his time with this club are limited within the available information.

A significant turning point in Ganet’s career came with his inclusion in the Equatorial Guinea national team. He became eligible to play for the national side through his father's heritage. He was selected by coach Esteban Becker for the 23-man squad participating in the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations, announced on January 4, 2015. He officially debuted for Equatorial Guinea just three days later, on January 7, 2015, entering the game as a substitute during a friendly match against Cape Verde which ended in a 1-1 draw.

Further details about his club career between his time with San Sebastián de los Reyes and joining Persita Tangerang are not provided. However, the article does mention that he achieved a championship win with Ittihad Tanger, claiming the Botola title in the 2017-18 season. The provided career statistics are current as of January 22, 2024, though the statistics themselves are not detailed in the article. 

Ganet’s background includes descent from the Bubi people, an ethnic group indigenous to Equatorial Guinea. Online resources such as Málaga’s official website (archived), Futbolme, National-Football-Teams.com and Soccerway provide additional information about his career.

title: Sayaka Ando
text:
Sayaka Ando is a Japanese model and gravure idol who was born on May 24, 1981, in Takasaki, Gunma, but spent her formative years growing up in Sendai, Japan. She began her career in the entertainment industry with her debut in 2004, specifically through a release titled *Eternal*. 

Ando’s professional background includes a university education; she is a graduate of Miyagi Gakuin Women's University. Her work has primarily centered around the gravure industry, a popular genre in Japan featuring photographic and video releases focused on models. This is evidenced by the extensive list of DVDs she has released throughout her career.

Starting in December 2004 with *Eternal*, Ando consistently released DVDs over the following years. *Lesson 2* followed in March 2005, then *Healing Venus* in June of the same year. She continued this pattern with *Aqua* in October 2005, and a compilation release, *Ando Sayaka Collection Box* in December 2005. Releases continued in 2006 with *Fascino* in April and *Toi Kimi no Kioku* in August. 

In 2007, she released *Duet* in February, followed by *Day* and *Night* in October and December respectively. Her DVD releases concluded, as listed, with *Poison* in March 2008. Alongside her DVD work, Ando has also been involved in photobook production, having released *Mitsu no A* in April 2005, though the specific day within April is not stated. 

Outside of her professional life, the article notes information regarding her personal life. Sayaka Ando became a mother, giving birth to her first child in September 2012 and her second child in November 2014. 

Information regarding Ando can be found at the Japanese Idol Directory, and a fan website is also noted. The article also includes a link to her official website, and a reference to a broader “List of Race Queens,” suggesting a possible connection to promotional work in motorsports, though the nature of this connection isn’t detailed within the provided text.

title: Dana Awartani
text:
Dana Awartani is a Saudi visual artist born in 1987, with Palestinian heritage. She currently lives and works in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and is known for her diverse artistic practice encompassing painting, video art, and sand mosaic. A defining characteristic of her work is the integration of traditional methods found within Islamic art into a contemporary context.

Awartani’s education began with a Foundation Degree in Art and Design from the Byam Shaw School of Art in 2006. She continued her studies at Central Saint Martins in London, graduating with a bachelor’s degree in fine art in 2009. Furthering her specialization, she earned a master’s degree in traditional arts from The Prince’s School of Traditional Arts in London in 2011. Her time at The Prince’s School provided her with training in techniques like stained glass, miniature painting, and gilding, drawing from a broad range of global artistic traditions. Recognizing a gap in the curriculum regarding the illumination of texts, she sought out a private instructor in Turkey to specifically learn and master this discipline. 

Awartani’s art is distinguished by its meticulous detail and prominent use of geometric patterning, drawing heavily from the aesthetics of Islamic art. She explores the connection between geometry and the natural world, and believes geometric principles can convey deeper truths and function as a symbolic visual language. This approach stems from a tradition, developed over a millennium ago, which utilized geometry as a means of artistic expression in place of depicting divine figures. While this practice is becoming less common, Awartani continues to refine and employ these specialized techniques.

She believes that appreciation for Islamic art is often overlooked within Arab culture, despite its pervasive presence in everyday environments like mosques.  She describes finding a personal connection to these forms, recognizing the intentionality and storytelling embedded within each structured piece. Awartani views her work not merely as artistic creation, but as a spiritual practice, a form of worship and remembrance of God, requiring complete focus and a positive mindset. 

Awartani’s work has gained international recognition, including her inclusion in the Rhizoma project at the 55th Venice Biennale in 2013. Her pieces are now part of the permanent collections of prominent institutions such as the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden in Washington D.C., and the British Museum in London.

title: Yuu Watase
text:
Yuu Watase was born on March 5, 1970, in Kishiwada, Osaka, and began her career as a manga artist at the young age of 18 in 1989 with a short story titled “Pajama de Ojama.” Since then, she has created a substantial body of work, publishing over 50 volumes encompassing both one-shot stories and long-running manga series. She is particularly well-known for her popular series *Fushigi Yûgi*. 

Watase initially pursued formal art training after high school, attending a private art school focused on manga. However, she left the school mid-course, as she had already debuted her first work. She has a preference for traditional art methods, believing they allow for more emotional expression in her work, although she has experimented with digital programs like Adobe Photoshop to enhance her traditional artwork.

Throughout her career, Watase has faced challenges. She recounted an experience with an editor during the serialization of *Arata: The Legend*, where she was repeatedly asked to redraw scenes, leading to exhausting workdays and a diminishing passion for the project. The constant need for approval overshadowed her creative drive and connection to the story and its fans. 

In 2019, Watase publicly came out as X-gender, a Japanese non-binary gender identity. Viz Media, which publishes some of her work in English, clarified that her preferred pronouns remain "she" and "her" in English translations. 

Watase’s extensive catalog includes series published under various imprints. Her major works published under Flower Comics include the *Fushigi Yûgi* series (including multiple spin-offs like *Genbu Kaiden* and the ongoing *Byakko Senki*), *Ceres, Celestial Legend*, *Alice 19th*, and *Absolute Boyfriend*. She also ventured into the shōnen genre with *Arata: The Legend*, published by Shōnen Sunday Comics. Beyond her serialized works, she has numerous short stories and collections published under titles like *YuuTopia Collection* and *Yuu Watase Best Selection*.  Furthermore, many of her series have been re-released in different formats, including *bunko* editions and *kanzenban* editions, and she has also created numerous artbooks and illustrated novels related to her manga.

In 1998, Watase received the 43rd Shogakukan Manga Award in the shōjo category for *Ceres, Celestial Legend*, acknowledging her significant contributions to the manga industry.

title: Vanda Pignato
text:
Vanda Pignato, born in São Paulo, Brazil in 1961, is a lawyer, activist, and politician who served as First Lady of El Salvador from 2009 to 2014. She became First Lady through her marriage to President Mauricio Funes, and notably, was the first First Lady in El Salvador’s history to simultaneously hold a political position. She was appointed Secretary of Social Inclusion by President Funes in 2009 and continued in that role under his successor, Salvador Sánchez Cerén, beginning in 2014.

Prior to her involvement in Salvadoran politics, Pignato was an activist within Brazil’s Workers’ Party and worked as an advisor to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, later President of Brazil. She moved to El Salvador in 1992, representing the Workers’ Party and serving as Director of the Center for Brazilian Studies at the Brazilian Embassy. 

As First Lady and Secretary of Social Inclusion, Pignato focused on promoting women’s rights and gender equality. She recognized the systemic disadvantages faced by Salvadoran women, including lower literacy rates and economic dependence, which often trapped them in abusive situations. Her key initiative was the establishment of *Ciudad Mujer* (Women City) in 2011. These centers, five in total, brought together fifteen government agencies to provide comprehensive services to women, including healthcare, financial advice, job training, legal aid, and support for victims of violence. By November 2014, *Ciudad Mujer* had assisted an estimated 603,000 women.

The *Ciudad Mujer* program gained international recognition and support, receiving praise from organizations like the Inter-American Development Bank and the United Nations. Inspired by Pignato’s work, Brazil announced plans to launch a similar "Women's House" project, and Guatemala, Colombia, and Mexico also expressed interest in adopting the model. 

Beyond *Ciudad Mujer*, Pignato also led the Salvadorian Institute for Women Development and served as the first President of the Salvadorian National Council for the Youth. She played a role in responding to the severe flooding that affected El Salvador in 2011, lobbying for humanitarian aid in the United States and meeting with international leaders. She received the Ellis Island Medal of Honor in 2012 for her work with the Salvadoran American community and her dedication to women’s rights. 

Pignato and Mauricio Funes separated in 2014. In 2015, she announced a cancer diagnosis and took a leave of absence from her position. More recently, allegations surfaced in 2017 concerning illicit funding from the Brazilian construction company Odebrecht to Funes’s presidential campaign, reportedly directed through Lula da Silva. Consequently, an arrest warrant was issued for Pignato in 2018 as part of an investigation into embezzlement and money laundering, with authorities citing concerns that she might attempt to flee the country despite her health condition.

title: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
text:
Muhammad Ali Jinnah, born Mahomedali Jinnahbhai in Karachi in 1876, was a barrister and politician who became the founder of Pakistan, serving as its first governor-general until his death in 1948. He received his legal training at Lincoln's Inn in London and upon his return to India, practiced law at the Bombay High Court, gradually shifting his focus to national politics. Initially, Jinnah was a prominent figure within the Indian National Congress, advocating for Hindu-Muslim unity and playing a key role in the 1916 Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the All-India Muslim League. He proposed a fourteen-point plan for constitutional reform to protect Muslim rights. However, he resigned from the Congress in 1920 due to disagreements over their adoption of satyagraha, which he considered disruptive.

Subsequently, Jinnah dedicated himself to the All-India Muslim League, working to safeguard Muslim interests against potential marginalization in a Hindu-dominated India. He led the League in passing the Lahore Resolution in 1940, outlining the demand for a separate Muslim state. The League’s influence grew during World War II, particularly while Congress leaders were imprisoned, and they achieved significant electoral success in post-war provincial elections. Ultimately, the inability of the Congress and Muslim League to agree on a power-sharing arrangement led to the acceptance of the partition of British India into independent India and Pakistan.

As Pakistan’s first governor-general, Jinnah focused on establishing the new nation’s government and assisting the millions of Muslim migrants who relocated from India to Pakistan. He personally oversaw the establishment of refugee camps to aid this massive displacement. Jinnah died in September 1948, just over a year after Pakistan’s independence, leaving behind a lasting legacy. He is widely revered in Pakistan as “Quaid-e-Azam” (“Great Leader”) and “Baba-e-Qaum” (“Father of the Nation”), with his birthday observed as a national holiday and numerous institutions bearing his name.

Born into a wealthy merchant family, Jinnah's early life included a period of education in Bombay and Karachi. He abandoned an apprenticeship in London to study law, motivated in part by legal issues facing his family. While in England, he was influenced by British liberalism and adopted Western dress and mannerisms. He became the first Muslim barrister to practice in Bombay, quickly gaining a reputation for his legal skills and earning a substantial income. He was also involved in trade union activities, advocating for workers’ rights and contributing to the enactment of the Trade Union Act of 1926.

Jinnah’s political career began with participation in the Indian National Congress, where he initially aligned with moderate leaders promoting Hindu-Muslim cooperation. However, he often clashed with more radical factions and questioned the legitimacy of self-appointed Muslim leaders who sought separate representation. He entered the Imperial Legislative Council in 1909 as a compromise candidate and used this platform to advocate for his community's interests. Throughout his life, Jinnah was known for his self-confidence, sharp intellect, and meticulous attention to detail, earning him respect even from his adversaries.

title: Vadhir Derbez
text:
Vadhir Derbez, born Vadhir Alejandro GonzálezTorres on February 18, 1991, is a Mexican actor and singer who has been active in the entertainment industry since childhood. He is the son of renowned Mexican comic actor Eugenio Derbez. His career began in 1997 with appearances on his father’s television program, *Derbez en Cuando*, and he continued with roles in shows like *Tatiana y En Familia con Chabelo* and *Diseñador do ambos sexos* in the early 2000s. He secured his first substantial part in the soap opera *Cómplices Al Rescate* in 2002, followed by roles in *La familia P. Luche*, *De pocas, pocas pulgas*, *Par de ases*, and *Mujer, Casos de la Vida Real*. He gained further recognition for his recurring role as Marco López Pérez in the popular series *Vecinos* from 2006, appearing in 36 episodes.

Derbez’s television work extends to reality competition, notably winning the first season of Univision’s *Mira Quien Baila* in 2010. He also appeared as Maximiliano 'Max' Zaga in *Gossip Girl: Acapulco* in 2013, and played César Suárez, a character in the soap opera *La querida del Centauro* in 2016. That same year he starred in *Entre correr y vivir*, a joint production of TV Azteca and Televisa, as race pilot Rodrigo Hernández. In 2019, he won the first season of the reality show *¿Quién es la máscara?* disguised as “Camaleon.” He has also expanded into international television, appearing in the Netflix series *Sense8* in 2016.

Beyond television, Derbez has a presence in theatre and film. He debuted on stage in 2004 as Tom Sawyer in an adaptation of Mark Twain’s novel. He later participated in the musical *Grease* in 2013, playing multiple roles, and starred as Jerry in the Broadway musical *Rock of Ages* in 2014 alongside Dulce Maria. He reprised his role in *Grease* in 2017 with a tour of the United States. His film career started with voice work in the animated film *Imaginum* in 2005, but gained momentum with a role in the action film *Ladrones* in 2015. He had his first leading film role in *El tamaño si Importa* in 2016 and featured in *3 Idiotas* the following year. In 2017, he made his Hollywood debut playing a younger version of his father’s character in *How to Be a Latin Lover*, and also co-starred in the comedy *Dulce familia*.

Derbez also pursues a music career, releasing his debut EP in 2016, featuring singles like “Te Olvidé” and “Me Haces Sentir”. He has released several other singles since, including “Al Final” which was featured on the soundtrack for *3 Idiotas*, and "Latin Lover". He continued to release singles through 2022, including collaborations with various artists. He studied at Culver Academies, where he excelled in equestrianism and even participated in Barack Obama's 2008 Inaugural parade.

title: Sada Thompson
text:
Sada Carolyn Thompson was a highly respected American actress with a career spanning stage, film, and television. Born in Des Moines, Iowa, in 1927, she moved with her family to Fanwood, New Jersey, and graduated from Scotch Plains-Fanwood High School in 1945.
