She then pursued higher education, earning a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre from the Carnegie Institute of Technology, now Carnegie Mellon University. 

Thompson began her career working in regional theatre, performing in productions of plays like *The Seagull*, *Pygmalion*, *Our Town*, *Arms and the Man*, and *Blithe Spirit*. She honed her skills further with training at the Pittsburgh Playhouse, appearing in numerous of their shows. Her professional debut came Off-Broadway in 1955 with *Under Milk Wood*, followed by a television appearance in *Goodyear Television Playhouse* the next year. She made her Broadway debut in 1959 with the musical *Juno*.

Throughout her stage career, Thompson garnered significant critical acclaim, winning an Obie Award, a Tony Award for Best Actress in a Play for her performance in *Twigs* in 1972, three Drama Desk Awards, and two Sarah Siddons Awards for her work in Chicago theatre. In 2005, she was inducted into the American Theater Hall of Fame.

Her success on Broadway led to opportunities in television. She was initially cast as Irene Lorenzo on *All in the Family*, but was quickly replaced by Betty Garrett due to creative differences with producer Norman Lear regarding the character's portrayal. Thompson then found lasting recognition as Kate Lawrence in the television series *Family*, from 1976 to 1980. Her realistic and nuanced performance earned her an Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series in 1978, along with three Golden Globe nominations. In total, she was nominated for an Emmy nine times, including for her guest role as Carla's mother on *Cheers*.

Beyond these prominent roles, Thompson had a substantial television career, appearing in shows such as *Owen Marshall: Counselor at Law*, *The Love Boat*, *Father Dowling Mysteries*, *Andre's Mother*, *Indictment: The McMartin Trial*, *ER* and *Law & Order*. She also appeared in several films, including *The Pursuit of Happiness*, *Desperate Characters*, and *Pollock*.

Thompson was married to Donald E. Stewart from 1949 until her death. They resided in Southbury, Connecticut, and had one daughter, Liza Stewart, who works as a costume designer. Sada Thompson passed away on May 4, 2011, in Danbury, Connecticut, at the age of 83, due to complications from lung disease.

title: Michael L. MacDonald
text:
Michael L. MacDonald, born May 4, 1955, is a Canadian politician currently serving as a Conservative member of the Canadian Senate. He was appointed to the Senate on January 2, 2009, following a recommendation from then-Prime Minister Stephen Harper. 

Born in Louisbourg, Nova Scotia, MacDonald grew up as the youngest of ten children. He pursued higher education at the University of King's College in Halifax, graduating with an Honours degree in political science in 1977. Following his studies, MacDonald embarked on a career in politics, beginning as a researcher for the Progressive Conservative Party of Canada Research Office from 1978 to 1980. 

He continued to gain experience working within Nova Scotia’s provincial government, initially serving in the office of Member of the Legislative Assembly Gerald Sheehy between 1980 and 1982. He then progressed to the role of Executive Assistant to Premier John Buchanan from 1982 to 1984.  Further roles followed as Executive Assistant, first to Thomas McMillan from 1984 to 1985, and then to Stewart McInnes from 1985 to 1987.

Alongside his political work, MacDonald has been a business owner, running the Fortress Inn in his hometown of Louisbourg since 1988. He also sought elected office on multiple occasions, though without success.  He first ran for federal office in 1988 in the riding of Cape Breton—East Richmond, achieving second place with 7,173 votes. He then contested a provincial seat in 1993 in Dartmouth-Cole Harbour for the Progressive Conservative Association of Nova Scotia, again finishing second, this time with 2,905 votes. He ran in the same provincial riding in 1998, placing third with 2,084 votes, and later ran federally in Dartmouth—Cole Harbour in 2004, finishing third with 8,739 votes.

In February 2022, MacDonald became embroiled in controversy during the convoy protest in Ottawa. A video surfaced showing him making critical and dismissive comments about the city and its residents, specifically referencing perceived entitlement and high salaries coupled with limited work hours. He also voiced support for the protesting convoy, stating his desire for them to remain in Ottawa. He further made a personal comment about his wife, referring to her as "a Karen" due to her wanting the protest to end. Following the public reaction to the video, MacDonald delivered an apology in the Senate chamber for his remarks.

Michael MacDonald currently resides in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia, with his wife, Marilyn, and their two sons, Lauchlan and Liam.

title: Neil Googe
text:
Neil Googe is a British comic artist with a career spanning several decades and multiple publishers. He began his work in the late 1990s with contributions to titles like *Shotgun Mary* and *2000 AD*, where he worked on several *Judge Dredd* stories. A significant early project was a graphic novel adaptation of the video game *Silent Hill*, completed in 1999, but it was never published due to disagreements with Konami, despite being finished, advertised, and assigned an ISBN. Googe reportedly lost the only copy of the completed work on a CD.

In 2000, Googe co-founded the independent British comic publisher Com.x, where he created *Bazooka Jules*, though only three issues were released. He then transitioned to the American comic book market, collaborating with Gail Simone on *Welcome to Tranquility* for Wildstorm, after previously working on *Majestic*. Further American projects included *Wildcats: World's End* with Christos Gage and the *World of Warcraft* graphic novel *Dark Riders* with Mike Costa, published by DC Comics following the Wildstorm merger. 

Googe continued to contribute to DC Comics with one-shot issues such as *Rose and Thorn*, a *Detective Comics* Harley Quinn issue, a *Legends of the Dark Knight* Harley Quinn installment, and *The Flash*. He also returned to *2000 AD* to work on *Survival Geeks*. Currently, Googe is developing a creator-owned project called *Welcome to the Hood*, planned as both a pen-and-paper role-playing game and a comic series. He is also revisiting *Bazooka Jules* under the name *Bazooka Jules: Tales from Caliber Bay*, reimagining it as a world setting for role-playing games with accompanying comic short stories, and working on other tabletop and RPG products, including a Pathfinder supplement. He intends to continue working on regular comic projects alongside these new ventures.

His extensive bibliography includes work on titles like *Mercy Heights*, *Pulp Sci-fi: “Coy’s Big Score”*, and *Hondo-City Justice*. Several of his works, including *Majestic* and *Welcome to Tranquility*, have been collected into trade paperbacks.
